q: A company is designing its Google Cloud resource hierarchy. Which of the following lists the levels from top to bottom in the correct order?
options: Projects, then folders, then the organization, then resources
The organization, then projects, then folders, then resources
Folders, then the organization, then projects, then resources
The organization, then folders, then projects, then resources
explain: The hierarchy is organization at the top, then folders, then projects, then resources. IAM policies and organization policies set at a higher level are inherited downward — they never flow sideways or upward.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An IAM policy granting the Compute Viewer role is set at the folder level. A project sits inside that folder. What happens?
options: The policy applies only to the folder object itself
The policy is inherited by the project and everything inside it
The policy is blocked until it is re-applied at the project level
The policy also applies to the folder's sibling folders
explain: IAM policies inherit down the resource hierarchy, so a grant at the folder level flows to all child projects and their resources. Inheritance never moves sideways to siblings or upward to parents.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: Which identity setup is required before a company can create an organization node in Google Cloud?
options: A Cloud Identity or Google Workspace account
A billing account with an active payment method
A Shared VPC host project
A custom IAM role
explain: The organization node is tied to a Cloud Identity or Google Workspace domain, so one of those must exist first. A billing account is not required to create the organization itself.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A startup has three projects but wants a single consolidated invoice. What should they do?
options: Create a separate billing account for each project
Export each project's usage to Cloud Storage
Link all three projects to a single billing account
Move all resources into one project
explain: Many projects can link to one billing account, producing one consolidated invoice. Each project links to exactly one billing account at a time, so consolidation happens at the billing account, not by merging projects.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A team wants an email notification when forecasted spend exceeds $500 in a month. Which feature should they configure?
options: A quota increase request
A billing export to BigQuery
An organization policy constraint
A billing budget with an alert threshold and notification channel
explain: Billing budgets with alert thresholds notify you (email, Pub/Sub) when actual or forecasted spend crosses a limit. Exports enable analysis after the fact, and org policies restrict resource configuration rather than spend.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: You try to create a Cloud SQL instance with gcloud but get an error saying the API is not enabled. What is the fix?
options: Request a quota increase
Enable the Cloud SQL Admin API in the project
Create a new billing account
Grant yourself the Owner role
explain: Google Cloud APIs must be enabled per project before their services can be used. Quotas, billing, and IAM roles do not substitute for enabling the API.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A deployment fails because the project hit its limit of 24 CPUs in us-central1. What is the correct next step?
options: Request a quota increase for CPUs in that region
Create a new organization
Enable the Compute Engine API
Switch to a different billing account
explain: Quotas are adjustable guardrails, not hard ceilings — request an increase from IAM & Admin > Quotas. A new organization or billing account does not change the project's quota.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: Finance wants cloud costs broken down by team and environment across 50 projects. What is the best approach?
options: Create one project per team
Use a separate billing account per team
Apply consistent labels (for example, team and env) and group by label in billing reports
Rename every resource with a team prefix
explain: Labels are the standard cost-attribution mechanism: billing reports and the BigQuery export can break costs down by label. Separate billing accounts fragment invoicing unnecessarily, and renaming resources does not feed billing reports.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: Fifty new analysts all need the same set of IAM roles. What is the recommended way to manage this?
options: Grant the roles to each user individually
Add the users to a Google group and grant the roles to the group
Create a service account for each analyst
Grant all of them the Owner role for simplicity
explain: Granting roles to a Google group means membership changes automatically adjust access, and it follows least privilege. Individual grants do not scale, and Owner violates least privilege.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A company must ensure no VM in any project ever receives a public IP address. Which mechanism enforces this centrally?
options: A VPC firewall rule
A billing budget
Removing the Compute Admin role from developers
An organization policy constraint (compute.vmExternalIpAccess) set at the organization level
explain: Organization policies enforce constraints across the whole resource hierarchy, and compute.vmExternalIpAccess blocks external IP assignment. Firewall rules filter traffic but cannot prevent an IP from being assigned.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A company wants to analyze detailed, line-item billing data with SQL queries. What should they set up?
options: A billing export to BigQuery
A billing budget
A Cloud Logging sink
A billing export to Cloud Storage only
explain: The BigQuery billing export loads detailed usage and cost data into tables you can query with SQL. The Cloud Storage export produces flat files, and budgets only trigger alerts.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: Which statement about Google Cloud project IDs is true?
options: They can be changed at any time from the console
They must exactly match the project name
They are globally unique and cannot be changed after creation
Two projects in different organizations may share one
explain: Project IDs are globally unique and immutable once the project is created. The project name is a separate, mutable display label.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: Which gcloud command creates a new project with the ID my-new-project?
options: gcloud projects update my-new-project
gcloud projects create my-new-project
gcloud init --project=my-new-project
gcloud compute projects create my-new-project
explain: gcloud projects create provisions a new project. gcloud init is an interactive setup walkthrough, and there is no compute-scoped project creation command.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A company needs its application to survive a zonal failure with the least operational overhead. What should the architect verify when choosing where to deploy?
options: That the project has an organization node
That billing export is enabled
That the Cloud SQL Admin API is enabled
That the chosen region has multiple zones and resources are spread across them
explain: A region is a collection of zones, so spreading resources across zones within one region survives a zonal failure. Organization nodes, billing exports, and API enablement do not provide fault tolerance.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: The Cloud SQL Admin API is enabled in Project A. Can an application in Project B use it?
options: No, because APIs are enabled per project
Yes, because enabled APIs are shared across the organization
Yes, if the two projects share a VPC
Only for networking-related APIs
explain: API enablement is scoped to a single project, so Project B must enable the API independently. Sharing a VPC affects networking, not API enablement.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A company runs separate development, staging, and production environments, each containing many projects. How should folders be used?
options: Create one folder per developer
Folders cannot contain projects, so use labels instead
Create dev, staging, and prod folders and place each environment's projects inside for grouped IAM and policy management
Place every project in a single folder
explain: Folders group projects so IAM policies and organization policies can be applied once per environment. One folder per developer or a single flat folder defeats that grouping.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: Who is able to link a project to a billing account?
options: Anyone with the Viewer role on the project
Someone holding a billing role such as Billing Account Creator or Billing Account Administrator on that billing account
Any authenticated Google user
Only Google Cloud support
explain: Linking requires billing IAM permissions on the billing account (plus rights on the project). The Viewer role grants read-only access and cannot modify billing linkage.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: Before a major product launch, an engineer wants to confirm the project will not hit resource limits. Where should they check current usage against limits?
options: Cloud Trace
Billing reports
Cloud DNS
IAM & Admin > Quotas in the Cloud Console
explain: The Quotas page shows current usage versus limits per service and region, and it is where increases are requested. Trace, billing, and DNS do not track quota consumption.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A security team needs a searchable inventory of every resource across all projects in the organization, including change history. Which service provides this?
options: Cloud Trace
Cloud Profiler
Cloud Asset Inventory
Cloud Build
explain: Cloud Asset Inventory provides a searchable view of resources, IAM policies, and metadata across the organization with history. Trace and Profiler are performance tools, not inventory tools.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A new project is created with default settings. What VPC network exists in it?
options: A default VPC network in auto mode with a subnet in each region
No network until one is created manually
A custom-mode VPC with no subnets
A Shared VPC already attached
explain: New projects get a default auto-mode VPC with one subnet per region, unless an organization policy disables it. Shared VPC must be explicitly configured by a network administrator.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A company wants to run a stateless containerized web API that scales to zero when idle, with minimal operational overhead. Which compute option is the best fit?
options: A Compute Engine managed instance group
Cloud Run
A GKE Standard cluster
Bare Metal Solution
explain: Cloud Run is serverless for containers: it scales to zero, and Google manages the infrastructure. A MIG or GKE cluster leaves node management with you, which is more operational overhead than the scenario needs.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A team wants to run Kubernetes workloads without managing or patching nodes themselves. Which should they choose?
options: GKE Standard with manually managed node pools
Compute Engine VMs running kubelet
Cloud Run
GKE Autopilot
explain: GKE Autopilot is the managed mode where Google provisions and manages nodes, so the team only defines workloads. In GKE Standard mode the customer manages node pools, upgrades, and sizing.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A batch rendering workload is fault-tolerant and can be interrupted at any time. How can the company minimize its compute cost?
options: Use Spot VMs for the workload
Use sole-tenant nodes
Use on-demand VMs with attached GPUs
Purchase committed use discounts with a three-year term
explain: Spot VMs offer deep discounts for interruptible, fault-tolerant work — exactly this scenario. Sole-tenant nodes and GPUs add cost, and committed use discounts suit steady, non-interruptible usage.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A workload needs 10 vCPUs and 40 GB of RAM, which falls between the standard predefined machine types. What minimizes cost without overprovisioning?
options: Use the next larger predefined machine type
Split the workload across two smaller VMs
Create a custom machine type with exactly 10 vCPUs and 40 GB of RAM
Use a memory-optimized predefined machine type
explain: Custom machine types let you specify exact vCPU and memory counts so you stop paying for capacity you do not need. The larger predefined type wastes money, and splitting adds management overhead.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A company needs 20 identical web servers that automatically replace failed instances and scale with traffic. What should they build?
options: Twenty standalone VMs created one by one
An instance template plus a managed instance group with autoscaling
A single very large VM
Twenty Cloud Run functions
explain: An instance template defines the identical configuration and a managed instance group provides self-healing and autoscaling. Standalone VMs have neither, and a single VM is a single point of failure.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: Regulatory data must be retained for seven years and is almost never read. Which Cloud Storage class minimizes storage cost?
options: Standard
Nearline
Coldline
Archive
explain: Archive is the lowest-cost class, designed for data accessed less than once a year. Standard and Nearline charge more per GB stored, which adds up over seven years of retention.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A company keeps database backups that are restored roughly once a month for testing. Which Cloud Storage class is the most cost-effective fit?
options: Nearline
Archive
Standard
Coldline
explain: Nearline is priced for data accessed about once a month. Archive is cheaper to store but charges high retrieval fees that would outweigh the savings at monthly access frequency.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: Objects in a bucket should automatically move to Coldline after 90 days and be deleted after 365 days. How should this be implemented?
options: Manually move and delete objects on a schedule
A Cloud Scheduler job that lists and moves objects
A Cloud Storage lifecycle management rule
Object versioning
explain: Lifecycle management rules automatically transition storage classes or delete objects based on age and other conditions. Manual moves and Scheduler jobs add operational overhead, and versioning retains rather than deletes.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A database VM in a single zone needs the highest-performance block storage available. Which disk type should be attached?
options: Standard persistent disk
SSD persistent disk
A Cloud Storage bucket
Filestore
explain: SSD persistent disks deliver far higher IOPS and throughput than standard disks for latency-sensitive databases. Cloud Storage is object storage and Filestore is file storage — neither is block storage for a VM.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A stateful VM must keep its data disk available through a zonal outage with no manual failover. Which storage option should back it?
options: A zonal standard persistent disk
A local SSD
A Cloud Storage bucket mounted with gcsfuse
A regional persistent disk
explain: Regional persistent disks replicate data synchronously across two zones, so the disk survives a zonal failure. Zonal disks and local SSDs are lost with the zone or the VM.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A global application needs a relational database that scales horizontally and provides strong consistency across continents. Which database should be chosen?
options: Spanner
Cloud SQL
Bigtable
Firestore
explain: Spanner is the globally distributed relational database with horizontal scale and external consistency. Cloud SQL is regional, while Bigtable and Firestore are NoSQL and do not offer relational semantics.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A company ingests billions of time-series sensor readings per day and needs low-latency lookups by device ID and timestamp. Which database is the best fit?
options: BigQuery
Bigtable
Cloud SQL
Spanner
explain: Bigtable is a wide-column NoSQL store built for massive-scale, low-latency key-based access such as time series. BigQuery is for analytics, not millisecond lookups, and Cloud SQL cannot scale to this write volume.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: Analysts need to run ad-hoc SQL queries over petabytes of historical data with no infrastructure to manage. Which service should they use?
options: Cloud SQL
Bigtable
BigQuery
Memorystore
explain: BigQuery is the serverless data warehouse: petabyte-scale SQL analytics with no servers to manage. Cloud SQL is transactional, Bigtable is key-value, and Memorystore is an in-memory cache.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A mobile app needs a serverless document database with real-time synchronization to client devices. Which should the team choose?
options: Cloud SQL
Spanner
Bigtable
Firestore
explain: Firestore is the serverless document database with built-in real-time sync to mobile and web clients. Cloud SQL and Spanner are relational, and Bigtable lacks the document model and client sync.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A company wants PostgreSQL compatibility with higher performance and availability than Cloud SQL for a demanding transactional workload. Which database fits?
options: AlloyDB for PostgreSQL
Bigtable
Firestore
BigQuery
explain: AlloyDB is Google's high-performance PostgreSQL-compatible database for demanding transactional workloads. Bigtable, Firestore, and BigQuery are not PostgreSQL-compatible relational options.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A web application needs a fully managed in-memory cache to reduce load on its primary database. Which service should be used?
options: Cloud Storage
Memorystore for Redis
Bigtable
Pub/Sub
explain: Memorystore provides managed Redis (and Memcached) for sub-millisecond caching. Cloud Storage is object storage, Bigtable is persistent NoSQL, and Pub/Sub is messaging — none serve as an in-memory cache.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A VM should accept SSH connections only from the corporate office IP range. How should this be enforced?
options: Delete the subnet's default route
Assign the VM an external IP and nothing else
Create a VPC firewall rule allowing tcp:22 from the office CIDR range, targeted with the VM's network tag
Enable Cloud NAT on the subnet
explain: VPC firewall rules control ingress by source CIDR and can target VMs by network tag, which is exactly this requirement. Cloud NAT provides outbound-only connectivity and does not filter inbound SSH.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: Private VMs without external IP addresses need to download OS updates from the internet, but nothing on the internet may initiate connections to them. What provides this outbound-only connectivity?
options: An external Application Load Balancer
VPC peering
An external IP address on each VM
Cloud NAT
explain: Cloud NAT lets private instances reach the internet for outbound connections while remaining unreachable inbound. External IPs or load balancers would expose the VMs, and peering connects VPCs rather than the internet.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A company serves HTTPS traffic to users worldwide from backends in multiple regions, using a single anycast IP address. Which load balancer should they deploy?
options: Global external Application Load Balancer
Regional internal passthrough Network Load Balancer
Regional external proxy Network Load Balancer
DNS-based round robin
explain: The global external Application Load Balancer provides a single anycast IP with Layer 7 routing to backends across regions. Regional load balancers are confined to one region, and DNS round robin lacks health checking and failover.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: Microservices inside a VPC need load balancing that is not reachable from the internet. Which load balancer type fits?
options: External Application Load Balancer
Internal Application Load Balancer
Cloud CDN
Cloud DNS
explain: Internal load balancers distribute traffic within the VPC with private IPs only. External load balancers are internet-facing, while Cloud CDN and Cloud DNS serve different purposes entirely.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A central networking team must manage a single VPC used by application workloads in dozens of projects. Which design should they implement?
options: VPC peering between every pair of projects
A Cloud VPN tunnel per project
Shared VPC with the network hosted in a central host project
One subnet per project in the default VPC
explain: Shared VPC lets a host project own the network while service projects attach to it, keeping administration centralized. Full-mesh peering across dozens of projects is unmanageable, and VPNs are for hybrid connectivity.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: VPC A is peered with VPC B, and VPC B is peered with VPC C. Can workloads in VPC A communicate directly with workloads in VPC C?
options: Yes, routes propagate automatically through the middle VPC
Yes, as long as firewall rules allow the traffic
Yes, by routing through VPC B as a transit network
No, because VPC peering is non-transitive
explain: VPC peering is non-transitive: each pair of VPCs needs its own peering. Firewall rules cannot substitute for the missing peering, and VPC B does not forward traffic between peers.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A company wants managed, authoritative DNS hosting for its public domain with a high availability SLA. Which service should they use?
options: Cloud DNS
A BIND server running on a Compute Engine VM
Cloud NAT
Private Google Access
explain: Cloud DNS is the managed authoritative DNS service with a 100% availability SLA. Running BIND on a VM adds patching and availability work, and NAT and Private Google Access are unrelated to DNS hosting.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A company needs private, high-throughput, low-latency connectivity between its on-premises datacenter and Google Cloud. Which option should they choose?
options: Cloud VPN over the public internet
Dedicated Interconnect
Cloud NAT
Carrier Peering
explain: Dedicated Interconnect provides a private, dedicated connection with high throughput for hybrid workloads. Cloud VPN traverses the public internet with lower throughput, and Cloud NAT only handles outbound traffic for VMs.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A subnet must accommodate at least 500 VM IP addresses. Google Cloud reserves 4 addresses per subnet. Which is the smallest CIDR range that fits?
options: 10.0.0.0/24 (252 usable addresses)
10.0.0.0/25 (124 usable addresses)
10.0.0.0/23 (508 usable addresses)
10.0.0.0/22 (1,020 usable addresses)
explain: A /23 provides 512 addresses minus 4 reserved, or 508 usable — the smallest range holding 500 VMs. A /24 only yields 252 usable addresses, which is too small, while a /22 wastes address space.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A team wants to deploy a standard web application from source code using a simple deploy command, with automatic scaling and built-in traffic splitting between versions. Which fully managed option fits best?
options: GKE Autopilot
Compute Engine
Cloud Run functions
App Engine standard environment
explain: App Engine standard deploys from source with gcloud app deploy, autoscales, and splits traffic across versions natively. GKE still involves cluster concepts, and Cloud Run functions are event-driven rather than versioned web services.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A company wants code to run automatically whenever a file is uploaded to a Cloud Storage bucket, with no servers to manage. Which approach has the least operational overhead?
options: Cloud Run functions triggered by Eventarc on object finalization
A VM that polls the bucket every minute
A GKE CronJob that lists new objects
Cloud Scheduler invoking a script on a VM
explain: Event-driven Cloud Run functions scale to zero and run only on upload events. Polling VMs or CronJobs keep infrastructure running and add code to maintain.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: Multiple VMs need concurrent read-write access to a shared POSIX-compliant file system (NFS). Which storage service should be used?
options: A zonal persistent disk attached to each VM
Filestore
A Cloud Storage bucket
Bigtable
explain: Filestore is the managed NFS file service designed for shared multi-VM access. A persistent disk attaches to a single VM, Cloud Storage is object storage without POSIX semantics, and Bigtable is a NoSQL database.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: Before migrating, a company wants to estimate the monthly Google Cloud cost of a planned architecture. Which tool should they use?
options: Cloud Billing reports
Recommender
Cloud Trace
Google Cloud Pricing Calculator
explain: The Pricing Calculator estimates future costs for planned resources. Billing reports show historical spend, Recommender suggests optimizations, and Trace analyzes latency — none estimate planned architectures.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A company runs a stable baseline of VMs 24/7 and is willing to commit to one or three years of usage. How can they reduce the hourly cost of that steady usage?
options: Switch the VMs to Spot VMs
Rely on sustained use discounts
Purchase committed use discounts
Use preemptible GPUs
explain: Committed use discounts reward 1- or 3-year commitments to steady usage with significant savings. Spot VMs suit interruptible work, not a stable baseline, and sustained use discounts are a legacy mechanism.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A team wants to be paged when a VM's CPU utilization stays above 80% for five minutes. Which feature should they configure?
options: A Cloud Monitoring alerting policy on the CPU utilization metric
A log-based metric
An uptime check
A Cloud Trace span
explain: Alerting policies evaluate metric conditions over a duration and trigger notifications. Uptime checks probe endpoints rather than metrics, and Trace analyzes request latency.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A company wants to verify that its public HTTPS endpoint responds correctly from multiple geographic locations. Which should they create?
options: A VPC firewall rule
A Cloud Profiler profile
A Cloud Monitoring uptime check
A VPC Flow Logs configuration
explain: Uptime checks probe a URL or IP from global locations and alert on failures. Firewall rules filter traffic, Profiler analyzes code performance, and Flow Logs record network telemetry.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A team wants to run SQL queries analyzing a month of application logs, for example counting errors by service. What should they set up?
options: Read the logs only in the Logs Explorer
A Cloud Logging sink routing the logs to BigQuery
Cloud Trace
A longer retention period on the default log bucket
explain: A log sink to BigQuery makes log entries queryable with SQL for analysis. The Logs Explorer is for interactive browsing, and retention alone does not enable SQL analytics.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: How long are logs retained in the default _Default log bucket unless the retention is changed?
options: 7 days
7 years
10 years
30 days
explain: The _Default bucket retains logs for 30 days by default, configurable up to 3,650 days. Longer compliance retention typically uses sinks to Cloud Storage or BigQuery.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A team needs host metrics such as CPU, memory, and disk from their VMs in Cloud Monitoring, plus third-party application logs in Cloud Logging. What should they install on the VMs?
options: The Ops Agent
The Cloud SQL Auth Proxy
Anthos Service Mesh
The Cloud Profiler agent
explain: The Ops Agent is the unified agent collecting host metrics and logs into the operations suite. The SQL Auth Proxy connects to Cloud SQL, and Profiler samples application code performance.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: Which command opens an SSH session to a VM named web-1 in the zone us-central1-a?
options: gcloud ssh web-1
gsutil ssh web-1
gcloud compute ssh web-1 --zone=us-central1-a
gcloud compute connect web-1
explain: gcloud compute ssh is the correct command, with --zone specifying the VM's zone. gsutil manages Cloud Storage, and the other two commands do not exist.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: Which command copies a local file named report.pdf into a Cloud Storage bucket named my-bucket?
options: gcloud compute scp report.pdf my-bucket
gcloud storage cp report.pdf gs://my-bucket/
gcloud sql import report.pdf
bq load my-bucket report.pdf
explain: gcloud storage cp (or the equivalent gsutil cp) copies objects to and from buckets using the gs:// scheme. gcloud compute scp copies between VMs, not buckets.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A team wants a point-in-time backup of a persistent disk before performing a risky database upgrade. What should they create?
options: A machine image of the entire project
A Cloud Storage lifecycle rule
A second regional persistent disk
A snapshot of the persistent disk
explain: Snapshots capture incremental point-in-time copies of persistent disks and can be used to restore or create new disks. Lifecycle rules manage object storage, not VM disks.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: Daily automated backups of several persistent disks with a 14-day retention are required. How should this be implemented?
options: A snapshot schedule attached to the disks
A cron job on each VM copying data
Manual snapshots taken each morning
Cloud Scheduler invoking gsutil
explain: Snapshot schedules automate snapshot creation on a cadence with configurable retention. Manual snapshots and VM cron jobs add operational overhead and are error-prone.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A managed instance group must be moved to a new instance template with no downtime for users. Which update approach should be used?
options: Recreate every instance simultaneously
Delete the group and recreate it
A rolling update that replaces instances gradually within surge and unavailability limits
SSH into each VM and update it in place
explain: Rolling updates replace instances incrementally so capacity stays available, controlled by max surge and max unavailable settings. Recreating everything at once causes an outage.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: Unhealthy instances in a managed instance group should be detected and automatically recreated. What enables this behavior?
options: A VPC firewall rule
An autohealing policy with a health check
A snapshot schedule
A larger machine type
explain: Autohealing policies use health checks to detect failed instances and recreate them. Firewall rules and snapshots do not monitor or repair instance health.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A GKE Standard cluster needs a Kubernetes version upgrade with minimal disruption to running workloads. What is the recommended approach?
options: Delete the cluster and recreate it on the new version
Upgrade all node pools simultaneously
Disable cluster autoscaling during the upgrade
Perform a rolling node pool upgrade, optionally using surge or blue-green upgrades
explain: Rolling, surge, and blue-green node pool upgrades replace nodes gradually so workloads keep running. Deleting the cluster or upgrading everything at once causes downtime.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: Which command lists the nodes in a GKE cluster?
options: kubectl get nodes
gcloud container clusters list
gsutil ls
gcloud compute instances list
explain: kubectl get nodes queries the Kubernetes API for cluster nodes. gcloud container clusters list lists clusters themselves, not their nodes.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: Requests flowing through several microservices are slow, and the team needs to identify which service adds the most latency. Which tool should they use?
options: Cloud Logging
A Cloud Monitoring dashboard
Cloud Trace
Cloud Asset Inventory
explain: Cloud Trace performs distributed tracing that breaks request latency down by service and span. Logging records events and Monitoring charts metrics, but neither traces a request across services.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A team wants an alert every time the string OutOfMemoryError appears in their application logs. What should they create?
options: An uptime check
A log-based metric counting matching entries, with an alerting policy on it
A Cloud Trace span
A billing budget
explain: Log-based metrics turn matching log entries into a countable metric that alerting policies can evaluate. Uptime checks probe endpoints and cannot inspect log content.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A VM is unreachable over SSH after a firewall rule change locked everyone out. How can an administrator regain console access to fix it?
options: Assign the VM a new external IP address
Delete and recreate the VM
Enable Cloud NAT
Connect to the serial console with gcloud compute connect-to-serial-port
explain: The serial console provides out-of-band access independent of SSH and firewall rules. A new IP or NAT does not bypass the blocking firewall rule, and deleting the VM destroys its state.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: Every VM created from an instance template must install a monitoring agent on its first boot. How should this be configured?
options: Add a startup script to the instance template's metadata
SSH into each VM after creation and install it manually
Use a shutdown script
Add the agent to a firewall rule
explain: Startup scripts in instance metadata run automatically on first boot, so every instance from the template is configured identically. Manual installation does not scale, and shutdown scripts run at termination.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A team wants advance warning before their project hits Compute Engine API quotas. What should they do?
options: Enable Cloud Trace on the project
Delete unused projects
Create a Cloud Monitoring alert on quota usage metrics
Request unlimited quota from support
explain: Quota metrics are visible in Cloud Monitoring, so an alerting policy can warn before limits are reached. Trace analyzes latency, and quotas cannot be made unlimited.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A project's cloud spend suddenly doubles overnight. Where should the engineer look first to find the cause?
options: Cloud Trace
Billing reports broken down by service and SKU
VPC Flow Logs
Cloud DNS query logs
explain: Billing reports show spend by service, project, and SKU, revealing which resource drove the spike. Trace, Flow Logs, and DNS logs contain no cost data.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A team wants to manage Google Cloud infrastructure declaratively using YAML templates native to the platform. Which service should they use?
options: Cloud Build
Cloud Scheduler
Puppet
Deployment Manager
explain: Deployment Manager is Google Cloud's native infrastructure-as-code service using declarative YAML (and Jinja/Python) templates. Cloud Build runs CI/CD pipelines and Cloud Scheduler triggers jobs on a cron schedule.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A running managed instance group needs a larger machine type. What is the correct approach?
options: Create a new instance template with the larger machine type and update the MIG to use it
Edit the existing instance template in place
SSH into each VM and change its machine type
Delete the project and recreate it
explain: Instance templates are immutable, so changes require a new template followed by a MIG update (rolling or recreating). Editing in place is not possible, and per-VM changes would be wiped by the group.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A managed instance group should keep serving traffic even if an entire zone fails. How should it be configured?
options: As a single-zone MIG with one very large VM
As two separate MIGs in the same zone
As a regional MIG distributing instances across multiple zones
As a MIG using only Spot VMs
explain: A regional MIG spreads instances across zones in the region, surviving a zonal failure. Single-zone configurations share the zone's fate regardless of VM size.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A fleet of Compute Engine VMs needs OS patches applied on a recurring schedule with minimal manual effort. Which service should be used?
options: Manual patching over SSH
VM Manager OS patch management
Cloud Trace
A VPC firewall rule
explain: VM Manager's patch management automates OS patching across fleets on a schedule with compliance reporting. Manual SSH patching does not scale, and Trace and firewall rules are unrelated to patching.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: An application pod in GKE is crash-looping. What is the most useful first diagnostic step?
options: Delete the cluster
Increase the node pool size
Restart Cloud Logging
Check the pod's logs with kubectl logs
explain: kubectl logs shows the container's output, which usually reveals the crash cause. Resizing the node pool or deleting the cluster treats symptoms without diagnosing the failure.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A team wants a shared dashboard showing request latency and error rate for their Cloud Run service. Where should they build it?
options: A Cloud Monitoring custom dashboard
Cloud Trace alone
Billing reports
Cloud Asset Inventory
explain: Cloud Monitoring dashboards visualize metrics such as latency and error rate in one shared view. Trace shows individual request traces, and billing and asset inventory have no performance metrics.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A VM fails to boot after a configuration change. Where can the boot-time error messages best be diagnosed?
options: VPC Flow Logs
The billing export to BigQuery
The VM's serial port output in Cloud Logging
Cloud DNS logs
explain: Serial port output captures the VM's console including boot messages, and it is available in Cloud Logging. Flow Logs record network packets and DNS logs record queries — neither shows boot output.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A Cloud SQL instance needs automated daily backups plus point-in-time recovery to any minute in the last seven days. What should be enabled?
options: Manual on-demand exports only
Automated backups with binary logging enabled
A persistent disk snapshot schedule
Cloud Storage object versioning
explain: Automated backups combined with binary (transaction) logs enable point-in-time recovery. Manual exports alone cannot restore to an arbitrary minute, and disk snapshots are for Compute Engine disks.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A company needs its relational database to remain available and recoverable even if an entire Google Cloud region fails. Which option provides cross-region protection?
options: A zonal Cloud SQL instance
A regional persistent disk
A single-zone GKE cluster
A Cloud SQL cross-region read replica
explain: Cross-region read replicas keep a copy of the data in another region, protecting against regional failure. Zonal and regional (multi-zone) options only survive zone-level events within one region.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: An engineer works across several projects and wants to change the default project used by gcloud commands. Which command does this?
options: gcloud config set project PROJECT_ID
gcloud auth login
gcloud projects delete PROJECT_ID
gsutil config
explain: gcloud config set project sets the default project for subsequent commands. gcloud auth login authenticates the user, and per-command --project flags only override for a single invocation.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: During underlying host maintenance, what happens to a standard Compute Engine VM by default?
options: It is terminated and must be restarted manually
It is deleted
It is live-migrated to another host with no downtime
It is paused for 24 hours
explain: The default host maintenance behavior is live migration: the VM moves to another host transparently. Terminate-on-maintenance is only the default for Spot VMs and other special cases.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A developer needs to view VM metrics and configurations but must not be able to modify anything. Which role follows the principle of least privilege?
options: Owner
Editor
Compute Admin
Compute Viewer
explain: Compute Viewer grants read-only access to Compute Engine resources, which is exactly what is needed. Owner, Editor, and Compute Admin all grant modification rights far beyond the requirement.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: Why should predefined IAM roles generally be preferred over the basic roles (Owner, Editor, Viewer)?
options: Basic roles have been removed from Google Cloud
Predefined roles grant narrower, service-specific permissions that follow least privilege
Predefined roles are free while basic roles cost extra
Basic roles cannot be assigned at the folder level
explain: Predefined roles bundle only the permissions needed for a specific job function, while basic roles are extremely broad (Editor can modify almost everything). Least privilege means choosing the narrowest role that works.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: No predefined IAM role matches the exact set of permissions a contractor needs. What should the administrator create?
options: A custom IAM role containing only the required permissions
A temporary Owner grant
A new organization for the contractor
A service account with the Editor role
explain: Custom roles let you assemble precisely the permissions required — the textbook least-privilege answer. Temporary Owner grants and Editor roles over-provision access.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: An application running on Compute Engine needs to read objects from Cloud Storage. What is the recommended identity for the application to use?
options: The developer's personal user account
A shared username and password stored on the VM
A service account attached to the VM, granted the Storage Object Viewer role
The Owner role granted to the project
explain: Service accounts are identities for workloads; attaching one to the VM with a minimal role avoids human credentials on machines. Personal accounts and shared passwords cannot be audited or rotated cleanly.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A support engineer occasionally needs to act as an application's service account for debugging, but distributing the account's keys is prohibited. What should be used?
options: Download the service account key and email it to the engineer
Grant the engineer the Owner role
Create a second service account with the same roles
Service account impersonation via the Service Account Token Creator role
explain: Impersonation issues short-lived tokens so the engineer can act as the service account without ever handling long-lived keys. Downloading and sharing keys is exactly the practice to avoid.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: What is the main security concern with user-managed service account keys?
options: They can be leaked, copied, or forgotten, expanding the attack surface — Google-managed keys are preferred
They expire after one hour
They do not work with Google Cloud APIs
They incur an additional monthly charge
explain: Downloadable keys can be committed to code, shared, or lost, and each copy is a new attack vector. Best practice is to avoid them using attached service accounts, impersonation, or Workload Identity Federation.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: An on-premises CI/CD system needs to call Google Cloud APIs without storing a long-lived service account key. Which feature enables this?
options: A user-managed service account key
The Owner role on the CI service account
Workload Identity Federation
Cloud NAT
explain: Workload Identity Federation lets external identity providers exchange their tokens for short-lived Google Cloud credentials — no keys to store or rotate. A user-managed key is the pattern being replaced.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A company wants SSH access to its VMs tied to IAM identities, with no shared SSH keys to manage. Which feature should they enable?
options: Project-wide SSH keys in instance metadata
OS Login
Cloud VPN
IAP Desktop only
explain: OS Login links IAM users to Linux accounts and manages SSH keys automatically, eliminating shared keys. Project-wide metadata keys are static, shared, and harder to revoke per user.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: Administrators need SSH and RDP access to VMs that have no public IP addresses, without deploying bastion hosts. What provides this securely?
options: Temporarily assigning public IPs
Cloud NAT
A VPN tunnel to each VM
Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) TCP forwarding
explain: IAP TCP forwarding tunnels administrative protocols through Google's infrastructure with IAM-based access control — no bastions or public IPs needed. Cloud NAT only provides outbound connectivity.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: An IAM allow policy is made up of which elements?
options: Bindings that associate members with roles, optionally with conditions
Only user email addresses
Firewall rules and routes
Billing budgets and alerts
explain: An allow policy is a collection of bindings, each granting a role to members (users, groups, service accounts) with optional IAM Conditions. Firewall rules and budgets belong to different systems.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A contractor should be able to read objects in a bucket only during business hours. How can this time restriction be enforced?
options: A VPC firewall rule
A billing budget
An IAM Condition with a time restriction on the role binding
A separate project for the contractor
explain: IAM Conditions add attributes such as time windows to a binding, so access is only valid during business hours. Firewall rules filter network traffic, not IAM permissions.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: What is the difference between an organization policy and an IAM policy?
options: They are two names for the same thing
Organization policies set centralized constraints and restrictions on resources, while IAM policies grant permissions to members
IAM policies only control billing
Organization policies grant IAM roles
explain: Organization policies are guardrails that constrain what can be configured (for example, blocking public IPs); IAM policies answer who is allowed to do what. They solve different problems.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A company must guarantee that no one — regardless of any other role grants — can delete production Cloud Storage buckets. Which mechanism enforces this?
options: Remove every IAM role from all users
A VPC firewall rule
An organization policy
An IAM deny policy on the buckets
explain: IAM deny policies explicitly forbid actions and take precedence over any allow policies, which is exactly the 'no one, no matter what' requirement. Organization policies constrain resource configuration rather than overriding grants.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A company must control and regularly rotate the encryption keys protecting its Cloud Storage data. Which service should they use?
options: Cloud KMS with customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK)
TLS certificates on the clients
VPC Service Controls
An IAM deny policy
explain: Cloud KMS with CMEK gives the customer ownership of key lifecycle including rotation, while Google still performs the encryption. TLS protects data in transit, not stored objects.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A company wants to reduce the risk of data exfiltration by defining a boundary that Google Cloud services cannot copy data across. Which service creates this perimeter?
options: Cloud NAT
A billing budget
VPC Service Controls
Cloud DNS
explain: VPC Service Controls define a security perimeter around projects and services to mitigate data exfiltration. NAT, budgets, and DNS do not restrict cross-boundary data movement.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: VMs without external IP addresses need to reach Google APIs and services such as Cloud Storage. What enables this private access?
options: Cloud NAT
Private Google Access on the subnet
An external Application Load Balancer
Dedicated Interconnect
explain: Private Google Access lets VMs with only internal IPs reach Google APIs and services. Cloud NAT is for the public internet, and a load balancer or Interconnect is unnecessary for API access.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A compliance team needs a record of who changed IAM policies in the last month. Where should they look?
options: Cloud Trace
VPC Flow Logs
The billing export
Cloud Audit Logs (Admin Activity) in Cloud Logging
explain: Admin Activity audit logs record configuration changes including IAM policy modifications, with the actor identity and timestamp. Trace, Flow Logs, and billing contain no IAM change records.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: What is the recommended way to protect Google Cloud user accounts against credential theft and phishing?
options: Enforce 2-step verification through Cloud Identity or Google Workspace
Have the whole team share one administrator account
Disable multi-factor authentication for convenience
Use service accounts instead of human accounts
explain: Enforced 2-step verification adds a second factor so stolen passwords alone are insufficient. Shared accounts destroy auditability, and service accounts are for workloads, not people.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A production project must be protected from accidental deletion. What should be placed on the project?
options: A VPC firewall rule
A billing budget
A lien
An uptime check
explain: Liens block project deletion until they are explicitly removed, guarding against accidents. Firewall rules, budgets, and uptime checks do not affect deletion.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A new hire asks for broad administrative access to everything so they can get started quickly. Following Google Cloud best practices, what should the administrator do?
options: Grant the Owner role as requested
Grant only the predefined roles needed for their specific tasks
Create a new organization for the hire
Give them a service account key with Editor access
explain: Least privilege means starting with the minimal predefined roles for the person's tasks and expanding only as needed. Owner-on-day-one and standing service account keys both violate that principle.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A developer needs a browser-based terminal with the Cloud SDK preinstalled and a small persistent home directory for scripts, without provisioning any infrastructure. Which option is the best fit?
options: A Compute Engine VM with a large persistent disk for tooling
The Cloud Console Logs Explorer with a query filter
Cloud Shell, which provides a browser terminal, preinstalled gcloud/kubectl/bq tools, and 5 GB of persistent home-directory storage
A Cloud Workstations managed development environment
explain: Cloud Shell is the free browser-based terminal with the SDK preinstalled and 5 GB of persistent $HOME storage; only the underlying VM is ephemeral. A full VM is overkill for a shell session, Cloud Workstations are heavier managed IDEs, and the Logs Explorer is not a terminal.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An engineer works across development and production projects and wants named, switchable sets of gcloud defaults (project, region, zone). Which approach should they use?
options: Create named gcloud configurations (gcloud configurations create/activate) for each environment
Run gcloud auth login before every command
Set the CLOUDSDK_CORE_PROJECT environment variable in each terminal tab
Run gcloud init once and edit the SDK binary afterward
explain: Named configurations store complete property sets that you switch between with gcloud configurations activate. gcloud auth login changes identity rather than defaults, environment variables are fragile across sessions, and gcloud init only bootstraps the single default configuration.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A developer is building a Python app locally with Google Cloud client libraries and wants the libraries to pick up their user credentials automatically. Which command sets this up?
options: gcloud auth login
gcloud iam service-accounts keys create
gcloud config set project
gcloud auth application-default login
explain: gcloud auth application-default login writes Application Default Credentials that client libraries discover automatically. gcloud auth login authenticates only the CLI itself, downloading a service account key is discouraged, and setting the project provides no credentials at all.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An administrator accidentally deletes a production project. What is true about recovering it?
options: The project is permanently destroyed the moment deletion is confirmed
The project enters a 30-day recovery window during which it can be restored with gcloud projects undelete
Only Google Cloud support can restore it, and only within 24 hours
A new project with the same project ID can be created immediately to replace it
explain: Deleted projects are retained for about 30 days and can be restored with gcloud projects undelete; the project ID stays reserved until final deletion. No support ticket is required, and the ID cannot be reused while the deleted project still exists.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A finance analyst needs to link new projects to the company's billing account but must not be able to change payment instruments or see full billing details. Which role fits?
options: Billing Account Administrator
Billing Account User
Project Owner
Billing Account Viewer
explain: Billing Account User grants exactly the right to link projects to the billing account without broader powers. Billing Account Administrator can modify payments (too broad), Viewer is read-only, and Project Owner carries no rights on the billing account itself.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A team wants an email at 80% of actual spend and another alert if forecasted spend will reach 100% of their monthly budget. How should they configure this?
options: Create two separate billing accounts, one per threshold
Enable the billing export to BigQuery and query it daily
Set an organization policy constraint on spend
Create a billing budget with custom alert thresholds for actual and forecasted spend, with email notifications
explain: Billing budgets support multiple thresholds evaluated against actual or forecasted spend, notifying via email or Pub/Sub. A common misconception is that budgets cap spending — they only alert. Exports enable analysis but do not notify, and organization policies cannot constrain spend.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An external auditor needs the company's detailed monthly cloud cost data as flat files they can download, without being given BigQuery access. Which export should be configured?
options: A billing export to Cloud Storage, which delivers CSV/JSON cost files to a bucket
A billing export to BigQuery only
A Cloud Logging sink to Cloud Storage
A billing budget with Pub/Sub notifications
explain: The Cloud Storage billing export produces downloadable files the auditor can fetch directly; the BigQuery export requires SQL access to query. Logging sinks carry log entries rather than billing data, and budgets only send alerts.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: Billing is disabled on a project that runs several production VMs. What happens to the running resources?
options: They keep running and the charges are written off
They are immediately and permanently deleted
Billable resources are stopped or suspended until billing is re-enabled
Only new resources are blocked; existing ones are unaffected
explain: Disabling billing suspends billable resources — running VMs are stopped — but does not delete them, and they can be restarted once billing is re-enabled. It neither forgives charges nor leaves workloads running for free.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An engineer tries to apply the label Team: Data-Engineering to a VM and the API rejects it. What is wrong?
options: Labels cannot be applied to Compute Engine VMs
The label key must be at least 20 characters long
Labels require the Owner role to apply
Label keys and values must be lowercase; 'Team' and 'Data-Engineering' violate the format
explain: Label keys and values must be lowercase (letters, numbers, underscores, and hyphens), so the uppercase characters cause the rejection. Labels work fine on VMs, have no 20-character minimum, and do not require the Owner role.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A company needs environment-based access control (for example, only the prod on-call group can administer prod databases) enforced by IAM itself. Labels cannot do this. What should they use?
options: Resource Manager tags combined with IAM Conditions in role bindings
More descriptive resource names
A separate billing account per environment
Labels with a Cloud Function that revokes access
explain: Tags, unlike labels, are designed for policy enforcement and can be referenced in IAM Conditions to gate access. Labels are for organization and cost attribution, not access control; names and billing accounts do not drive IAM decisions.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An organization policy denies external IP assignment at the organization level. A folder administrator creates a folder-level policy allowing external IPs for one project. What is the effective result?
options: The folder policy overrides the organization policy for that project
Both policies are ignored because they conflict
The project gets external IPs but the rest of the organization does not
The organization-level denial still applies, because denied values merge down and a child policy cannot lift a parent's denial
explain: For list constraints, parent and child policies merge, and a value denied higher in the hierarchy stays denied below — child policies cannot punch holes in a parent's denial. Any exemption must be granted at the level where the denial was set.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A deployment fails with a quota error for in-use IP addresses, but the Quotas page shows plenty of regional CPU quota remaining. What should the engineer check first?
options: Whether the Compute Engine API is enabled
Which specific quota is exhausted — IP address quotas are tracked separately from per-region CPU quotas, so CPU headroom is irrelevant
Whether the billing account has sufficient credit
The VPC firewall rules for the subnet
explain: Quotas are independent pools: exhausting the IP address quota is unaffected by remaining CPU quota. API enablement and billing do not produce quota errors, and firewall rules do not limit quota consumption.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A security review must list every principal that can modify VMs in a project and which roles grant that access. Which command produces this?
options: gcloud projects get-iam-policy PROJECT_ID
gcloud compute instances list
gcloud logging read for Admin Activity logs
gcloud billing accounts list
explain: get-iam-policy dumps the project's allow-policy bindings, showing exactly who holds which roles. Listing instances shows VMs rather than grants, and audit logs record past actions rather than current permissions.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: After an acquisition, a project must move from the acquired company's organization to the parent company's organization. Which statement is true?
options: Projects can never change organizations; all resources must be recreated
The project must be deleted and restored in the new organization
The project can be moved with the resourcemanager.projects.move permission, carrying its resources and configuration with it
Moving is automatic once the billing account is shared
explain: Resource Manager supports moving projects between organizations for users with the move permission; resources, IAM bindings, and network configuration move along. Sharing a billing account affects invoicing only, not organization membership.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A company uses Microsoft 365 for email and has no Google Workspace, but needs a Google Cloud organization node for centralized policy management. What should they set up?
options: Cloud Identity, which provides the identity domain for the organization without requiring Google Workspace
A consumer Gmail account as the organization owner
A second billing account
A Shared VPC host project
explain: Cloud Identity supplies the domain-backed identity that an organization node requires; Google Workspace is not mandatory. Consumer Gmail accounts cannot anchor an organization node.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An engineer needs the exact flag to set a bucket's storage class during creation with the gcloud CLI. What is the fastest reliable way to find it?
options: Open a Cloud Support case to ask for the flag syntax
Run gcloud storage buckets create --help to read the command's documented flags and examples
Read the bucket's IAM policy in the console
Try likely flag names until one is accepted
explain: Every gcloud command group ships built-in --help documenting its flags with examples, which is the authoritative quick reference. A support case is slow overkill, IAM policies do not document CLI flags, and guessing wastes time.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An application VM is running with the project's default Compute Engine service account, which currently holds broad roles. Following least privilege, what should the team do?
options: Keep the default service account since Google manages it
Create a dedicated service account with only the roles the application needs and attach it to the VM
Download a key for the default service account and store it on the VM
Grant the default service account the Owner role so nothing breaks
explain: Workloads should run as dedicated service accounts holding only the permissions they need; the default account's broad grants violate least privilege. Downloading keys or widening roles increases the attack surface rather than reducing it.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A startup with twelve projects wants a single $2,000 monthly budget covering all of them with one alert stream. How should the budget be scoped?
options: Create twelve identical budgets, one per project
Budgets can only track a single project, so this is impossible
Put all resources into one project
Create one budget at the billing-account level covering all linked projects
explain: A budget can scope to the entire billing account (or a chosen subset of projects), aggregating spend across projects into one alert stream. Per-project budgets fragment alerting, and merging projects solely for billing destroys useful isolation.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: Two separate organizations — a parent company and a subsidiary — want one consolidated invoice. What is true about billing accounts and organizations?
options: One billing account can link projects from multiple organizations, so both orgs' projects can share a single billing account
Each organization requires its own billing account; consolidation is impossible
Projects must be moved into one organization first
Consolidation requires merging the Cloud Identity domains
explain: Billing accounts are not bound to a single organization: projects from different orgs can link to one billing account for a unified invoice. No organization move or identity-domain merge is needed.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An engineer's gcloud commands are unexpectedly acting on the wrong project, and gcloud auth list shows two signed-in accounts. What is the likely cause and fix?
options: The wrong API is enabled; enable the correct one
The Cloud SDK installation is corrupted; reinstall it
An unintended account is active; switch it with gcloud config set account and verify the project with gcloud config list
The project was deleted; recreate it
explain: gcloud acts as the active account against the configured default project, so a second signed-in account explains the mix-up; auth list reveals it and config set account corrects it. Reinstalling the SDK or recreating the project does not address identity confusion.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: For compliance, no VM in the organization may expose a serial console. Which control enforces this centrally?
options: A VPC firewall rule blocking port 22
An IAM deny policy on compute.instances
Deleting the serial port output logs
The boolean organization policy constraint compute.disableSerialPortAccess set to enforced at the organization level
explain: The boolean constraint disables serial port access hierarchy-wide from one place. Firewall rules filter network traffic rather than the serial console, and deleting logs hides evidence instead of blocking access.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A support ticket asks for the project's project number (not the ID or name) to look up quota usage. How does the engineer find it?
options: It is the same as the project ID
Run gcloud projects describe PROJECT_ID and read the projectNumber field
Project numbers are only visible to billing administrators
Derive it from the project's creation date
explain: gcloud projects describe returns the immutable numeric projectNumber alongside the ID and name, visible to anyone who can view the project. The number is distinct from the project ID.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A company decides to commit to one year of steady Compute Engine usage for a discount. Where are committed use discounts purchased and managed?
options: In the Cloud Console under Billing > Commitments
With gcloud compute instances create using a commitment flag
Automatically; Google applies them whenever usage looks steady
Through a support ticket only
explain: Commitments are purchased and managed in the console under Billing > Commitments (or via the API); there is no per-VM creation flag, they are never automatic, and no support ticket is required.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A managed service provider resells Google Cloud to clients and needs separate invoices per client under one master billing arrangement. What should they use?
options: One project per client with labels
A separate organization per client
Billing subaccounts under the master billing account, one per client
A billing budget per client
explain: Billing subaccounts give each client their own invoice while rolling up to the master account for the reseller. Labels do not produce separate invoices, and budgets only generate alerts.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An application suddenly receives HTTP 429 responses with rateLimitExceeded from a Google Cloud API it calls heavily. What is the right response?
options: Purchase a committed use discount
Check the API's quota in the console, implement exponential backoff, and request a quota increase if the limit is adjustable
Enable the API again
Move the workload to a different region
explain: A 429 rateLimitExceeded signals an API rate quota: back off exponentially and request an increase for adjustable quotas. Committed use discounts cover sustained resource usage rather than API rates, the API is already enabled, and regions do not change API quotas.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A small internal tool gets a few requests per minute with occasional brief spikes and must stay as cheap as possible. Which machine type is the most cost-effective choice?
options: An E2 shared-core machine type such as e2-micro, which bursts CPU on a shared core at the lowest price point
A C2 compute-optimized machine type
An M2 memory-optimized machine type
A sole-tenant node
explain: Shared-core E2 types are the cheapest option for tiny, bursty workloads. C2 and M2 target heavy compute and memory needs at far higher cost, and sole-tenancy adds a premium for hardware isolation rather than savings.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A team must clone a VM — its boot disk data, attached data disks, metadata, and machine type — into another region for disaster-recovery testing. Which resource captures all of this?
options: A snapshot of the boot disk
A custom image
An instance template
A machine image, which stores the VM's full configuration plus all attached disks
explain: Machine images capture disks, metadata, and configuration together, enabling full-VM cloning across regions. Snapshots cover a single disk, custom images cover only the boot disk, and templates store configuration without disk data.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A security team wants protection against rootkits and boot-level malware on its VMs, with cryptographic verification of the boot chain. Which feature provides this?
options: Confidential VMs
Sole-tenant nodes
Shielded VMs, with Secure Boot, a virtual TPM, and integrity monitoring
OS Login
explain: Shielded VMs verify boot integrity through Secure Boot and a vTPM, with monitoring that flags tampering. Confidential VMs encrypt memory contents rather than verifying boot, sole-tenancy is about hardware isolation, and OS Login manages SSH access.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A cost estimate for Windows Server VMs comes back far higher than the Linux estimate for identical machine types. What explains the difference?
options: Windows VMs require sole-tenant nodes
Windows Server uses premium images that add a per-vCPU licensing surcharge
Windows VMs cannot use Spot pricing
The estimate tool double-counts Windows by mistake
explain: Premium OS images (Windows Server, RHEL, SLES) carry license fees on top of infrastructure cost. Sole-tenancy is not required for Windows, Spot pricing works with Windows, and the estimator is not in error.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: An HPC job needs the lowest-latency temporary scratch space on each VM; the data may be lost when the VM stops. Which storage should be used?
options: A standard persistent disk
A Cloud Storage bucket
Filestore
Local SSDs, which are physically attached NVMe disks offering very high IOPS with an ephemeral lifetime
explain: Local SSDs are VM-attached NVMe storage for scratch and cache with the highest throughput, but data dies with the VM. Persistent disks and Filestore persist (costing more per IOPS), while Cloud Storage is object storage with network latency.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A database workload's IOPS needs grow faster than its capacity needs, and the team wants to provision performance independently of disk size. Which disk type supports this?
options: Hyperdisk, which lets IOPS and throughput be provisioned independently of capacity
Standard persistent disk
Balanced persistent disk
A snapshot schedule
explain: Hyperdisk decouples provisioned IOPS and throughput from capacity, while pd-standard and pd-balanced tie performance to disk size. A snapshot schedule is a backup mechanism, not a performance control.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: Compliance requires GKE nodes to have no public IP addresses and the control plane to be unreachable from the internet. Which cluster configuration meets this?
options: A public cluster with a firewall rule blocking ingress
An Autopilot cluster with the public endpoint enabled
A zonal cluster with Cloud NAT
A private GKE cluster with private nodes and a private control-plane endpoint
explain: Private clusters give nodes internal-only IPs and keep the control plane off the public internet. Firewall rules on a public cluster do not remove public IPs, and Cloud NAT only provides outbound connectivity.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A team wants GKE version upgrades automated on a vetted, slightly delayed cadence — newer than Stable but not bleeding edge. Which release channel fits?
options: Rapid channel
No channel, with manual upgrades
Regular channel
Disabling node auto-upgrade entirely
explain: The Regular channel delivers recent but vetted versions with automatic upgrades — the middle cadence. Rapid tracks the newest (least vetted) versions, no channel means manual upgrade toil, and disabling auto-upgrade forfeits security patches.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A new container image deployed to GKE is crash-looping in production. What is the fastest way to return to the previous working version?
options: Delete the cluster and recreate it
Run kubectl rollout undo deployment/<name> to revert to the previous ReplicaSet
Delete the crashing pods and wait for them to recover
Scale the deployment to zero, then back up
explain: rollout undo reverts to the previous ReplicaSet immediately. Deleting pods recreates them from the same bad image, scaling to zero causes an outage, and rebuilding the cluster is drastic and slow.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A pod needs to read from a Cloud Storage bucket, but the security team forbids downloading service account keys. How should the pod authenticate?
options: Store a service account key in a Kubernetes Secret
Grant the node pool's service account the Storage Admin role
Use GKE Workload Identity to bind the pod's Kubernetes service account to a Google service account with Storage Object Viewer
Make the bucket publicly readable
explain: Workload Identity federates the Kubernetes service account to a least-privilege Google service account with no keys to leak. Keys in Secrets are the anti-pattern being avoided, broadening the node service account over-provisions every pod on the node, and public buckets expose data.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A team needs to deploy a web app packaged as a custom Docker container with its own OS dependencies, fully managed. Which App Engine environment fits?
options: Standard environment with a custom runtime
Cloud Run functions
A Compute Engine managed instance group
Flexible environment, which runs custom Docker containers on managed VMs
explain: The flexible environment supports custom runtimes via Docker images; the standard environment only offers Google's curated runtimes. A managed instance group is self-managed rather than fully managed.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A team wants to canary a new App Engine version with 5% of live traffic before a full rollout. How should they do it?
options: Use App Engine traffic splitting to send 5% of traffic to the new version
Deploy to a second project and update DNS
Create a Cloud Load Balancer in front of both versions
Stop the old version and start the new one
explain: Native traffic splitting shifts a percentage of traffic (by IP, cookie, or random) between versions with instant rollback. A second project with DNS changes is clumsy, and stopping the old version is a flag-day cutover rather than a canary.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A data pipeline step must run to completion once per night, processing a batch of files and then shutting down with nothing billed while idle. Which compute option fits best?
options: A Cloud Run service with min-instances set to 1
A Cloud Run job triggered by Cloud Scheduler, which runs to completion and scales to zero
A GKE Deployment running 24/7
An App Engine flexible service
explain: Cloud Run jobs are built for run-to-completion batch work and bill only while executing. Services with min-instances and always-on GKE or flexible deployments keep resources (and cost) alive between runs.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A Cloud Run service handles many lightweight concurrent requests, but costs are high because nearly every request seems to spawn a new instance. Which setting should be tuned?
options: Decrease the maximum instances
Enable CPU always allocated
Increase the container concurrency so each instance handles more simultaneous requests
Add a Serverless VPC Access connector
explain: Raising concurrency lets one instance serve many requests at once, cutting the instance count. Lowering max instances risks throttling under load, always-on CPU raises cost, and a VPC connector affects networking rather than scaling.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A Cloud Run service must connect to a Cloud SQL instance over its private IP address. What enables this connectivity?
