options: Assign the Cloud Run service a public IP
Cloud NAT on the Cloud Run side
Expose the Cloud SQL instance on a public IP with authorized networks
Direct VPC egress from Cloud Run into the VPC hosting the Cloud SQL private IP
explain: Direct VPC egress (or a Serverless VPC Access connector) places the service on the VPC so private IPs are reachable. Cloud Run services have no public IP to assign, and exposing the database publicly defeats the security goal.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A bucket was created in the US multi-region, but new data-residency rules require the data to live in the EU. What must be done?
options: Create a new bucket in an EU location and transfer the objects over, because bucket location is immutable
Edit the bucket's location in the console
Run gsutil mb with a location flag against the existing bucket
Change the project's default region
explain: Bucket location cannot be changed after creation, so migration means creating a new bucket and transferring objects (for example, with the Storage Transfer Service). No edit or gsutil flag rewrites an existing bucket's location.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A team stores logs in the Archive storage class and deletes them after 60 days, then notices unexpected early-deletion charges. What caused them?
options: Archive has no minimum storage duration
Retrieval fees charged for the delete operation
The bucket's location
Archive's 365-day minimum storage duration — deleting at 60 days bills the remaining time as if stored
explain: Archive enforces a 365-day minimum storage duration; early deletion is billed as though the object were stored the full term. Nearline (30 days) and Coldline (90 days) have shorter minimums, so the storage class must match the real retention period.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: An external partner without a Google account needs to download one private object, with access expiring after two hours. What is the simplest secure approach?
options: Generate a signed URL for the object with a two-hour expiration
Make the bucket public during the transfer
Grant the partner's personal email the Storage Object Viewer role
Email the object as an attachment
explain: Signed URLs grant time-limited object access to anyone holding the URL, with no Google account required. Public buckets overexpose data, IAM grants require a Google identity, and email is insecure and size-limited.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: Regulators require certain financial records in Cloud Storage to be immutable (WORM) for seven years, undeletable even by administrators. How should this be enforced?
options: Enable object versioning
Set a lifecycle rule to delete objects after seven years
Apply a retention policy and lock it, making objects immutable until the retention period expires
Store the records in two different regions
explain: A locked retention policy enforces WORM compliance: objects cannot be deleted or overwritten until expiry, even by administrators. Versioning preserves old copies but still allows deletion, and replication adds durability rather than immutability.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: Analysts query a BigQuery table filtering on event_date and grouping by user_id. The table is currently unpartitioned. What is the best optimization?
options: Partition by user_id and cluster by event_date
Partition by event_date and cluster by user_id
Create a separate dataset per month
Increase the query timeout
explain: Partition on the low-cardinality filter column (date) so queries prune whole partitions, and cluster on the high-cardinality group-by column. Partitioning by user_id would create far too many partitions, and separate datasets complicate every query.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: An analyst's ad-hoc queries occasionally scan terabytes and spike the BigQuery bill. What control caps the damage from a single query?
options: Delete the dataset after each query
Partition the tables
Set maximum bytes billed per query (or a custom cost quota) so oversized queries fail instead of running
Require queries to run at night
explain: Maximum-bytes-billed makes any query exceeding the cap fail before it incurs cost. Partitioning reduces typical scans but does not cap them, and scheduling changes when cost occurs rather than limiting it.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A company runs predictable, high-volume BigQuery workloads 24/7 and wants lower, flat-rate pricing instead of per-query charges. What should they buy?
options: More on-demand queries
A larger BigQuery dataset
BI Engine reservations
BigQuery slot reservations (committed capacity at a flat rate)
explain: Slot commitments provide dedicated query capacity at a predictable flat rate, which beats pay-per-byte pricing for steady heavy workloads. On-demand stays per-byte, and BI Engine accelerates dashboards rather than replacing slot pricing.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A Cloud SQL MySQL instance must survive a zonal outage with automatic failover and no data loss. Which configuration provides this?
options: Enable high availability, which maintains a synchronous standby in another zone with automatic failover
Create a cross-region read replica
Enable automated backups
Increase the instance's vCPUs
explain: Regional high availability keeps a synchronous standby in a second zone and fails over automatically. Read replicas require manual promotion (and can lag), backups restore to a point in time but do not fail over, and vCPUs do not affect availability.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: Security policy forbids public IP addresses on databases. A Cloud SQL instance must still be reachable from application VMs. How should connectivity be set up?
options: Assign a public IP and restrict it with authorized networks
Use private IP via private services access so the instance gets only an internal address on the VPC
Connect through Cloud NAT
Expose the instance through an external load balancer
explain: Private services access gives Cloud SQL a private VPC IP with no public exposure at all. Authorized networks still leave a public IP address, Cloud NAT is for outbound VM traffic, and a public load balancer reintroduces internet exposure.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: Payment events must be processed in order per customer, and malformed messages must not block the queue forever. Which Pub/Sub design handles both?
options: One topic per customer with no subscriptions
A push subscription with a 10-second ack deadline
An ordering key set to the customer ID, plus a dead-letter topic for repeatedly failing messages
Two identical subscriptions on the same topic
explain: Ordering keys guarantee per-key ordering, while a dead-letter topic quarantines poison messages after the maximum delivery attempts. Per-customer topics do not scale, ack deadlines do not order messages, and duplicate subscriptions double-process everything.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: The on-call team wants pages for high error rates to include a link to the incident runbook. Where should the runbook link live so it appears in every notification?
options: In the metric's labels
In a Cloud Logging sink filter
In the dashboard's JSON
In the alerting policy's documentation field, delivered through the configured notification channels
explain: The documentation field supports Markdown links and is included in alert notifications. Metric labels and sink filters never surface in pages, and dashboards are separate from the alerting path.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: An uptime check reports a checkout endpoint as healthy because it returns HTTP 200, but the page actually shows an error message. How should the check be improved?
options: Add response content matching so the check requires expected text in the body
Switch the check from HTTPS to TCP
Increase the check frequency
Replace the uptime check with a log-based metric
explain: Content matching validates the response body, catching soft errors that still return HTTP 200. A TCP check validates less, higher frequency does not detect bad content, and log-based metrics cannot probe an endpoint.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A service has a 99.9% availability SLO. The team wants to be alerted quickly when errors burn through the error budget much faster than allowed. Which alert type fits?
options: An uptime check on the homepage
An SLO burn-rate alerting policy, which fires when the error budget is consumed too fast
A billing budget alert
A log-based metric without an alerting policy
explain: Burn-rate alerts detect rapid error-budget consumption inside the SLO window — the standard SRE approach. Uptime checks monitor a single endpoint, billing budgets track spend, and a metric without an alerting policy notifies no one.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A new log sink routing to BigQuery was created an hour ago, but no rows are arriving in the dataset. The filter matches recent logs. What is the most likely cause?
options: BigQuery datasets cannot receive log sinks
The sink needs 24 hours before first delivery
The sink's writer identity lacks permission to write to the dataset (for example, BigQuery Data Editor)
Log sinks only work with Cloud Storage destinations
explain: Every sink gets a unique writer identity that must be granted write permission on the destination; without it, exports silently fail. Sinks deliver within minutes, and BigQuery is a first-class sink destination.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: Compliance requires application logs to be retained for one year in tamper-proof storage. The default bucket keeps 30 days. What should be configured?
options: Increase the _Default bucket to 365 days without locking it
Create a custom log bucket with a 365-day retention and lock it to prevent deletion or reduction
Export the logs to a spreadsheet monthly
Rely on the _Required bucket
explain: Custom log buckets support long retentions, and locking makes the retention tamper-proof. An unlocked bucket's retention could later be shortened, and the _Required bucket holds only Admin Activity and System Event logs.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: After a data incident, the team must determine who ran queries against a BigQuery dataset last week. Which logs contain this, and what must be true?
options: Admin Activity logs, which are always enabled
Cloud Trace spans
VPC Flow Logs
Data Access audit logs for BigQuery, which must be explicitly enabled since they are off by default
explain: Data reads and writes are recorded in Data Access audit logs — but these are disabled by default because of their volume and cost, so they must be enabled proactively. Admin Activity covers configuration changes, not queries.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: Exceptions are scattered across dozens of microservice logs, and the team needs a ranked list of the most frequent crashes. Which tool aggregates this automatically?
options: Error Reporting, which groups exceptions from logs into error groups with counts
Cloud Profiler
Cloud Trace
The Metrics Explorer
explain: Error Reporting parses exceptions from Cloud Logging and groups identical errors with occurrence counts and first/last-seen times. Profiler samples CPU usage, Trace follows request latency, and Metrics Explorer charts numeric metrics.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A service's p99 latency doubled after a deploy, and engineers suspect one function is now CPU-bound. Which tool shows where CPU time is spent as a flame graph?
options: Cloud Trace
Cloud Profiler, which continuously profiles production code with minimal overhead
Cloud Logging
Uptime checks
explain: Cloud Profiler captures CPU and heap profiles rendered as flame graphs, pinpointing hot functions in production. Trace shows request latency across services rather than in-process CPU, and logs and uptime checks do not profile code.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: An engineer runs gcloud compute instances set-machine-type on a running VM and gets an error. What is the required step?
options: Stop the VM first; the machine type can only be changed while the instance is stopped
Create a snapshot first
Delete the boot disk
Enable OS Login
explain: Changing the machine type requires the instance to be stopped (TERMINATED state). A snapshot backs up data but does not unblock the operation, and deleting the boot disk destroys the VM.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A database VM needs scheduled disk snapshots that quiesce the filesystem so backups are application-consistent. Which feature provides this?
options: A standard snapshot schedule
A Cloud Storage lifecycle rule
Manual snapshots from the console
A snapshot schedule with guest flush enabled, which pauses I/O during snapshot creation
explain: Guest flush quiesces the filesystem (VSS on Windows, fsfreeze on Linux) for application-consistent snapshots. Standard schedules are crash-consistent only, and lifecycle rules manage object storage rather than disks.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A managed instance group runs long batch jobs that must not be restarted unexpectedly. The team needs to roll out a new instance template without auto-restarting running instances. Which update type should they use?
options: Proactive, the default
Delete the MIG and recreate it
Opportunistic, so instances only pick up the new template when they are next recreated for another reason
A rolling update with maxSurge set to 100%
explain: Opportunistic updates defer the template rollout until instances are naturally recreated, avoiding surprise restarts. Proactive updates replace instances during the rollout, and maxSurge only controls extra capacity during proactive updates.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: After a zonal outage, a regional MIG has most instances concentrated in the two surviving zones. How does the group return to an even spread once the zone recovers?
options: Manually delete and recreate instances in the recovered zone
Proactive instance redistribution, which automatically rebalances instances across zones
Convert the MIG to single-zone
Disable autoscaling
explain: Regional MIGs rebalance instances across zones automatically through proactive instance redistribution. Manual recreation is operational toil, single-zone reduces resilience, and autoscaling is unrelated to zone spread.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A company has a change freeze every December and must guarantee no GKE node auto-upgrades occur that month. What should they configure?
options: Delete the node pools in December
Disable node auto-upgrade permanently
A maintenance exclusion window covering December
Move the cluster to a different region
explain: Maintenance exclusions block upgrades during specified windows while keeping auto-upgrade (and its security patches) active the rest of the year. Permanently disabling auto-upgrade forfeits patches, and deleting node pools destroys capacity.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: Before performing host maintenance on a GKE node, an administrator must evict its pods gracefully so workloads reschedule elsewhere. Which command does this?
options: kubectl delete node
kubectl cordon
kubectl scale deployment to zero
kubectl drain, which cordons the node and evicts pods respecting PodDisruptionBudgets
explain: kubectl drain evicts pods gracefully — honoring PodDisruptionBudgets — so they reschedule elsewhere. kubectl cordon only prevents new scheduling without moving existing pods, and deleting the node object does not evict anything.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: During a disaster-recovery drill, the team must verify that a regional Cloud SQL instance fails over to its standby. Which command triggers the failover?
options: gcloud sql instances failover INSTANCE_NAME
gcloud sql instances promote-replica
gcloud sql instances restart
gcloud compute instances reset
explain: gcloud sql instances failover initiates a manual failover to the high-availability standby. Promote-replica is for read-replica topologies, and restart merely reboots the current primary.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: The team wants every git tag push (like v1.2.0) to automatically build and push a release container image. How should the Cloud Build trigger be configured?
options: A manual-only trigger invoked from the console
A trigger with a tag regex (for example, v.*) so tag pushes start builds automatically
A Cloud Scheduler job that polls the repository
A trigger on every pull request
explain: Tag-based triggers fire on matching tag pushes — the standard release-automation pattern. Manual triggers do not automate anything, Scheduler polling is redundant, and pull-request triggers build unreleased code.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: One cloudbuild.yaml must build images for dev, staging, and prod with different image tags and cluster names. How should the variable parts be handled?
options: Maintain three separate YAML files
Hardcode the prod values and edit them per environment
Store the values in the Dockerfile
Use user-defined substitutions (for example, $_ENV) passed at build or trigger time
explain: User-defined substitutions parameterize build configs so a single file serves every environment. Separate files drift out of sync, hardcoding invites mistakes, and Dockerfiles do not receive build trigger values.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: An engineer is about to update a Deployment Manager deployment that manages production networking and wants to review the planned changes before applying them. What should they do?
options: Run the update with --preview to inspect the proposed changes without applying them
Apply the update and roll back if something breaks
Delete the deployment and recreate it
Edit the YAML and trust the diff is correct
explain: The --preview flag renders the planned changes for review before anything is applied. Applying blind risks production networking, and delete/recreate causes an outage.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: Cloud spend jumped 40% this month with no new projects. Where should the team look first for waste like idle or oversized VMs?
options: Cloud Trace
Recommender's cost recommendations (idle VM, machine-type rightsizing, idle persistent disks)
VPC Flow Logs
The Cloud DNS dashboard
explain: Recommender surfaces idle VMs, overprovisioned machine types, and idle disks with projected savings. Trace analyzes latency, while Flow Logs and DNS show network data rather than waste.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A nightly report job must call an authenticated Cloud Run service over HTTPS at 2 AM. Which scheduler setup handles authentication?
options: A Cloud Scheduler HTTP target with no auth, and make the service public
A cron job on a VM with curl
A Cloud Scheduler job with an HTTP target using OIDC token authentication against the service's URL
A Pub/Sub topic with no subscription
explain: Cloud Scheduler supports OIDC (or OAuth) tokens on HTTP targets, letting it invoke authenticated services directly. Making the service public for a cron job is insecure, and a VM cron adds management overhead.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: An SRE wants to tail recent error logs for a Cloud Run service from a deployment script. Which command queries Cloud Logging from the CLI?
options: gsutil cat
A bq query against the _Default bucket
kubectl logs
gcloud logging read with a filter on resource type, service name, and severity
explain: gcloud logging read queries log entries with filters and is fully scriptable. gsutil reads storage objects, the log bucket is not a BigQuery table, and kubectl logs only works for GKE pods.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: SSH is blocked by a firewall misconfiguration and the team needs an interactive shell on the VM to fix it. Serial console credentials were never configured. What is the path forward?
options: Wait for SSH to start working on its own
Set up serial console access first (for example, via a startup script that configures a user), then connect with gcloud compute connect-to-serial-port
Assign a second external IP to bypass the firewall
Enable Cloud NAT
explain: The interactive serial console requires OS-level credentials configured in advance — a startup script can set them — and then connect-to-serial-port bypasses SSH entirely. A new external IP hits the same firewall rule, and Cloud NAT does not help inbound SSH.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A platform team built a useful Cloud Monitoring dashboard and must replicate it across 30 projects. What is the most reliable method?
options: Export the dashboard JSON and import it into each project
Recreate it by hand in each project
Take screenshots and share them
Copy the alerting policy instead
explain: Dashboards are JSON documents, so export/import reproduces them exactly and can be scripted. Manual recreation drifts between projects, screenshots are not functional, and alerting policies are a different resource.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: An alerting policy is configured and firing, but no emails arrive. The notification channel shows as unverified. What is the fix?
options: Increase the alert threshold
Recreate the entire monitoring workspace
Complete the channel verification (click the verification link sent to the address)
Delete and recreate the alerting policy
explain: Email and several other channel types stay dormant until verified, so notifications never leave. Threshold changes and policy recreation do not address an unverified channel.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: API calls from an application are intermittently rejected with 403 rate-limit errors. The team needs to see per-API traffic, error rates, and quota consumption in one place. Where should they look?
options: Cloud Trace
The billing export
VPC Flow Logs
The APIs & Services dashboard, which shows traffic, errors, and quota metrics per API
explain: The API dashboard graphs requests, error ratios, and quota usage for each enabled API. Trace follows request latency, billing shows cost, and Flow Logs show packets — none of them show API quota consumption.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A contractor must read only objects under gs://reports/contractor-acme/ in a shared bucket. What is the cleanest way to scope this?
options: Grant Storage Object Viewer with an IAM Condition restricting resource.name to the contractor's prefix
Make the whole bucket public
Create a separate bucket per contractor
Set object ACLs one by one as files arrive
explain: An IAM Condition on resource.name enforces prefix-scoped access in a single binding — scalable and auditable. Per-object ACLs do not scale as files arrive, separate buckets multiply management overhead, and public buckets expose everything.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A deny policy blocks storage.buckets.delete for all principals to protect backups. The break-glass admin group must retain the ability to delete. How should the policy handle this?
options: Deny policies cannot have exceptions, so remove the deny
Grant the break-glass group the Owner role
Add a deny exception for the break-glass group in the deny rule
Put the break-glass group in a different organization
explain: Deny rules support exception principals, preserving the blanket protection while keeping emergency access. Granting Owner does not help because deny policies override any allow, and another organization does not change the bucket's policy.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A user reports 'permission denied' accessing a BigQuery dataset, but their role looks correct. Which tool explains exactly which policy statement allowed or denied the call?
options: Cloud Trace
The billing export
VPC Flow Logs
The IAM Policy Troubleshooter, which evaluates the effective policy for a principal, resource, and permission
explain: The Policy Troubleshooter simulates the access check against allow and deny policies and identifies the deciding binding. Audit logs record that a denial happened but not the policy evaluation behind it.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A developer debugging locally needs to briefly act as a production service account without downloading its key. What is the secure approach?
options: Download the key and delete it after debugging
Use service account impersonation (gcloud --impersonate-service-account) after being granted Service Account Token Creator on it
Grant the developer the service account's roles permanently
Share the key over chat and rotate it later
explain: Impersonation mints short-lived tokens with no key material to leak or forget. Even temporary key downloads create exposure windows, and permanent role grants violate least privilege.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A GitHub Actions workflow must deploy to Cloud Run. The security team prohibits storing long-lived service account keys in GitHub Secrets. How should the workflow authenticate?
options: Store a service account key in GitHub Secrets anyway
Use a developer's personal credentials in the workflow
Configure Workload Identity Federation with an OIDC identity pool trusting GitHub Actions, exchanging short-lived tokens
Make the Cloud Run service publicly deployable
explain: Workload Identity Federation lets GitHub's OIDC tokens exchange for short-lived Google Cloud credentials with nothing stored. Keys in Secrets are exactly the anti-pattern being banned, and personal credentials in CI are unauditable.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: After adding a deny-all ingress firewall rule, administrators can no longer SSH via IAP TCP forwarding. Which firewall rule restores IAP access without opening SSH to the internet?
options: Allow tcp:22 from 35.235.240.0/20, the IAP TCP-forwarding source range
Allow tcp:22 from 0.0.0.0/0
Assign public IPs to all VMs
Delete the deny-all rule
explain: IAP tunnels originate from 35.235.240.0/20, so allowing that range restores IAP SSH while keeping the deny-all posture for everything else. Opening 0.0.0.0/0 exposes SSH globally, and public IPs defeat the private design.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: The company wants SSH access to VMs to require phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication tied to IAM identities. Which setup delivers this?
options: Project-wide SSH keys in instance metadata
OS Login with 2-step verification enforcement for SSH connections
A shared SSH key rotated monthly
Cloud VPN
explain: OS Login binds SSH to IAM identities and can require 2-step verification, giving per-user MFA. Static metadata keys and shared keys lack per-user MFA entirely, and VPN provides network access rather than SSH authentication.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: PCI compliance requires the encryption keys protecting cardholder data in Cloud Storage to be rotated at least every 90 days, under the company's control. Which approach meets this?
options: Google-managed encryption keys
TLS on all client connections
Customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) in Cloud KMS with a 90-day rotation schedule
A VPC firewall rule
explain: CMEK with a rotation schedule gives customer-controlled, automatic key rotation for data at rest. Google-managed keys rotate but are not customer-controlled, and TLS protects data in transit rather than stored objects.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: Creating a CMEK-encrypted persistent disk fails with a KMS permission error. The user already has Compute Admin. What is missing?
options: The user needs the Owner role
The KMS API must be disabled and re-enabled
The disk must be created in the same zone as the key ring
The Compute Engine service agent needs the Cloud KMS CryptoKey Encrypter/Decrypter role on the key
explain: Google's Compute Engine service agent performs the actual encryption, so it needs encrypter/decrypter on the key — the user's own roles do not cover it. Owner grants the user more power but grants the service agent nothing.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A database password stored in Secret Manager must rotate automatically every 30 days and notify the application. How should this be set up?
options: Configure Secret Manager rotation on a 30-day schedule, which can publish to Pub/Sub to trigger an application reload
Have an engineer manually create a new secret version monthly
Store the password in an environment variable instead
Rotate by deleting and recreating the secret
explain: Rotation schedules automate new secret versions on a cadence, with Pub/Sub notifications so consumers reload. Manual rotation is toil that gets skipped, and environment variables are neither rotatable nor audited.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A policy requires that only container images signed by the security team can be deployed to production GKE clusters. What enforces this at deploy time?
options: Vulnerability scanning in Artifact Registry
Binary Authorization with an attestations-required policy on the cluster
An IAM policy on the cluster
A Kubernetes NetworkPolicy
explain: Binary Authorization blocks deployment of images lacking the required attestations — genuine deploy-time enforcement. Scanning is advisory only, IAM controls who may deploy rather than what may deploy, and NetworkPolicy controls traffic.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: The security team wants a VPC Service Controls perimeter around production, but fears breaking legitimate data flows. How can they preview the impact before enforcing?
options: Enforce immediately and roll back if alerts fire
Create the perimeter in a separate organization
Use dry-run mode, which logs would-be violations without blocking traffic
Skip the perimeter and rely on firewall rules
explain: Dry-run mode evaluates the policies and logs violations without enforcement, letting teams fix legitimate flows first. Enforcing blind risks production outages, and a separate organization does not preview this environment's traffic.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A VPC Service Controls perimeter protects analytics projects. One trusted data-science project outside the perimeter needs read access to a BigQuery dataset inside. What is the right mechanism?
options: Dissolve the perimeter
Move the dataset outside the perimeter
Make the dataset public
Add an egress rule on the perimeter and a matching ingress rule allowing that project's access
explain: Ingress and egress rules carve precise, audited exceptions across the perimeter boundary. Dissolving the perimeter or moving data destroys the security model, and public datasets abandon access control.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: Leadership wants to guarantee that no one can grant access to personal Gmail accounts on company cloud resources. Which control enforces this organization-wide?
options: An IAM deny policy listing every Gmail address
The organization policy constraint iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains (domain restricted sharing)
Deleting all existing IAM bindings
A billing budget
explain: Domain restricted sharing constrains which identity domains may appear in IAM policies — the centralized, scalable answer. Enumerating addresses in a deny policy never scales, and deleting bindings breaks legitimate access.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: The security team must receive Google Cloud notifications about security advisories and compliance issues for each project. How should contacts be designated?
options: Add the team to every project's IAM policy as Viewers
Create a billing budget per project
Configure Essential Contacts on projects and folders with the security category
Subscribe personal emails to a newsletter
explain: Essential Contacts designate who receives categorized Google notifications (security, technical, billing) per resource. The Viewer role grants access but does not route notifications, and budgets track spend.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: Before migrating a BigQuery dataset to a shared analytics project, the team must find any columns containing national ID numbers. Which service scans for PII patterns?
options: Cloud Trace
Manual SELECT * queries
Security Command Center
Cloud DLP inspection using built-in infoTypes for government IDs
explain: Cloud DLP inspection scans structured data for infoTypes such as government IDs, emails, and credit cards, reporting findings per column. Manual queries do not scale, and Security Command Center finds misconfigurations rather than PII content.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: Analysts need realistic data for testing, but raw customer emails must never leave the secure project. How can the team share a safe copy?
options: Use Cloud DLP de-identification (for example, masking or tokenization) to transform PII before sharing
Copy the raw tables and trust the analysts
Delete the email column entirely
Export to CSV and email it
explain: De-identification preserves data utility such as format and joinability while removing PII — masking and tokenization are the standard techniques. Raw copies violate policy, deleting columns may break tests, and CSV over email is uncontrolled exfiltration.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A weekly review must surface misconfigurations like publicly accessible buckets and overly broad firewall rules across all projects. Which service centralizes these findings?
options: Cloud Monitoring
Security Command Center, whose Security Health Analytics detectors flag misconfigurations
Cloud Trace
The Pricing Calculator
explain: Security Command Center aggregates security findings, including Security Health Analytics misconfiguration detectors, across the organization. Cloud Monitoring tracks metrics rather than security posture.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A regulated customer requires explicit human approval before Google support personnel can access their data during a support case. Which feature provides this gate?
options: Access Transparency
VPC Service Controls
Access Approval, which holds support access until a designated approver consents
An IAM deny policy
explain: Access Approval intercepts Google administrator access requests and requires customer approval with a justification. Access Transparency only logs access after the fact, and neither VPC Service Controls nor IAM policies govern Google personnel.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A bucket still uses fine-grained access with legacy object ACLs, causing inconsistent permissions that IAM audits cannot see. What is the recommended fix?
options: Add more object ACLs
Make the bucket public for consistency
Grant Storage Admin to everyone who needs access
Enable uniform bucket-level access (and enforce it with the storage.uniformBucketLevelAccess org policy) so IAM is the single access control
explain: Uniform bucket-level access disables object ACLs, making IAM the sole auditable control plane. More ACLs deepen the inconsistency, while public buckets and broad Admin grants move in the wrong direction.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: After a leaked service account key incident, leadership wants to prevent anyone in the organization from creating new user-managed service account keys. Which control does this?
options: An IAM deny policy on iam.serviceAccounts
Deleting all service accounts
The boolean organization policy constraint iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation
Rotating keys more often
explain: The boolean constraint blocks user-managed key creation hierarchy-wide — the purpose-built preventive control. Deleting service accounts breaks workloads, and rotation does not prevent new keys from being created.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: The security team needs a baseline 'deny all high-risk ports' rule that no project administrator can override with a more permissive VPC firewall rule. Where should this live?
options: A VPC firewall rule with priority 0
A hierarchical firewall policy at the organization or folder level, which is evaluated before VPC firewall rules
An IAM policy
A Cloud Armor policy
explain: Hierarchical firewall policies are evaluated before VPC-level rules, so an organization-level deny cannot be overridden by project administrators. A priority-0 VPC rule still lives under project control, and IAM and Cloud Armor do not filter VM traffic.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A regulated workload must protect data while it is being processed — encrypted in memory so even the hypervisor host cannot read it. Which technology provides this?
options: CMEK for persistent disks
TLS 1.3 between services
Shielded VMs
Confidential VMs with memory encryption (AMD SEV-SNP), protecting data in use
explain: Confidential Computing encrypts VM memory so data stays protected during processing. CMEK covers data at rest, TLS covers data in transit, and Shielded VMs verify boot integrity — none of them encrypt in-use memory.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: An on-premises application must reach a partner's managed database service on Google Cloud over private connectivity, without the partner peering VPCs. Which service enables this?
options: Private Service Connect, exposing the service through a private endpoint with an internal IP
VPC peering initiated by the customer
A public IP allowlist on the database
Cloud DNS forwarding
explain: Private Service Connect publishes a managed service as a private endpoint consumable across VPC and organization boundaries without peering. Peering requires both sides' cooperation and has transitivity limits, while public allowlists expose the service.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: Auditors need a tamper-proof record of every IAM policy change over the past year. The default log bucket only keeps 30 days. What preserves this history?
options: Route Admin Activity audit logs to a locked custom log bucket with a one-year (or longer) retention
Enable Data Access audit logs only
Export the IAM policy to a spreadsheet monthly
Rely on Cloud Trace
explain: Admin Activity logs record every IAM policy change; routing them to a locked custom bucket retains them immutably well beyond 30 days. Data Access logs cover data reads rather than policy changes, and spreadsheets are neither automatic nor tamper-proof.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A large enterprise needs monthly invoicing with net payment terms instead of automatic credit card charges for its Google Cloud usage. Which billing account type do they need?
options: A standard self-serve online billing account, which supports invoicing by default
An invoiced (offline) billing account, which provides monthly invoicing and requires Google approval
A prepaid credits account purchased at a retail store
A second Google payments profile, which changes the invoicing terms automatically
explain: Invoiced (offline) billing accounts support monthly invoicing with payment terms, but they must be approved by Google. Self-serve online accounts charge a card or bank account automatically, and payments profiles alone do not change billing terms.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A team starts the Google Cloud Free Trial to evaluate the platform. Which statement about the trial credits is correct?
options: The credits never expire and can be used indefinitely
The credits cover any Google service including premium support plans
The trial converts to a paid account automatically with no action needed
The credits expire after 90 days, and the account must be upgraded to a paid billing account to keep resources running
explain: Free Trial credits expire after 90 days; upgrading to a paid billing account is a manual step required to continue. The trial does not auto-convert, and credits cannot be applied to everything such as support plans.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: Finance wants a budget alert that tracks only BigQuery spend in the production project, ignoring all other services and projects. How should the budget be configured?
options: Create a separate billing account just for BigQuery
Apply budget filters for the BigQuery service and the production project so only matching spend is tracked
Create two budgets, one per requirement, and subtract them
Add a label to every query and filter billing reports instead of using a budget
explain: Budgets support filters on projects, services, labels, and credit treatment, so one budget can isolate BigQuery spend in prod. A separate billing account fragments invoicing unnecessarily, and labels alone produce reports rather than alerts.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: The team wants non-production VMs automatically stopped when monthly spend reaches 100% of budget. Budgets only send alerts, so what architecture enables the automatic response?
options: Configure the budget to publish to Pub/Sub at the 100% threshold, and have a Cloud Function subscribed to that topic stop the VMs
Check the budget's built-in auto-shutdown option
Set an organization policy that disables Compute Engine at a spend limit
Export billing to BigQuery and run a daily manual review
explain: Budgets can publish threshold alerts to Pub/Sub, and a subscribed function can take programmatic action such as stopping VMs. There is no native auto-shutdown checkbox in budgets, and organization policies cannot constrain spend.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: Finance builds a dashboard on the BigQuery billing export expecting intraday spend updates, but the data is only current through yesterday. What explains this?
options: The billing export is broken and must be recreated
Billing exports are generated once per day, so they do not provide real-time spend data
The dataset needs the premium BigQuery edition for intraday freshness
The export only works when the dataset is in the US multi-region
explain: The billing export loads data daily, so same-day spend is not visible in it. The export is not broken, no premium edition changes the cadence, and dataset location does not affect freshness.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A security review wants unused APIs disabled to reduce attack surface. Which gcloud command disables the Dataproc API in the current project?
options: gcloud services delete dataproc.googleapis.com
gcloud api remove dataproc
gcloud services disable dataproc.googleapis.com
gcloud projects delete --api=dataproc
explain: gcloud services disable turns off an API in the project. There is no services delete or api remove command, and deleting the project is wildly disproportionate.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An engineer enables the Kubernetes Engine API, and notices the Compute Engine API becomes enabled automatically at the same time. Why?
options: This is a console bug; the APIs are unrelated
GKE declares Compute Engine as a dependency, and enabling an API automatically enables its dependencies
The billing account requires both APIs together
An organization policy forces both APIs on
explain: Google Cloud APIs declare dependencies, and enabling a service auto-enables the services it depends on. It is not a bug, and neither billing nor organization policy causes this behavior.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An architect needs the list of zones available in europe-west1 before placing resources. Which command provides this?
options: gcloud compute regions describe europe-west1
gcloud zones list --all
gcloud compute list-zones europe-west1
gsutil ls -L europe-west1
explain: gcloud compute regions describe returns the region's metadata including its zones. The other commands do not exist in that form, and gsutil manages Cloud Storage rather than Compute Engine geography.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A deployment fails on the in-use IP address quota in us-central1, while europe-west1 shows plenty of headroom. What does this imply about the quota?
options: IP address quotas are global, so this result is impossible
The billing account is exhausted
In-use IP address quotas are tracked per region, so the team can deploy in europe-west1 or request an increase for us-central1
The VPC firewall is blocking the quota
explain: Many Compute Engine quotas, including in-use IP addresses, are enforced per region, so headroom in one region does not help another. Billing and firewall rules do not produce quota errors.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An automation script applies 70 labels to a VM and the API rejects the request. What is the cause?
options: Labels incur a charge after the first ten
A single resource can carry at most 64 labels
Labels require the Owner role to apply
Compute Engine VMs do not support labels
explain: Google Cloud enforces a limit of 64 labels per resource. Labels are free, do not require Owner, and are fully supported on VMs.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A feature announced last week is missing from the engineer's local gcloud installation. What is the correct fix?
options: Run gcloud components update to pull the latest SDK components
Reinstall the operating system
Run gcloud init again
Wait for the feature to be backported automatically
explain: gcloud components update refreshes the SDK to the latest release, which includes newly launched features. gcloud init only reconfigures authentication and defaults, and nothing auto-updates the local install.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An engineer authenticated gcloud on a shared workstation and wants to remove their credentials from that machine afterward. Which command does this?
options: gcloud auth revoke to remove the stored credentials
gcloud auth login with a different account
Deleting the current project
gcloud config set project to a dummy value
explain: gcloud auth revoke deletes the local credential for an account. Logging in as someone else leaves the original credential behind, and project or config changes do not remove credentials.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: The finance team must receive Google Cloud notifications about payment failures and invoice issues. How should they be designated?
options: Grant every finance member the Billing Account Administrator role
Create a billing budget for the finance team
Open a support ticket for each notification
Configure Essential Contacts with the billing notification category on the relevant projects or folders
explain: Essential Contacts route categorized Google notifications (billing, security, technical) to the right people without granting IAM roles. The Administrator role grants far more power than receiving notifications requires.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A company is building an internal cost estimator and needs programmatic access to SKU-level pricing for Google Cloud services. Which API provides this?
options: The Cloud Logging API
The Recommender API
The Cloud Billing Catalog API
The IAM API
explain: The Cloud Billing Catalog API returns the public price list of SKUs for programmatic use. The Logging API serves logs, Recommender serves optimization suggestions, and IAM serves access management -- none publish pricing.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A small company has one organization and five projects. Is creating folders mandatory?
options: Yes, every project must live inside a folder
Yes, folders are required before billing can be enabled
Yes, IAM policies cannot be attached without folders
No, projects can sit directly under the organization; folders are optional groupings for IAM and policy management
explain: Folders are optional: projects may be created directly under the organization node. Folders become valuable for grouping IAM and organization policies, but nothing requires them.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: Which gcloud command grants user Priya the Storage Object Viewer role on project analytics-prod?
options: gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding analytics-prod --member=user:priya@example.com --role=roles/storage.objectViewer
gcloud iam grant priya@example.com storage.viewer
gsutil iam ch user:priya@example.com:objectViewer gs://analytics-prod
gcloud projects update analytics-prod --add-user=priya@example.com
explain: add-iam-policy-binding adds a member-to-role binding on the project with the correct member and role syntax. The other commands are invented, and gsutil iam ch targets buckets rather than projects.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An administrator adds an IAM Condition to a role binding via the API, but the call is rejected until the policy version is changed. Which policy version supports conditional bindings?
options: Version 1
Version 3
Version 2
Policy versions do not affect conditions
explain: IAM Conditions require allow-policy version 3; versions 1 and 2 cannot carry conditions. The version must be set explicitly when managing policies through the API.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A proposed organization policy might break existing deployments. The team wants to see what would violate it before enforcing anything. What should they use?
options: Enforce the policy immediately and roll back if alerts fire
Delete the deployments first
Dry-run mode, which logs would-be violations without blocking any operation
Cloud Audit Logs alone
explain: Organization policies support dry-run mode, which evaluates the constraint and logs violations without enforcement. Enforcing blind risks outages, and audit logs only record what already happened.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A billing budget keeps alerting early because promotional credits are counted as spend. How can the budget ignore credits?
options: Set the budget's credit treatment to exclude credits, promotions, and discounts
Create a new billing account without credits
Delete the promotional credits
Lower the budget threshold to compensate
explain: Budgets have a credit-treatment setting controlling whether credits, promotions, and discounts count toward the threshold. A new billing account or deleting credits is unnecessary, and lowering the threshold works around rather than fixes the accounting.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: Finance needs per-VM cost breakdowns, but the BigQuery billing export only shows SKU-level totals. What is missing?
options: Nothing; the export cannot break costs down further
The detailed usage cost export, which adds resource-level fields such as the specific VM or disk behind each charge
A Cloud Logging sink
The Pricing Calculator
explain: Google Cloud offers two BigQuery exports: the standard usage-cost export (SKU granularity) and the detailed export (resource-level granularity). Enabling the detailed export provides the per-resource fields finance needs.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A script calls Google Cloud REST APIs directly and needs a short-lived OAuth token for the Authorization header. Which command mints one for the active account?
options: gcloud auth login
gsutil token create
gcloud iam service-accounts keys create
gcloud auth print-access-token
explain: gcloud auth print-access-token outputs a short-lived access token for the active credential. gcloud auth login performs interactive authentication rather than minting a token, and creating a service account key is the long-lived pattern to avoid.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: Cloud spend spiked this week and the team suspects one expensive SKU. In the console, where can they break the spike down by individual SKU?
options: Cloud Trace
VPC Flow Logs
Billing reports, grouped and filtered by SKU
The Cloud DNS dashboard
explain: Billing reports can group and filter cost by service, project, label, and SKU, pinpointing the expensive SKU. Trace, Flow Logs, and DNS contain no cost data.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A partner needs to create new billing accounts for each client engagement under the reseller arrangement. Which IAM role grants the ability to create billing accounts?
options: Project Owner
Billing Account User
Billing Account Viewer
Billing Account Creator
explain: Billing Account Creator grants the right to create new billing accounts (and become their administrator). Billing Account User can only link projects to existing accounts, and Viewer is read-only.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An engineer wants to inspect every property of the currently active gcloud configuration (account, project, region, zone). Which command shows this?
options: gcloud auth list
gcloud info --short
gcloud projects list
gcloud config list
explain: gcloud config list displays all properties of the active configuration. gcloud auth list shows signed-in accounts rather than configuration properties, and projects list enumerates projects.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A project with running production VMs is moved from one billing account to another. What happens to the running workloads?
options: Nothing; the workloads keep running and subsequent charges accrue to the new billing account
The VMs are stopped until the new billing account is verified
The VMs are deleted and must be recreated
All workloads experience a 24-hour billing interruption
explain: Changing a project's billing account does not disturb running resources; charges simply flow to the new account afterward. Stopping or deleting workloads is not part of the move.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A batch job runs for 30 hours, can tolerate being preempted, and must be as cheap as possible. Which statement about Spot VMs is true for this workload?
options: Spot VMs have no maximum lifetime, so the 30-hour job can run on them (unlike legacy preemptible VMs, which were capped at 24 hours)
Spot VMs are guaranteed to run for a full 24 hours before preemption
Spot VMs cannot be preempted once they start running
Spot VM pricing is fixed and identical to on-demand pricing
explain: Spot VMs carry no maximum lifetime, removing the old 24-hour preemptible cap, which suits long interruptible jobs. They can still be preempted at any time with short notice, and their pricing is discounted relative to on-demand.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: An engineer stops a VM for the weekend to save money, but Monday's bill still shows charges for it. What is the most likely explanation?
options: Stopped VMs are billed at the full running rate
Persistent disks attached to a stopped VM continue to accrue storage charges until they are deleted
Billing data is delayed by a week
The project must be deleted to stop all charges
explain: Stopping a VM halts compute charges, but attached persistent disks keep billing for provisioned storage. Deleting the disks (after snapshotting anything needed) is what removes the remaining cost.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A stateful application runs in a managed instance group, and each instance must keep its data disk and internal IP address when autohealing recreates it. What should be configured?
options: A standard regional MIG
An unmanaged instance group
A stateful MIG with stateful persistent disks and stateful internal IPs
A larger boot disk on the instance template
explain: Stateful MIGs preserve designated disks, IPs, and metadata across instance recreations, which is exactly what a stateful workload needs. Standard MIGs treat instances as disposable, and unmanaged groups provide no autohealing at all.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A GKE node starts failing its health checks repeatedly. Which feature automatically detects this and recreates the node?
options: The cluster autoscaler
Manual node pool resizing
The horizontal pod autoscaler
Node auto-repair, which monitors node health and recreates unhealthy nodes
explain: Node auto-repair watches node health and replaces nodes that stay unhealthy. The cluster autoscaler adjusts node count based on pending pods, and the horizontal pod autoscaler scales pods rather than repairing nodes.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: New pods stay in Pending state with events reporting insufficient CPU on every node. Which component adds nodes to schedule them?
options: The cluster autoscaler, which grows node pools when pods cannot be scheduled
The horizontal pod autoscaler
The vertical pod autoscaler
Node auto-repair
explain: The cluster autoscaler adds nodes when pods are unschedulable due to resource constraints. HPA and VPA adjust pod counts and pod resource requests respectively, while auto-repair only replaces broken nodes.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: An engineer tries to edit an environment variable on an already-deployed Cloud Run revision directly. What happens?
options: The change applies immediately to the running revision
Revisions are immutable, so the change creates a new revision that can then receive traffic
The service is deleted
Traffic automatically shifts to the edited revision
explain: Cloud Run revisions are immutable snapshots; any configuration change produces a new revision. Traffic only moves when you explicitly shift it, and nothing is deleted by editing.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A public API runs on Cloud Run and must accept requests without any authentication. What is the correct IAM configuration?
options: Make the entire project public
Remove all IAM policies from the service
Grant the Cloud Run Invoker role to allUsers on the service
Put Cloud Armor in front and disable IAM
explain: Granting roles/run.invoker to allUsers allows unauthenticated invocation of that service only. Making the project public or removing policies exposes far more than intended, and Cloud Armor does not replace IAM authentication.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A Cloud Run service needs a database password at runtime, but the password must not be baked into the container image. What is the best approach?
options: Set the password as an ENV in the Dockerfile
Hardcode it in the application source
Store it in a Cloud Storage object readable by everyone
Reference the password from Secret Manager as an environment variable or mounted volume
explain: Cloud Run integrates with Secret Manager to inject secrets as environment variables or files without embedding them in the image. Dockerfile ENV values and hardcoded secrets leak into image layers, and a world-readable bucket exposes the secret.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: An App Engine app.yaml file sets service: billing. What does deploying it create?
options: A separate billing service running alongside the default service in the same application
A renamed project
A new Google Cloud project
A new version of the default service
explain: The service field in app.yaml defines a separate App Engine service (microservice) within the same application, each with its own versions and scaling. It does not rename or create projects, and it is not merely a version.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A legacy App Engine application keeps session state in instance memory, so instances must stay running continuously under operator control. Which scaling type fits?
options: Automatic scaling
Manual scaling, where the operator sets the instance count and instances run until explicitly changed
Basic scaling
Cloud Run functions
explain: Manual scaling keeps a fixed number of instances running continuously, preserving in-memory state. Automatic and basic scaling create and destroy instances dynamically, which would wipe the sessions.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A company needs object storage that survives a full regional outage with synchronous writes to two regions and fast failover. Which bucket location type fits?
options: A single-region bucket
A multi-region bucket
A dual-region bucket
Two regional buckets synced with rsync
explain: Dual-region buckets replicate objects synchronously across a specific pair of regions with a low RTO. Single-region buckets die with their region, multi-region spreads across a continent without the paired synchronous guarantee, and manual sync adds lag and toil.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A bucket holds objects with unpredictable access patterns, and the team does not want to maintain lifecycle rules to optimize storage cost. Which feature handles class transitions automatically?
options: Manual storage class changes per object
Lifecycle management rules
Object versioning
Autoclass, which automatically transitions objects between storage classes based on access
explain: Autoclass monitors access patterns and moves objects between Standard, Nearline, Coldline, and Archive automatically. Lifecycle rules require the team to predict the pattern up front, and versioning retains old copies rather than optimizing class.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: Legal requires certain objects to be undeletable until litigation ends, but the end date is unknown. Which mechanism enforces this?
options: A temporary hold on the objects, which blocks deletion until the hold is explicitly released
A retention policy with a fixed seven-year period
Object versioning
Locking the entire bucket
explain: Temporary holds prevent deletion or overwrite until released, which suits an unknown end date. Retention policies need a fixed duration, versioning preserves copies without blocking deletion, and bucket locks do not exist as a feature.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: An engineer deletes a bucket by mistake and needs the objects back. Which feature retains recently deleted objects and buckets for a recovery window?
options: Object versioning
Soft delete, which retains deleted objects and buckets for 7 days by default
Persistent disk snapshots
A lifecycle rule
explain: Soft delete keeps deleted objects and buckets recoverable for the retention duration (7 days by default). Versioning protects object contents but not bucket deletion itself, and snapshots and lifecycle rules are unrelated mechanisms.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A versioned bucket keeps growing because old object versions accumulate. How can noncurrent versions be deleted automatically 30 days after they are superseded?
options: Delete them manually each month
Disable versioning
A lifecycle rule matching noncurrent versions with an age condition
A retention policy
explain: Lifecycle rules support conditions on noncurrent versions (such as days since the version became noncurrent) to expire them automatically. Disabling versioning stops new versions but leaves existing ones, and retention policies block deletion rather than causing it.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: European data-residency rules require customer data to stay in the EU. Analysts will query it with BigQuery. Where must the dataset be created?
options: In the US multi-region for the best performance
In any region, because BigQuery encrypts data everywhere
In a US region with an EU label attached
In an EU region or the EU multi-region
explain: BigQuery dataset location controls where data is stored, so EU residency requires an EU regional or multi-regional location. Labels do not move data, and encryption does not satisfy residency requirements.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A team wants to share aggregated query results with another department without granting any access to the underlying dataset tables. What should they create?
options: An authorized view, which grants the view's readers access to the query results but not the source tables
A public dataset
A copy of every table for the other department
A project-level IAM binding for the department
explain: Authorized views let specified users query the view while the view's own service identity reads the underlying tables. Public datasets expose everything, copying tables duplicates data, and project bindings grant broader access than needed.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: An analyst accidentally deletes the wrong BigQuery table and needs the data as it was three days ago. What is the fastest recovery path?
options: Restore from a manual backup
Use time travel to query the table as of three days ago, within the 7-day window
Rebuild the data from application logs
Contact Google Cloud support
explain: BigQuery time travel retains table history for 7 days, so querying FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF a timestamp three days back recovers the data instantly. Manual backups only help if one was taken, and rebuilding from logs is slow and lossy.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: Analysts need to run SQL directly against CSV files landing in Cloud Storage without loading them into BigQuery first. What should they use?
options: bq load for every file
A Dataflow pipeline
An external (federated) table pointing at the Cloud Storage objects
A Cloud SQL instance
explain: External tables query data in place in Cloud Storage with standard SQL and no load step. bq load copies data into native tables, Dataflow is a processing framework rather than a query interface, and Cloud SQL is a separate transactional database.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A Cloud SQL instance's disk keeps filling up, and the team wants storage to grow automatically without downtime or manual intervention. What should be enabled?
options: Manual storage increases during maintenance windows
A larger machine type
A cross-region read replica
Automatic storage increase on the instance
explain: Automatic storage increase grows the instance's disk as it fills, with no downtime. Manual increases require intervention, machine types affect CPU and memory rather than disk, and read replicas do not expand the primary's storage.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: Developers currently connect to Cloud SQL with database passwords stored in config files. The team wants them to authenticate with their IAM identities instead. Which feature enables this?
options: Cloud SQL IAM database authentication
Authorized networks
Requiring SSL connections
Embedding a service account key in the application
explain: Cloud SQL IAM database authentication lets users and service accounts connect using IAM credentials instead of passwords. Authorized networks filter by IP rather than identity, and service account keys reintroduce the secret-management problem.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A team is migrating a legacy Cloud Datastore application and needs identical Datastore behavior and APIs. Which Firestore mode should they choose?
options: Native mode
Datastore mode
Bigtable compatibility mode
Spanner mode
explain: Datastore mode preserves the legacy Datastore API and behavior for existing applications. Native mode adds mobile and web SDK features with a different data model, and the other two modes do not exist.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A payment pipeline uses Pub/Sub, and processing the same payment twice would be a serious bug. How can duplicate delivery be prevented?
options: Rely on the default at-least-once delivery
Create two subscriptions for redundancy
Enable exactly-once delivery on the subscription
Set an ordering key
explain: Exactly-once delivery prevents duplicate message redelivery to the subscriber. The default is at-least-once, a second subscription doubles processing, and ordering keys sequence messages without deduplicating them.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: After fixing a consumer bug, the team must reprocess the last six hours of Pub/Sub messages. What is the correct mechanism?
options: Create a new topic and republish everything
Read from the dead-letter topic
Manually replay from application logs
Seek the subscription back to a timestamp six hours ago or to a snapshot
explain: Seeking a subscription to a past timestamp or snapshot replays acknowledged messages from that point. New topics and manual replays lose ordering and completeness, and the dead-letter topic only holds messages that repeatedly failed.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A VM has no firewall rules targeting it, yet it cannot receive any inbound connections while its outbound internet access works. Which default behavior explains this?
options: The implied firewall rules: deny all ingress and allow all egress, which exist in every VPC network
The default network blocks all traffic in both directions
Cloud NAT is required for inbound traffic
The VM needs a network tag before any traffic flows
explain: Every VPC network carries two implied rules: deny all ingress and allow all egress. Outbound works because of the implied allow-egress, while inbound needs an explicit allow rule; Cloud NAT and network tags are unrelated to this default.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A critical background service emits a heartbeat metric every minute. The team wants to be paged if the heartbeat stops arriving. Which alerting approach fits?
options: An alerting policy with a metric-absence condition, which fires when no data arrives for the configured duration
An uptime check on the service's homepage
A log-based metric counting heartbeat entries
A Cloud Monitoring dashboard
explain: Metric-absence conditions detect when a time series stops reporting, which is exactly a dead-service signal. Uptime checks probe network endpoints rather than metrics, and dashboards display data without notifying anyone.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A planned two-hour maintenance window will trigger several alerting policies. The team wants to suppress notifications during the window without losing the policies. What should they do?
options: Delete the alerting policies and recreate them afterward
Snooze the alerts for the duration of the maintenance window
Disable Cloud Monitoring for the project
Raise every threshold so nothing fires
explain: Snoozing suppresses notifications for a set period while keeping the policies intact and their history. Deleting policies loses configuration and history, and disabling Monitoring blinds the team to real problems during the window.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: The team is defining an availability SLI for an HTTP API. Which definition follows SRE practice?
options: The total number of requests per second
The result of an uptime check
The ratio of good events (for example, HTTP 2xx responses) to total valid requests
The average CPU utilization of the backends
explain: An SLI is a ratio of good events to total events, such as successful requests over all requests. Raw request counts and CPU utilization are not service-level indicators, and an uptime check is one probe rather than the service-wide ratio.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: An application needs its internal queue depth visible in Cloud Monitoring so the team can alert on backlog growth. Google provides no such metric. What should they do?
options: Only Google-provided metrics can appear in Cloud Monitoring
Parse it out of logs with a log-based metric instead
Wait for Google to add the metric
Write a custom metric from the application using the Monitoring API or OpenTelemetry
explain: Cloud Monitoring accepts custom metrics written by applications, which can then be charted and alerted on like any Google metric. Log-based metrics only count log entries rather than reporting gauge values, and there is no need to wait for Google.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: The Cloud Logging bill is dominated by noisy debug logs from one service. The team wants to stop ingesting those entries while keeping everything else. What should they configure?
options: An exclusion filter on the log sink or bucket that drops matching entries before ingestion
Delete the _Default log bucket
Shorten the retention period
Disable Cloud Logging for the project
explain: Exclusion filters discard matching log entries before they are ingested, directly cutting ingestion cost. Retention changes affect storage duration rather than ingestion, and disabling Logging removes all visibility.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: Compliance requires Admin Activity audit logs to be kept tamper-proof for a full year. The _Default bucket only keeps 30 days. Which bucket meets the requirement by default?
options: The _Default bucket with a longer retention typed in
The _Required bucket, which holds Admin Activity and System Event logs with a locked 400-day retention
A new custom bucket with a 7-day retention
The BigQuery billing export dataset
explain: The _Required bucket automatically receives Admin Activity and System Event logs with a locked 400-day retention that cannot be reduced. The _Default bucket's retention is configurable but not locked, and the billing export carries cost data rather than audit logs.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: The EU support team should be able to read logs from EU projects only, not from US projects. What is the cleanest way to scope their access?
options: Grant them the Logging Admin role on the organization
Create a separate organization for the EU team
Create log views that include only the EU projects' logs, and grant the team access to those views
Export the EU logs to CSV files monthly
explain: Log views present a filtered subset of a log bucket, and IAM on the view scopes who can read it. Organization-wide Logging Admin over-provisions access, and CSV exports are manual and stale.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: An engineer needs to force-trace one specific request as it flows through several microservices to diagnose a latency spike. How can they ensure the request is sampled?
options: Restart all the services
Create an uptime check for the request path
Search Cloud Logging for the request
Send the request with the X-Cloud-Trace-Context header carrying a trace ID and the force-trace option
explain: The X-Cloud-Trace-Context header propagates the trace ID across services, and its options flag can force sampling of that request. Restarts and uptime checks do not control trace sampling, and logs do not produce distributed traces.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: Cloud Build jobs keep failing at exactly 10 minutes even though the build steps need more time. What is the cause and fix?
options: Builds default to a 10-minute timeout; raise the timeout in the build configuration
Add more build steps to parallelize the work
Switch to a private worker pool
Enable retries on the trigger
explain: Cloud Build enforces a default timeout of 10 minutes per build, configurable up to a much larger limit. More steps do not extend the timeout, private pools change networking rather than duration, and retries rerun the same timed-out build.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A Cloud Build step must pull artifacts from an internal system that has no public IP address. The default build pool cannot reach it. What should be used?
options: The default public build pool with a firewall exception
A private worker pool with VPC network access to the internal system
Cloud Run instead of Cloud Build
Disable all firewall rules
explain: Private pools run builds on the customer's VPC network, reaching internal resources with private IPs. The default pool has no VPC access, Cloud Run is a different service, and disabling firewalls exposes the internal system.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: Several long-running standalone VMs must sit behind a load balancer, but the team cannot recreate them from a template. Which instance group type fits?
options: A managed instance group
An autoscaled instance group
An unmanaged instance group containing the existing VMs
A Cloud Run service
explain: Unmanaged instance groups let you attach existing, individually managed VMs to a load balancer without templates. Managed groups require an instance template and would recreate the VMs, losing their current state.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: An engineer suspects a pod is hitting its CPU limit in GKE. Which command shows current CPU and memory usage per pod?
options: kubectl logs
kubectl get pods
kubectl describe node
kubectl top pod, which reports live usage from the metrics server
explain: kubectl top queries the metrics server for live CPU and memory consumption per pod or node. kubectl logs shows container output, get lists objects without usage, and describe shows configuration rather than live metrics.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A Spanner database needs nightly backups retained for 30 days to meet the recovery policy. How should this be implemented?
options: Scheduled backups with a 30-day retention
Manual backups taken each night by an engineer
Persistent disk snapshots
Exporting the database to Cloud Storage nightly with a shell script
explain: Spanner supports scheduled backups with configurable retention, automating the nightly cadence. Manual backups depend on human reliability, disk snapshots apply to Compute Engine rather than Spanner, and scripted exports add fragile toil.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution
