q: Contractors must be able to access a project only during business hours (9 AM to 6 PM Eastern, weekdays), with no manual granting or revoking. Which mechanism enforces this?
options: A Cloud Scheduler job that adds and removes the IAM binding daily
An IAM Condition with a time-based CEL expression on the role binding
OS Login with 2-step verification
A VPC firewall rule with a schedule
explain: IAM Conditions support time-based expressions evaluated at request time, enforcing the window automatically. Scheduler-driven binding changes are fragile and leave gaps, and firewall rules do not control IAM access.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A contractor's engagement ends, but auditors may need the service account's activity history tied to its identity. What should be done with the service account?
options: Delete it immediately
Remove only its keys
Disable it, which blocks all use while preserving the identity and its audit trail
Leave it enabled until the next audit
explain: Disabling blocks authentication while keeping the account and its history intact for auditors. Deleting destroys the identity reference, removing keys leaves other authentication paths, and leaving it enabled keeps the risk active.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: The team wants to be notified if a Shielded VM's boot integrity check fails. What detects this and how is the team alerted?
options: Cloud Trace latency analysis
Uptime checks on the VM
OS patch management reports
Shielded VM integrity monitoring emits verification events to Cloud Logging, where an alerting policy can watch for failures
explain: Integrity monitoring verifies the measured boot chain and writes the results to Cloud Logging, which alerting policies can monitor. Trace, uptime checks, and patch reports do not observe boot integrity.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: Secrets stored in etcd for a regulated GKE cluster must be encrypted with a customer-managed Cloud KMS key rather than the default Google-managed key. What should be enabled on the cluster?
options: Confidential GKE nodes
Application-layer secrets encryption using a Cloud KMS key
Workload Identity
etcd backups to Cloud Storage
explain: Application-layer secrets encryption encrypts Kubernetes secrets with the specified Cloud KMS key before they are written to etcd. Confidential nodes protect data in use (memory), not secrets at rest in etcd.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A customer requires a human approval each time their externally-held encryption key is used by Google Cloud services. Which feature provides this per-use approval?
options: Access Approval
Access Transparency logs
Customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) alone
Key Access Justifications with an external key manager
explain: Key Access Justifications sends a justification request for each use of an externally-managed key, allowing approval or denial. Access Approval governs Google support access to data rather than key usage, and CMEK alone provides no per-use approval.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: Microservices need mutually-authenticated TLS using internally-issued certificates with automated rotation. Which managed service acts as the private certificate authority?
options: Certificate Authority Service
Google-managed SSL certificates
Self-signed certificates generated on each VM
Cloud KMS
explain: Certificate Authority Service is the managed private CA for issuing internal certificates. Google-managed certificates serve public load-balancer hostnames, and Cloud KMS manages keys rather than issuing X.509 certificates.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: The CISO wants OS Login enforced on every VM in the organization so SSH access is centrally managed through IAM. Which control applies this hierarchy-wide?
options: A startup script installed on each VM
A VPC firewall rule blocking port 22
The organization policy constraint compute.requireOsLogin
Manual configuration per project
explain: The compute.requireOsLogin boolean constraint enforces OS Login across the resource hierarchy from one place. Startup scripts and manual configuration do not scale centrally, and firewall rules filter traffic rather than managing SSH identity.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: External auditors need to read Admin Activity audit logs in the _Required log bucket, which the standard Logs Viewer role cannot see. Which role grants this?
options: Logs Viewer
Private Logs Viewer (roles/logging.privateLogViewer)
Logs Writer
Monitoring Viewer
explain: Private Logs Viewer adds read access to the _Required bucket and Data Access audit logs, which Logs Viewer excludes. Logs Writer grants write rather than read, and Monitoring Viewer covers metrics rather than logs.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A GitHub Actions workflow deploys via Workload Identity Federation, but access must be limited to pushes on the main branch of one repository. How is this restricted?
options: A separate service account per branch
IP allowlisting on the GitHub runners
A VPC firewall rule
An attribute condition on the workload identity pool provider, matching the repository and ref claims in the OIDC token
explain: Attribute conditions on the identity pool provider filter which external identities may impersonate the service account — for example, requiring the token's repository and ref claims to match main. Separate service accounts per branch do not scale, and firewall rules do not evaluate OIDC claims.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A login endpoint behind the external Application Load Balancer is being hammered by credential-stuffing bots. Which Cloud Armor integration distinguishes human users from bots?
options: Geo-based blocking rules
Preconfigured WAF rules
reCAPTCHA Enterprise risk assessment integrated with Cloud Armor security policies
Cloud CDN caching
explain: reCAPTCHA Enterprise produces bot risk scores that Cloud Armor rules can act on, directly addressing automated abuse. WAF rules match attack payload patterns rather than bot behavior, and geo-blocking filters by country.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: The security team reviewed a Security Command Center finding, confirmed it is a false positive, and wants it suppressed from active views without deleting the record. What should they do?
options: Delete the finding
Disable Security Command Center
Mute the finding, which suppresses it from active views while retaining the record
Ignore it; findings expire automatically
explain: Muting suppresses a finding from active views while preserving it for audit history; security marks can annotate it further. Findings cannot be deleted, disabling Security Command Center would lose all coverage, and findings do not auto-expire.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: An organization wants developers to start and stop VMs only when each VM carries an approved environment tag, with the check enforced by IAM at request time. Labels were considered but rejected for this. Why are tags the right fit, and how are they created?
options: Tags are the right fit because IAM Conditions can evaluate tag bindings on a resource, while labels cannot be used in IAM Conditions; tags are created as TagKeys and TagValues in Resource Manager and attached with tag bindings
Labels are actually the right fit because IAM Conditions evaluate labels directly, and tags are created on the Labels page in the console
Tags are the right fit because they appear on invoices, and they are created with gcloud compute instances add-labels
Neither works: IAM Conditions cannot evaluate any resource metadata, so the team must use separate projects per environment
explain: Tags (TagKeys/TagValues with tag bindings) are designed for access control and can be referenced in IAM Conditions, whereas labels are for organization and billing and are invisible to IAM Conditions. A common misconception is that labels and tags are interchangeable; only tags enforce policy at request time. Labels are created per-resource, not in Resource Manager, and IAM Conditions absolutely can evaluate resource metadata like tags.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An automation script that applies a large set of labels to a Compute Engine VM fails with a quota-style error once it reaches a certain count. What is the documented limit, and what is the correct fix?
options: A resource can carry at most 64 labels, so the script must stay within 64 labels per resource or split metadata across multiple resources
A project can carry at most 64 labels in total, so labels must be deleted from other resources first
Labels are limited to 10 per resource, and the only fix is to use network tags instead
There is no limit; the script must have a syntax error in the label names
explain: Google Cloud allows a maximum of 64 labels per resource, so the script must consolidate or drop labels to fit. The limit is per resource, not per project, and network tags serve a different purpose (firewall targeting), so swapping to tags does not work around a label limit.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A team tries to write a VPC firewall rule that targets VMs using a resource label like env=prod, but the console does not accept labels in the rule's target field. What should they use instead, and why?
options: They should use a separate VPC per environment, because firewall rules cannot target individual VMs at all
They should use a service account as the rule target, because labels are only visible to IAM
They should keep trying labels, because firewall rules do accept labels after the API is enabled
They should use network tags as the rule target, because firewall rules select VMs by network tags (or service accounts), not by labels, which are for billing and organization only
explain: Firewall rules target VMs by network tags or service accounts; labels are never evaluated by firewall rules. The misconception is that labels are a universal selector, but they exist for cost allocation and organization. Service accounts are also valid targets, but the direct replacement for a label-based selector is a network tag.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A platform team wants a proactive alert when any project consumes more than 80% of its Compute Engine CPU quota, before deployments start failing. Which approach works?
options: Build a Cloud Monitoring alert on the serviceruntime quota allocation and usage metrics, which expose quota consumption as time series
Create a billing budget, because budgets track quota consumption as well as spend
Poll the Quotas page in the console every hour, because quota usage cannot be monitored programmatically
Write a log-based metric on audit logs, because quota consumption is only visible in Admin Activity logs
explain: Cloud Monitoring exposes quota metrics (such as serviceruntime quota allocation/usage) that alerting policies can evaluate, giving advance warning before limits are hit. Billing budgets track spend, not quota; the Quotas page is manual; and quota consumption is a metric, not something parsed from audit logs.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A company wants a hard stop on spend: when a billing budget threshold is breached, a sandbox project's billing should be disabled automatically. Budgets alone only send notifications. What is the documented way to automate the shutoff?
options: Route the budget alert to a Pub/Sub topic and trigger a Cloud Function that disables billing on the project via the Cloud Billing API, which is the documented programmatic-billing-control pattern
Set the budget threshold to zero, which automatically disables billing on all projects
Enable the billing account's auto-shutoff toggle in the console, which stops all resources at the threshold
Delete the billing account when the alert fires, because budgets can run deletion workflows natively
explain: Budgets only notify; the documented hard-stop pattern publishes the budget alert to Pub/Sub and runs automation (commonly a Cloud Function) that disables billing on the project. There is no native auto-shutoff toggle, a zero threshold does not disable anything, and deleting the billing account is destructive and not what budgets do.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A new customer signs up for Google Cloud and asks how much free credit they receive to experiment, and for how long it lasts. What is the documented Free Trial offer?
options: $100 in credits valid for 30 days, restricted to App Engine only
$300 in credits valid for 90 days to spend on Google Cloud services
Unlimited credits for one year, but only for BigQuery
No credits; new accounts only get the Always Free tier
explain: The documented Free Trial gives new customers $300 in credits valid for 90 days across Google Cloud services. It is not limited to one product, it is not unlimited, and it exists alongside (not instead of) the Always Free tier.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A student wants to run a tiny Linux VM for coursework at no charge for months, without consuming trial credits. Which option fits the Always Free tier?
options: A Spot VM of any size, because preemptible capacity is excluded from billing
A VM with a GPU attached, because accelerators are free for educational accounts
Any machine type in any region, because the first VM in each project is always free
An e2-micro instance in an eligible US region, within the Always Free usage limits
explain: The Always Free tier includes a monthly allotment of f1-micro/e2-micro usage in eligible regions (such as us-west1, us-central1, us-east1), not any machine type or region. Spot VMs are discounted but billed, GPUs are never free, and there is no blanket first-VM exemption.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An engineer installs the Cloud SDK but finds that kubectl is missing. What is the correct way to add it?
options: Run gcloud components install kubectl to add the missing SDK component
Download kubectl from an unrelated third-party site and place it on the PATH
Run gcloud auth login again, which reinstalls all SDK components
Reinstall the entire operating system, because SDK components cannot be added later
explain: The SDK is modular, and gcloud components install adds components like kubectl without a full reinstall. Re-authenticating does not install software, reinstalling the OS is absurd, and third-party binaries bypass the SDK's managed updates.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An engineer finishes work on a shared workstation and wants to remove their Google credentials from the gcloud CLI so the next user cannot act as them. Which command does this?
options: gcloud config unset project, which deletes the user's Google account
rm -rf on the project directory, which clears cloud credentials
gcloud auth login --revoke, which is not a valid flag combination
gcloud auth revoke, which removes stored credentials for the account from the local SDK
explain: gcloud auth revoke deletes the locally stored credentials for the account, ending that CLI session's access. Unsetting the project changes only a default property, deleting a local directory does not touch stored credentials, and the account itself is untouched by revoke.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A developer runs a small web app inside Cloud Shell on port 8080 and wants to click through it in a browser tab. How can they reach it?
options: They cannot; Cloud Shell has no network access to processes it runs
They can use the Cloud Shell Web Preview button, which exposes ports 8080-8084 over HTTPS for browser testing
They must assign an external IP to the Cloud Shell VM with gcloud compute addresses create
They should open the VM's serial console, which renders HTML pages as text
explain: Cloud Shell's Web Preview feature forwards a set of ports (8080-8084) to the browser over HTTPS, ideal for quick testing. Cloud Shell VMs are ephemeral and not meant for static IPs, and the serial console is for troubleshooting, not web browsing.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An engineer must authenticate the gcloud CLI on a headless Linux server with no graphical browser. Which flow should they use?
options: Skip authentication entirely, because gcloud works anonymously for project resources
Copy their personal password into a gcloud config file, because passwords work for CLI auth
Run gcloud auth login --no-launch-browser and complete the authorization code flow from another machine
Email their service account key to the server administrator for manual installation
explain: The --no-launch-browser flag prints a URL and accepts a pasted authorization code, the documented headless flow. Passwords are not valid gcloud credentials, emailing keys is insecure, and gcloud cannot access project resources anonymously.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A developer has a service account key file for local testing and wants Google Cloud client libraries to use it automatically without embedding the path in code. What is the standard mechanism?
options: Upload the key to Cloud Storage and reference the gs:// URL in the code
Rename the file to credentials.txt and place it in the project root
Hardcode the key JSON into the application's source before each run
Set the GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS environment variable to the key file's path so Application Default Credentials picks it up
explain: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS is the documented environment variable that ADC uses to locate a service account key file. Renaming files or hardcoding secrets is fragile and insecure, and client libraries cannot read keys from a gs:// URL.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An engineer sets a default project with gcloud config set project, but one script must target a different project for a single command. Which takes precedence?
options: The --project flag on the command line, which overrides the configured default for that invocation
The configured default always wins, so the flag is ignored
The CLOUDSDK_CORE_PROJECT environment variable is ignored entirely by gcloud
Whichever was set most recently in time, regardless of mechanism
explain: gcloud precedence is command-line flags first, then environment variables, then configured properties, so --project wins for that invocation. The default is not sticky against flags, and recency across mechanisms is not how precedence works.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A developer tries to create a project in the console and is denied, even though they can create VMs in existing projects. Which permission are they missing?
options: compute.instances.create, which is required for all console actions
resourcemanager.projects.create, granted by roles such as Project Creator at the folder or organization level
billing.accounts.get, which is checked before any project creation
iam.serviceAccounts.actAs, which gates every Resource Manager call
explain: Creating projects requires resourcemanager.projects.create, typically granted via the Project Creator role on a folder or the organization. VM creation permissions are unrelated, billing read access does not grant creation rights, and actAs governs service account impersonation, not project creation.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A team lead must let project owners link their own projects to the corporate billing account, without granting anyone rights on the billing account itself. Which role enables this when granted on the project?
options: Billing Account Administrator, which must be granted on the billing account
Project Owner, which implicitly includes billing linkage rights
Project Billing Manager (roles/billing.projectManager), which allows linking that specific project to a billing account
Billing Account Viewer, which is sufficient for linking projects
explain: The Project Billing Manager role is designed to be granted on a project and permits linking that project to a billing account. Billing Account Administrator is broader and granted on the billing account, Project Owner carries no billing-account rights, and Viewer is read-only.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A team wants every Cloud Shell session to start with their custom tooling preinstalled, instead of installing it manually each time. What is the supported approach?
options: They can configure a custom Cloud Shell container image so sessions boot with their tooling baked in
Cloud Shell cannot be customized; the environment is fixed by Google
They should file a support ticket asking Google to change the base image for their organization
They can install tools once and rely on the VM disk, because Cloud Shell VMs are never recycled
explain: Cloud Shell supports a custom container image (via environment customization) so every session starts with the team's tooling. The base image is customizable by the user, sessions do get recycled after inactivity so manual installs do not persist, and no support ticket is needed.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: The finance team wants billing alerts, the legal team wants compliance notices, and the SRE team wants outage notifications, each routed to the right people. Which feature supports this routing?
options: IAM basic roles, which automatically subscribe Owners to all notification types
Pub/Sub topics named after each team, which Google Cloud publishes notifications to by default
Essential Contacts, which delivers Google Cloud notifications to designated contacts per category such as billing, legal, security, suspension, and technical
Cloud Billing budgets, which email every user in the organization regardless of category
explain: Essential Contacts routes notifications by category (billing, legal, security, suspension, technical) to the right people per project, folder, or organization. Budgets only cover spend alerts, basic roles do not manage notification routing, and Google does not publish to customer-named topics by default.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A regulated company requires every VM in the organization to boot with Shielded VM features (secure boot, vTPM, integrity monitoring) with no exceptions. Which central control enforces this on all new VMs?
options: An IAM deny policy on compute.instances.create, because deny policies control VM configuration
The organization policy constraint compute.requireShieldedVm, which mandates Shielded VM features on VM creation
A billing budget scoped to the organization, because budgets can restrict machine configurations
The default Compute Engine service account, which enables Shielded VM automatically when it has the Editor role
explain: The boolean organization policy constraint compute.requireShieldedVm enforces Shielded VM options at creation time across the hierarchy. IAM deny policies govern access, not VM configuration; budgets only alert on spend; and the default service account's role has nothing to do with Shielded VM settings.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: Audits keep finding buckets created with fine-grained ACLs, which the security team has banned in favor of uniform bucket-level access. How can they guarantee every new bucket enforces uniform access?
options: They cannot; bucket access mode is always the creator's choice
By adding an IAM deny policy on storage.buckets.create, which forces uniform access on creation
By enforcing the organization policy constraint storage.uniformBucketLevelAccess, which requires new buckets to use uniform bucket-level access
By enabling the BigQuery billing export, which reports buckets not using uniform access
explain: The list constraint storage.uniformBucketLevelAccess, enforced via organization policy, mandates uniform bucket-level access on new buckets. IAM deny policies control who can act, not resource configuration; billing export only reports costs; and bucket access mode is centrally governable.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An administrator is comparing two organization policy constraints: compute.disableSerialPortAccess and compute.trustedImageProjects. What is the fundamental difference between them?
options: The first is a boolean constraint (on or off), while the second is a list constraint (an allowed list of values)
The first is enforced by IAM and the second by VPC Service Controls
The first applies only to existing VMs while the second applies only to new VMs
Both are identical in behavior and the names are aliases for the same control
explain: Organization policy constraints come in two kinds: boolean constraints toggle a behavior on or off, and list constraints define allowed or denied values. Both are organization policy (not IAM or VPC SC), and both are evaluated at creation or update time, not split by resource age.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A script lists all Cloud Storage buckets in a project with thousands of buckets, but gcloud pages through results slowly in automation. How can the script cap the number of results returned in one call?
options: Pass --limit to bound the number of results returned
Pass --no-pagination, which is not a real gcloud flag
Set the project quota higher, because result counts follow quota limits
Pipe through head -n 50, which reduces the API response size
explain: The --limit flag caps how many resources a gcloud list command returns, which is the supported way to bound output in scripts. Piping to head still fetches everything first, quotas do not control listing size, and --no-pagination is not the mechanism for limiting counts.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A developer wants to edit code directly in the browser with IDE features like syntax highlighting and a file tree, without installing anything locally. Which Cloud Shell capability provides this?
options: The Cloud Shell terminal's cat command, which is the only editing tool available
The Cloud Shell code editor (Open Editor), a browser-based IDE built into Cloud Shell
The Cloud Console API Explorer, which edits source files attached to APIs
The Logs Explorer, which supports in-place editing of logged source files
explain: Cloud Shell includes a full browser-based code editor (the Open Editor button) with a file explorer and language support. The API Explorer and Logs Explorer are not code editors, and while terminal editors exist, the built-in IDE is the intended browser editing experience.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: Support asks an engineer to confirm the installed Cloud SDK version, the active configuration, and installation paths while debugging a CLI issue. Which single command surfaces this diagnostic summary?
options: gcloud auth list, which shows SDK version details
gcloud config list, which prints installation paths
gcloud info, which reports SDK version, configuration, properties, and installation details
gcloud version --diagnostics, which is not a valid command form
explain: gcloud info prints a diagnostic summary including the SDK version, active configuration, and installation paths. gcloud auth list shows only accounts, gcloud config list shows only properties, and version output is a subset of what info provides.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An engineer enables the Cloud SQL Admin API with gcloud services enable sqladmin.googleapis.com and notices dependent APIs were enabled too, without extra commands. What is true about service enablement?
options: Dependencies are only enabled when using the Cloud Console, never via gcloud
The engineer must have had the Service Usage Admin role, which silently skips dependencies
This was a bug; each API must always be enabled individually
Enabling a service automatically enables the services it depends on
explain: Service Usage automatically enables a service's dependencies when the service itself is enabled, by design. It is not a bug, it works the same via gcloud and console, and the role governs permission to enable, not dependency behavior.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An administrator must grant a contractor the Compute Viewer role on a project that already has a large IAM policy, without disturbing any existing bindings. Which command is safe, and which one is dangerous here?
options: gcloud projects set-iam-policy is safe because it merges changes; add-iam-policy-binding is dangerous because it duplicates bindings
Both commands are identical in effect, so either is safe
Neither is safe; IAM policies can only be changed in the Cloud Console
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding is safe because it adds one binding; set-iam-policy is dangerous because it replaces the entire policy and could wipe existing bindings
explain: add-iam-policy-binding performs a read-modify-write that appends a single binding, while set-iam-policy writes the whole policy authoritatively, so a stale read could delete other bindings. The two commands are not equivalent, and the CLI is fully capable of safe IAM edits when the additive form is used.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A financial firm must run a trading application on hardware shared with no other customer to satisfy a compliance audit, and it wants to bring its own existing OS licenses. Which Compute Engine option fits?
options: Sole-tenant nodes, which provide dedicated physical servers for the project's VMs and support bringing existing licenses
Spot VMs, which run on dedicated hardware reserved per customer
A regional managed instance group, which guarantees physical isolation between tenants
Cloud Run, which always runs on single-tenant infrastructure
explain: Sole-tenant nodes dedicate an entire physical server to one project, meeting hardware-isolation compliance needs and enabling BYOL. Spot VMs are discounted preemptible capacity on shared hardware, MIGs provide logical grouping not physical isolation, and Cloud Run is multi-tenant serverless.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A team attaches GPUs to Compute Engine VMs for model training and notices the VMs cannot use live migration during host maintenance. What configuration is required, and what is true about GPU availability?
options: GPUs support live migration, so the team should file a support ticket about the bug
The VMs must set the maintenance behavior to terminate (GPUs do not support live migration), and GPUs are only available in select zones and machine types
GPUs can be attached to any machine type in any region, and maintenance behavior is irrelevant
GPUs require sole-tenant nodes, so the team must purchase an entire physical server
explain: GPUs cannot live-migrate, so instances with GPUs must use terminate maintenance behavior and are restarted after host events; GPUs are also zonal resources available on specific machine types. There is no bug to report, availability is not universal, and sole tenancy is not required for GPUs.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: An in-memory analytics database needs 24 vCPUs and roughly 600 GB of RAM per VM, a ratio no predefined machine type matches. Which machine family should the architect choose?
options: Compute-optimized (C-series), because the highest vCPU count implies the most memory
Accidentally choosing Spot VMs, because machine family does not affect the memory ratio
Memory-optimized (M-series), which offers the highest memory-per-vCPU ratios for in-memory workloads
Shared-core machine types, which allow arbitrary memory attachments
explain: Memory-optimized machine types are purpose-built for workloads like in-memory databases with very high RAM-to-CPU ratios. Compute-optimized favors CPU, shared-core types are small burstable VMs without custom ratios, and Spot is a pricing model, not a machine family.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A team takes daily snapshots of a 500 GB persistent disk and is surprised the snapshot storage bill is far smaller than 500 GB per day. What explains this?
options: Snapshots are incremental: each snapshot stores only the blocks that changed since the previous one
Snapshots are compressed to a fixed 10 GB regardless of disk size
The first snapshot is free and only the most recent snapshot is billed
Snapshot billing is capped per project, so additional snapshots cost nothing
explain: Persistent disk snapshots are incremental, so daily snapshots of a slowly changing disk consume far less than a full copy each day. There is no fixed-size compression to 10 GB, every snapshot's changed blocks are billed, and no project-level cap makes extras free.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A company deploys identical web front ends in three regions from one template and wants the template itself to be resilient to a zonal failure of the template metadata. Which template scope should they use?
options: A regional instance template, which replicates the template across zones in the region
A global instance template, because templates are global resources by default
Three separate zonal templates, because templates cannot span zones
No template at all; MIGs can only be created from machine images
explain: Regional instance templates store the template redundantly across zones in a region, unlike zonal templates. Templates are zonal or regional, never global; and MIGs are routinely created from instance templates, not only from machine images.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A team runs a stateful batch workload in a MIG and wants to stage a new instance template but apply it to instances manually, one by one, during a maintenance window. Which update type should they configure?
options: Proactive updates, which immediately roll the new template to all instances
Opportunistic updates, which stage the new template and apply it only when each instance is manually recreated
Automatic updates, which cannot be paused once started
Canary updates, which are the only update type MIGs support
explain: Opportunistic update mode stages the new template and waits for manual instance recreation, giving the team per-instance control. Proactive mode rolls automatically, there is no separate automatic type, and canary is a strategy built on top of update settings, not the only mode.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A Cloud Run service behind a customer-facing API suffers slow first responses after idle periods. Traffic is spiky with long quiet gaps. What is the most direct way to reduce these cold starts?
options: Increase the container's memory limit, because cold starts are caused by insufficient memory
Rewrite the service in a compiled language, because cold starts only affect interpreted runtimes
Set a minimum number of instances so warm containers are always available to serve the first requests
Enable CPU throttling, which keeps instances warm between requests
explain: Minimum instances keep containers warm and ready, eliminating the scale-from-zero latency at the cost of idle spend. Memory size does not prevent cold starts, compiled languages start faster but still cold-start from zero, and the default CPU allocation is already request-scoped; always-allocated CPU is a different setting.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A Cloud Run service processes Pub/Sub messages with background threads that continue working for a few seconds after the HTTP response is sent, but the work is being cut off. What setting fixes this?
options: Set CPU to always allocated so the container keeps CPU outside of request processing
Increase the maximum instances, because throttling kills background threads
Switch to a larger region, because background work is region-restricted
Set the concurrency to 1, which automatically extends CPU allocation
explain: By default Cloud Run allocates CPU only during request processing, which kills background threads after the response; always-allocated CPU keeps the container running. Instance count and region do not affect CPU allocation, and concurrency 1 does not change the CPU allocation mode.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A team wants to roll out a new Cloud Run revision gradually: 5% of traffic for an hour, then 50%, then 100%, with instant rollback if errors spike. How should they implement this?
options: Use Cloud Run traffic splitting to shift percentages between revisions gradually, rolling back by shifting traffic to the previous revision
Deploy with a new service name for each percentage step, because a service only supports one revision
Edit the running revision's container image in place to each new version progressively
Use a Cloud Load Balancer URL map, because Cloud Run has no native traffic controls
explain: Cloud Run natively splits traffic across revisions by percentage, enabling gradual rollouts and instant rollback by moving traffic back. A service hosts many revisions, revisions are immutable so in-place edits are impossible, and no external load balancer is needed for this.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A data-processing function triggered by Cloud Storage events occasionally needs up to 45 minutes to finish large files, but executions are being killed at 9 minutes. What is the correct fix?
options: Split the file into smaller chunks, because 9 minutes is a hard limit for all Cloud Functions
Deploy as a 2nd gen Cloud Functions function, which supports timeouts up to 60 minutes
Increase the function's memory, because timeout scales with memory allocation
Move to App Engine standard, which is the only service without timeout limits
explain: 1st gen Cloud Functions cap execution at 9 minutes, while 2nd gen (Cloud Run based) allows up to 60 minutes. Memory does not extend timeouts, chunking is a workaround rather than the fix, and App Engine has its own request deadlines.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: An App Engine application is receiving abusive traffic from a set of known malicious IP ranges, and the team wants to block them before they reach application code. What is the native mechanism?
options: VPC firewall rules, which apply directly to App Engine standard instances
Cloud Armor policies, which only work with App Engine flexible
App Engine firewall rules, which allow and deny traffic by IP range with priority ordering
IAM deny policies on the App Engine service account, which filter by source IP
explain: App Engine has its own firewall that allows or denies ingress by IP CIDR ranges with priorities, evaluated before app code. VPC firewall rules do not apply to App Engine, Cloud Armor sits in front of load balancers rather than App Engine directly, and IAM deny policies govern API access, not network traffic.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A company must migrate 50 TB of objects from an S3-compatible on-premises store to Cloud Storage with checksum verification and resumability, without writing custom transfer code. Which service fits?
options: Pub/Sub notifications, which automatically copy objects between clouds
Storage Transfer Service, which moves data from S3-compatible sources to Cloud Storage as a managed job
Cloud Data Fusion, which is the managed Hadoop/Spark service
gsutil rsync run manually each night, because no managed transfer service supports S3-compatible sources
explain: Storage Transfer Service is the managed offering for one-time or recurring transfers from S3-compatible storage into Cloud Storage with integrity checks. Data Fusion is for data integration pipelines, manual rsync lacks managed scheduling and monitoring, and Pub/Sub notifications only signal changes within Google Cloud.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A research institute publishes a 2 TB public dataset in Cloud Storage. External researchers download it heavily, and the institute does not want to pay for their egress. How can the bucket be configured so downloaders pay?
options: Enable Requester Pays on the bucket, so the project of the requester is billed for access and egress charges
Make the bucket multi-regional, which eliminates all egress charges
Enable Autoclass, which shifts download costs to the requester automatically
Set a lifecycle rule deleting objects after download, which prevents repeat egress
explain: Requester Pays shifts data access and egress costs to the requester's project, the documented model for public datasets. Multi-region does not remove egress fees, Autoclass only optimizes storage class placement, and lifecycle deletion would destroy the dataset.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A healthcare company encrypts patient archives in Cloud Storage with keys it generates on its own hardware, and Google must never store those keys. Which encryption option meets this requirement?
options: Google-managed encryption keys, because Google never stores keys it manages
Customer-supplied encryption keys (CSEK), where the customer provides the key with each request and Google does not retain it
Customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) in Cloud KMS, which keeps keys out of Google's systems
TLS in transit, which satisfies at-rest encryption requirements
explain: With CSEK the customer supplies the raw key on each operation and Google does not store it, unlike CMEK where keys live in Cloud KMS. Google-managed keys are stored by Google by definition, and TLS only protects data in transit, not at rest.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A media pipeline must start transcoding within seconds whenever a new video object lands in a Cloud Storage bucket, including overwrite events. What is the most direct eventing setup?
options: Write a Cloud Scheduler job that lists objects, because notifications cannot detect overwrites
Poll the bucket with gsutil ls every minute, because Cloud Storage has no eventing
Create a Cloud Storage Pub/Sub notification on the bucket for object finalize events, triggering the pipeline from the topic
Enable object versioning, which automatically invokes Cloud Functions on new objects
explain: Cloud Storage Pub/Sub notifications publish events for object creation, deletion, and metadata updates, and a subscription can trigger the pipeline immediately. Polling is slow and wasteful, versioning alone triggers nothing, and notifications do fire on overwrites (finalize events).
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A trading platform stores critical data in a dual-region Cloud Storage bucket and needs a guaranteed recovery point objective of 15 minutes for asynchronous replication between the regions. Which feature provides this?
options: Autoclass, which accelerates replication as a side effect
Default dual-region replication, which guarantees a 15-minute RPO
Object versioning, which replicates versions within 15 minutes
Turbo Replication, which provides a 15-minute RPO SLA for dual-region buckets
explain: Turbo Replication is the add-on that gives dual-region buckets a 15-minute RPO for asynchronous geo-replication. Default replication has no RPO guarantee, versioning is about history not replication speed, and Autoclass manages storage classes, not replication.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: Analysts query a large BigQuery table filtering on event_date and grouping by user_id, and want to cut bytes scanned without partitioning changes. The table is already partitioned by event_date. What should they add?
options: Clustering by user_id, which colocates related rows so filters and grouping skip more data
A second partition on user_id, because BigQuery tables support multi-column partitioning
An authorized view, which reduces scanned bytes through access control
A materialized view on event_date, which is the only way to speed grouped queries
explain: Clustering sorts data within partitions by up to four columns, letting BigQuery prune blocks for filters and aggregations on user_id. BigQuery supports only single-column partitioning, authorized views govern access rather than scan size, and materialized views are a heavier solution than clustering for this pattern.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A dashboard runs the same expensive aggregation over a billion-row BigQuery table every five minutes, and the underlying data changes only hourly. How can the team serve it faster and cheaper?
options: Increase the query's slot reservation, because speed only comes from more slots
Create a materialized view of the aggregation, which precomputes results and refreshes automatically
Partition the table by ingestion time, which caches query results automatically
Export the table to Cloud Storage, because dashboards cannot query BigQuery directly
explain: Materialized views precompute and incrementally refresh aggregations, so repeated dashboard queries read the small result instead of scanning billions of rows. More slots do not reduce bytes scanned, partitioning alone does not cache results, and BigQuery is designed to be queried directly by dashboards.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A team needs to recover a BigQuery table as it existed 30 days ago, but time travel only reaches back 7 days. What should they have set up, or use now?
options: An authorized view, which retains historical data indefinitely
Streaming inserts, which keep a 30-day buffer of all changes
Table snapshots, which preserve table contents at a point in time beyond the 7-day time-travel window
Table clustering, which extends the time-travel window to 30 days automatically
explain: Table snapshots capture point-in-time copies retained independently of the 7-day time-travel window. Clustering does not affect history retention, authorized views are an access mechanism, and streaming buffers hold recent uncommitted rows, not month-old states.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A BigQuery table contains a national_id column that most analysts must never see, while other columns stay fully queryable. What is the native way to hide just that column?
options: Create a separate dataset per analyst, because column hiding requires dataset duplication
Use separate tables for each column, because column-level control does not exist
Apply column-level security with policy tags from a Data Catalog taxonomy, restricting the sensitive column
Delete the column, because BigQuery cannot restrict individual columns
explain: Policy tags provide native column-level security: columns tagged as sensitive require the fine-grained reader role. Deleting or duplicating data is unnecessary, and BigQuery does support column-level controls, contrary to the distractors.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: Marketing wants yesterday's Google Ads campaign data in BigQuery every morning without building or maintaining an ingestion pipeline. Which managed option does this?
options: Cloud Scheduler calling the Ads API, because no managed transfer exists for Google Ads
BigQuery ML, which imports marketing data as a side effect of training
Manual CSV uploads, because automated transfers require a third-party ETL tool
BigQuery Data Transfer Service, which offers scheduled managed transfers from sources like Google Ads
explain: BigQuery Data Transfer Service provides managed, scheduled ingestion from SaaS sources including Google Ads with no pipeline code. Cloud Scheduler would require custom code, BigQuery ML trains models rather than ingesting, and manual uploads defeat the automation requirement.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A Bigtable table stores sensor readings with a row key of device_id#timestamp, and one device's writes are overloading a single node. What row-key design principle is being violated?
options: Row keys must be UUIDs, because any meaningful key causes hotspotting
Keys should start with a high-cardinality, evenly distributed value and avoid monotonically increasing prefixes like timestamps that concentrate writes
Bigtable requires the timestamp to come first in every row key
Hotspotting is impossible in Bigtable, so the overload must come from the network
explain: Bigtable sorts rows lexicographically, so sequential or timestamp-leading keys funnel writes onto one node; good design promotes high-cardinality prefixes (or reversed timestamps) to spread load. UUIDs are one option but not mandatory, timestamps-first is the anti-pattern, and hotspotting is a well-documented Bigtable phenomenon.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A team stores 60 TB of rarely accessed historical telemetry in Bigtable where occasional throughput-heavy scans matter more than millisecond latency. Which storage type minimizes cost?
options: Memory storage, which is the cheapest Bigtable tier
Archived tables, because Bigtable automatically tiers cold data to Archive class
SSD storage, because Bigtable requires SSD for all production data
HDD storage, which is the lower-cost option suited to large, throughput-oriented, latency-tolerant data
explain: Bigtable HDD storage is designed for large (10 TB+) datasets where throughput matters more than latency, at lower cost than SSD. SSD is not mandatory, there is no memory storage tier, and Bigtable has no automatic Archive-class tiering.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A mobile game stores player session documents in Firestore and must automatically delete sessions older than 24 hours to control storage growth and stale data. What is the managed way to do this?
options: Enable point-in-time recovery, which also purges old documents
Move sessions to Cloud Storage, because Firestore cannot delete documents
Run a nightly Cloud Function that scans the whole collection, because Firestore has no automatic expiry
Set a Time-To-Live (TTL) policy on a timestamp field so Firestore deletes expired documents automatically
explain: Firestore TTL policies automatically delete documents once a designated timestamp field passes, with no custom code. A scanning function is unnecessary, point-in-time recovery is for backup not expiry, and Firestore deletes documents natively.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: An application needs a simple, low-latency cache for rendered web pages. There is no requirement for persistence or failover; if the cache is lost, pages are just re-rendered. Which Memorystore option is the most economical fit?
options: Memorystore for Redis with high availability, because all caches require replication
Cloud SQL with a memory table, because Memorystore cannot serve web content
Memorystore for Memcached, which offers simple distributed caching without persistence or failover overhead
Bigtable, because it is the only service with sub-millisecond reads
explain: Memcached is the lightweight option for plain caching with no persistence or HA requirements, and costs less than a replicated Redis setup. Redis HA is overkill here, Cloud SQL is not a cache, and Bigtable is a NoSQL database, not the economical cache choice.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A fleet of VMs currently runs both the legacy monitoring agent and the legacy logging agent, and the team wants a single supported agent collecting both metrics and logs. Which agent should they standardize on?
options: The Ops Agent, which collects both metrics and logs in one agent and is the documented successor to the legacy agents
The legacy monitoring agent, because it also collects logs when configured with syslog
The Cloud Trace agent, which handles metrics, logs, and traces together
No agent is needed; the metadata server collects guest metrics and logs automatically
explain: The Ops Agent is Google's unified agent for metrics and logs, replacing the legacy monitoring and logging agents. The legacy agents are separate and aging, there is no Cloud Trace agent for VMs, and the metadata server does not collect guest OS metrics or application logs.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A company with 500 VMs needs the Ops Agent installed on every current and future VM automatically, with compliance reporting on which VMs have it. What is the most maintainable approach?
options: Create an Ops Agent policy (agent policy) that automatically installs and maintains the agent on matching VMs
Add the agent to the golden image only, because agent policies cannot target running VMs
Ask developers to install the agent in their application Dockerfiles
SSH into each VM and install the agent by hand, then repeat for every new VM
explain: Ops Agent policies automatically install, update, and report compliance for the agent across matching VMs, including new ones. Manual installation does not scale, golden images miss already-running VMs, and Dockerfiles are irrelevant to VM guest agents.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: An SRE team manages 30 projects and wants a single Cloud Monitoring view showing CPU utilization across all of them, without switching projects. What should they configure?
options: A Shared VPC, because monitoring follows network boundaries
Thirty identical dashboards, one per project, opened in separate tabs
A metrics scope that includes all 30 projects, enabling cross-project viewing in Cloud Monitoring
A billing export to BigQuery, because Monitoring cannot span projects
explain: A metrics scope can include multiple monitored projects so charts, dashboards, and alerts see metrics across all of them. Shared VPC is about networking, duplicate dashboards are unmaintainable, and billing export is for costs, not operational metrics.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: During an incident, an engineer wants to run SQL queries over the last 6 hours of application logs to count errors by service, without exporting anything to BigQuery first. Which feature enables this?
options: The _Default sink, which automatically creates BigQuery tables for SQL access
The Logs Explorer regex bar, which runs full SQL dialect queries
Log Analytics, which provides a SQL interface over log buckets
Cloud Trace, which stores logs as spans queryable with SQL
explain: Log Analytics lets users run SQL directly against logs stored in log buckets. The Logs Explorer uses its own query language, not SQL; Cloud Trace handles latency traces, not log SQL; and sinks to BigQuery require explicit setup rather than happening automatically.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: Auditors ask how long Admin Activity audit logs are kept in the _Required log bucket with no custom configuration. What is the documented default?
options: 400 days, the fixed retention of the _Required bucket
30 days, the same as the _Default bucket
7 days, after which Admin Activity logs are purged
Indefinitely, because audit logs are never deleted
explain: The _Required bucket retains Admin Activity (and system event) logs for 400 days and its retention cannot be reduced. The _Default bucket keeps 30 days, there is no 7-day purge, and retention is finite, not indefinite.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A security team enables Data Access audit logs for Cloud Storage and is surprised by a sharp rise in log volume and cost. What explains this, and what was the prior default?
options: Data Access logs were already enabled, so enabling them again duplicated every entry
Data Access logs are disabled by default (except BigQuery) because they are high-volume; enabling them records every read and write, which grows volume and cost significantly
Admin Activity logs were disabled as a side effect, so the team lost coverage
Log volume is fixed per project, so the cost rise must come from another service
explain: Data Access logs are off by default precisely because read-heavy services generate enormous volumes; turning them on multiplies ingestion and cost. They were not previously on, Admin Activity logging is unaffected, and log volume scales with activity rather than being fixed.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A DBA needs a full copy of the production Cloud SQL instance for load testing, including current data, without affecting production performance or risking the live database. What is the simplest approach?
options: Stop the production instance and copy its data disk manually
Export to CSV and import into a new instance, because cloning is not supported
Clone the Cloud SQL instance, which creates an independent copy quickly without downtime on the source
Take a snapshot of the boot disk and restore it as a new database server
explain: Cloud SQL cloning creates a new independent instance from the source, fast and without source downtime. Stopping production causes an outage, CSV export/import is slow and lossy for large databases, and boot-disk snapshots do not capture the managed database.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A Cloud SQL instance runs a retail database with peak traffic every Saturday. The team wants database maintenance (patches, updates) to happen Tuesday nights only. How should they control this?
options: Disable automatic backups, which also disables all maintenance
They cannot; Cloud SQL performs maintenance at random times
They should delete the instance every Tuesday and recreate it, which applies updates
Set a maintenance window on the instance to restrict disruptive maintenance to the chosen day and time
explain: Cloud SQL maintenance windows constrain disruptive maintenance to a preferred weekly day and hour. Maintenance is not random, recreating instances is disruptive and unnecessary, and backups are unrelated to the maintenance schedule.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: An application's database latency spikes every afternoon, and the team suspects a few slow queries but cannot identify them. Which Cloud SQL feature surfaces the top resource-consuming queries?
options: Query Insights, which shows recent and top queries with execution statistics for diagnosis
The Cloud SQL Admin API quota page, which lists slow queries by SKU
VPC Flow Logs, which capture database query text on the network
The instance's serial console output, which logs every SQL statement
explain: Query Insights provides query-level visibility (latency, rows, execution counts) to find offending queries. The quota page shows API usage, VPC Flow Logs record network connections not query text, and serial output is for VM boot diagnostics, not databases.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A nightly Cloud Scheduler job that triggers a costly batch pipeline must be paused during a week-long incident investigation, then resumed unchanged. What is the correct action?
options: Delete the job and recreate it next week, because paused jobs lose their configuration
Pause the job, which suspends executions while preserving the schedule and configuration for later resume
Delete the target Cloud Run service, which is the only way to stop invocations
Change the cron schedule to February 30th, which never occurs
explain: Cloud Scheduler jobs support pause and resume, keeping the full configuration intact. Deletion would require rebuilding the job, deleting the target is destructive overkill, and a bogus date is a hack that misfires rather than a supported control.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: During a downstream outage, a team wants to stop a Cloud Tasks queue from dispatching new tasks while keeping the already-enqueued tasks for later, then resume dispatching. What should they do?
options: Delete the queue, because tasks cannot be retained without dispatching
Purge the queue, which deletes tasks but keeps the queue configuration
Pause the queue, which halts dispatches while retaining tasks until resumed
Set the queue's rate limit to zero, which is not a supported configuration
explain: Pausing a queue stops dispatches while preserving enqueued tasks, and resuming continues where it left off. Deleting or purging destroys the tasks, and while rate limits can be lowered, pause is the explicit supported control for this scenario.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A Workflows execution failed overnight, and the engineer needs to see exactly what input it received and which step failed with what error. Where is this recorded?
options: Only in the application's own logs, because Workflows has no observability
In the Cloud Scheduler execution history, because Workflows run inside Scheduler
Nowhere; failed executions discard their inputs for privacy
In the workflow's execution history, which records each execution's input, step states, and error details
explain: Workflows retains execution records showing inputs, per-step outcomes, and errors, viewable in the console or via API. Scheduler history covers only the trigger, inputs are not discarded, and Workflows has built-in observability beyond app logs.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: Before tightening a firewall rule that could cut off a production database, an engineer wants to verify that packets from the app subnet can still reach the database VM on port 5432. Which tool performs this proactive check?
options: Connectivity Tests in Network Intelligence Center, which simulate packet paths against live configuration
VPC Flow Logs, which predict future connectivity from past traffic
Cloud Trace, which traces firewall rule evaluation in real time
The IAP TCP forwarding audit log, which pre-validates firewall changes
explain: Connectivity Tests analyze the live network configuration to predict whether packets reach their destination, ideal for pre-change validation. Flow Logs record past traffic, Cloud Trace measures request latency, and IAP audit logs record access events rather than validating rules.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A Pub/Sub subscriber falls behind every morning, and the team wants an alert when the backlog of undelivered messages grows too large. Which metric should the alerting policy watch?
options: The topic's message retention duration, which directly measures backlog size
The subscription's unacknowledged message count (or oldest unacked message age), which reflects the growing backlog
The publisher's publish rate, because subscriber lag always matches publish spikes
The BigQuery billing export, because Pub/Sub metrics are not available in Monitoring
explain: Subscription-level metrics like unacked message count and oldest unacknowledged message age directly measure backlog. Retention duration is a configuration, publish rate alone does not prove lag, and Pub/Sub metrics are fully available in Cloud Monitoring.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A Cloud Run service with a misconfigured retry loop once scaled to 1,000 instances and caused a billing scare. How can the team put a hard ceiling on instance count for cost protection?
options: Reduce the container's memory, because instance count scales with memory
Use a billing budget, which automatically stops scaling at the threshold
Set the maximum instances on the service, which caps how far it can scale out
Set the minimum instances to zero, which also limits the maximum
explain: Maximum instances is the explicit ceiling on scale-out and the right cost guardrail against runaway scaling. Minimum instances control the floor, memory affects per-instance cost not count, and budgets only alert rather than cap scaling.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: An event-driven Cloud Function processes Cloud Storage uploads, but transient downstream failures cause some files to be skipped silently. How can the team make failed invocations retry automatically?
options: Increase the function's timeout, because retries happen automatically on any timeout
Switch to HTTP triggers, which retry every failed invocation by default
Manually re-upload each failed file, because event functions never retry
Enable retry on failure for the event-driven function, so failed deliveries are redelivered
explain: Event-driven functions support a retry-on-failure setting that redelivers events after failures. Timeouts do not enable retries, HTTP functions do not retry by default, and manual re-upload is the toil that the retry setting eliminates.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: An analyst is about to run an unfamiliar BigQuery query that might scan petabytes. How can they check the estimated bytes to be billed before the query actually runs?
options: Check the table's row count, which equals the bytes billed
Enable the query cache, which reports cost before execution
Run the query and check the bill afterward, because estimates are impossible
Use bq query --dry_run, which validates the query and reports estimated bytes scanned without executing it
explain: The --dry_run flag validates syntax and returns the estimated bytes processed without running or billing the query. Running first defeats the purpose, row counts do not equal bytes scanned, and the cache does not pre-report costs.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: Finance flags a sudden BigQuery cost spike, and the team needs to identify which queries scanned the most data in the last 7 days. Which data source answers this?
options: The Cloud Billing console's SKU breakdown, which lists individual queries
INFORMATION_SCHEMA views such as JOBS, which record per-query bytes processed, user, and timestamps
VPC Flow Logs, which capture BigQuery query text
The dataset's access logs, which do not exist for BigQuery
explain: INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS exposes metadata for recent jobs including bytes billed per query, ideal for cost forensics. Billing shows SKU totals not queries, Flow Logs do not see query text, and BigQuery does have audit logging, but JOBS views are the direct source.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A compliance team needs a weekly report of every object in a Cloud Storage bucket, including sizes and storage classes, to find stale data. What is the managed way to generate this inventory?
options: Query the bucket with BigQuery directly, because buckets are queryable tables
Run gsutil ls -r every Monday and email the output manually
Enable Storage Insights inventory reports, which generate scheduled CSV/Parquet listings of bucket objects
Enable object versioning, which produces weekly inventory emails
explain: Storage Insights inventory reports produce scheduled object listings for analysis without custom scripting. Manual gsutil runs are toil, versioning keeps history but generates no reports, and buckets are not BigQuery tables.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: After a suspicious kubectl command runs against production, the team needs to find who executed it and when. Which logs record control-plane API activity for a GKE cluster?
options: Cloud Trace spans, which capture kubectl invocations automatically
The workload's application logs, which mirror control plane activity
The node's serial console output, which logs all kubectl commands
GKE control plane audit logs (Admin Activity), which record API requests including kubectl actions
explain: GKE writes control-plane audit logs recording Kubernetes API calls, attributable to identities. Serial output covers VM boot, Cloud Trace covers request latency, and application logs only show workload behavior, not who called the API.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: The on-call team lives in Slack and wants critical alert notifications delivered to a #incidents channel instead of email. What should they configure in Cloud Monitoring?
options: A Slack notification channel, which delivers alert notifications to the chosen channel
A PagerDuty webhook pointed at Slack, because Monitoring cannot notify Slack directly
An uptime check with a Slack URL, because only uptime checks support chat tools
A log sink to Slack, because notification channels do not support chat applications
explain: Cloud Monitoring notification channels natively support Slack (along with email, PagerDuty, webhooks, and others). No PagerDuty intermediary is needed, uptime checks are for probing endpoints, and log sinks route logs rather than alert notifications.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: An Artifact Registry repository accumulates hundreds of old container image tags, increasing storage costs and clutter. How can old untagged or stale images be removed automatically?
options: Delete the repository monthly and recreate it, because registries cannot prune images
Set up Artifact Registry cleanup policies, which automatically delete images matching age or keep-count rules
Enable vulnerability scanning, which also deletes old images as a side effect
Reduce the image pull frequency, because storage billing follows pull counts
explain: Cleanup policies declaratively delete images by criteria like older-than or keep-most-recent, controlling storage growth. Recreating repos is disruptive, scanning only reports vulnerabilities, and storage is billed on bytes stored, not pulls.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: Finance notices persistent disk charges for disks that may no longer be attached to any VM. Which tool proactively identifies unattached disks and other idle resources for cleanup?
options: The Cloud Asset Inventory, which deletes unattached disks on a schedule
Manual console inspection, because Google Cloud offers no idle-resource detection
The Recommender (Active Assist), which surfaces findings like idle VMs and unattached persistent disks
Cloud Billing budgets, which automatically delete idle resources at thresholds
explain: Recommender generates idle-resource findings (idle VMs, unattached disks, idle IPs) with estimated savings. Budgets only alert on spend, Asset Inventory is a read-only inventory, and manual inspection is exactly the toil Recommender eliminates.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: An alert should fire only when BOTH CPU exceeds 90% AND error rate exceeds 5% for 10 minutes; either condition alone is normal. How should the alerting policy combine the two conditions?
options: Use the OR combiner, which fires only when every condition is met
Set both thresholds on one metric, because a policy supports only one condition
Create two separate alerting policies, because conditions cannot be combined
Use the AND combiner on a single policy with both conditions, so notification requires all conditions true
explain: Alerting policies support multiple conditions joined by AND, OR, or AND/OR logic; AND requires every condition to hold. Separate policies cannot express the conjunction, OR fires when any condition holds, and a policy can hold many conditions, not one.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: An SRE team wants a Cloud Monitoring dashboard filter that shows only production VMs, defined as VMs carrying the label env=prod, across all projects in the metrics scope. What construct supports label-based grouping?
options: Uptime checks with label parameters, which double as grouping filters
Billing exports, which are the only label-aware Monitoring feature
Monitoring groups, which dynamically include resources matching label-based filters
Separate metrics scopes per label value, because groups cannot use labels
explain: Monitoring groups collect resources by criteria including labels, and dashboards and alerts can scope to a group. Metrics scopes are about project visibility, uptime checks probe endpoints rather than group resources, and labels are usable across Monitoring, not only billing.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A developer needs to briefly act as a production service account to debug a permissions issue, without being able to attach that service account to resources or manage it. Which role grants exactly this impersonation ability?
options: Service Account Token Creator, which allows impersonating the service account by creating short-lived tokens
Service Account User, which is the impersonation role for direct token creation
Service Account Admin, the least-privilege role for temporary impersonation
Project Viewer, which includes impersonation rights on all service accounts
explain: Service Account Token Creator grants impersonation via short-lived credentials, while Service Account User grants the actAs right to attach the account to resources. Service Account Admin is full management (too broad), and Viewer grants no impersonation.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A team created a Cloud KMS key ring in us-central1 but new data-residency rules require keys to live in the EU. What must they do about the existing key ring?
options: Move the key ring with gcloud kms keyrings move, because key ring locations are editable
Create a new key ring in the EU and re-encrypt with new keys, because a key ring's location is immutable after creation
Edit the key ring's location in the console, which migrates the key material automatically
Nothing; key ring location is only a label and does not constrain where keys operate
explain: A key ring's location is fixed at creation and cannot be changed, so residency changes require a new key ring and re-encryption. There is no move command, the console cannot edit location, and location genuinely constrains where key material resides.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: After a suspected key compromise, a team must immediately stop a KMS key version from decrypting anything, but keep the option to restore it if the alert proves false. Should they destroy or disable the key version?
options: Rotate the key, because rotation retroactively invalidates old versions
Destroy it, because destruction is instantly reversible within 30 days
Disable the key version, which immediately blocks its use but can be re-enabled; destruction is irreversible after its waiting period
Delete the entire key ring, which is the only way to stop a single version
explain: Disabling a key version immediately prevents its use while remaining reversible, whereas destroying schedules irreversible destruction. Destroying is not reversible, deleting the ring is overkill, and rotation only affects future encryptions, not existing versions.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: Compliance requires Pub/Sub message payloads to be encrypted with customer-managed keys held in Cloud KMS, with the team controlling rotation. What must be configured on the topic?
options: Nothing; Pub/Sub topics are always CMEK-encrypted by default
A CSEK passed with each publish call, because Pub/Sub does not support CMEK
TLS between publishers and subscribers, which satisfies the at-rest requirement
CMEK for the topic, granting the Pub/Sub service agent the Cloud KMS Encrypter/Decrypter role on the key
explain: Pub/Sub supports CMEK per topic, and the Pub/Sub service agent needs encrypter/decrypter on the key for it to work. Topics default to Google-managed keys, CSEK is not the Pub/Sub mechanism, and TLS covers only transit, not at-rest storage.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A database credential stored in Secret Manager is used by a short-lived migration job and must become automatically unusable 7 days after creation, even if the team forgets to clean it up. How can this be enforced?
options: Rely on the migration job to delete the secret, because Secret Manager has no expiry feature
Rotate the secret weekly, which also deletes old versions automatically
Store the secret in a regional replica, because regional secrets expire automatically
Set an expiration (TTL) on the secret so Secret Manager disables or destroys it automatically at the deadline
explain: Secret Manager supports expiration policies that automatically disable or destroy secrets at a set time. Depending on manual cleanup is unreliable, rotation creates new versions rather than expiring the secret, and replication scope has nothing to do with expiry.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: An internal HR application sits behind Identity-Aware Proxy, and the backend needs to know the authenticated user's email and identity reliably on each request. How does IAP pass this to the backend?
options: IAP appends the user's password to the request body for the backend to parse
IAP adds a signed JWT identity token in a header that the backend can verify to identify the user
The backend must call the IAM API on every request, because IAP passes no identity information
IAP only works for Google accounts, so identity headers are unavailable for workforce users
explain: IAP injects a signed JWT (the IAP identity assertion header) carrying the authenticated user's identity, which backends verify cryptographically. Passwords are never forwarded, no per-request IAM call is needed, and IAP supports workforce and Google identities alike.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A service account was deleted yesterday during cleanup, but the team realizes an audit trail still needs to reference it, and a replacement with the same name is needed. What is true about recovery?
options: Deleted service accounts are gone instantly and can never be recovered
Only Google support can restore service accounts, and only within 24 hours
A deleted service account can be undeleted within 30 days, restoring the same identity
The name can be reused immediately by creating a new account, with full history preserved
explain: Deleted service accounts are soft-deleted and can be undeleted within 30 days, preserving the identity and its bindings. They are not instantly gone, no support ticket is required, and a fresh account with the same name would be a different identity without the history.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A team builds an internal admin tool using Google OAuth sign-in that must be usable only by members of the company's Google Workspace domain. How should the OAuth consent screen be configured?
options: Skip the consent screen entirely, because internal apps are exempt from OAuth configuration
Set the consent screen to External, because internal tools still need external verification
Publish the app and add every employee as a test user, because user type cannot restrict by domain
Set the user type to Internal, which restricts sign-in to accounts in the organization's Workspace domain
