explain: The Internal user type limits OAuth sign-in to users within the company's Workspace organization, with no per-user allowlisting needed. External is for public apps, test users are an External-app concept, and every OAuth client needs a consent screen configuration.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: The SOC wants automatic detection of suspicious cloud activity such as a service account granted an unusually broad role at 3 AM, without writing custom detection rules. Which Security Command Center capability covers this?
options: Security Health Analytics, which only checks static misconfigurations on a schedule
Cloud Asset Inventory, which detects threats in real time
The _Default log sink, which pages the SOC automatically
Event Threat Detection, which applies Google threat intelligence to detect anomalous activity like unusual IAM grants
explain: Event Threat Detection continuously analyzes log data for malicious patterns such as anomalous grants or exfiltration. Security Health Analytics finds misconfigurations rather than active threats, Asset Inventory is a point-in-time inventory, and log sinks only route data without detection.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A GKE cluster runs sensitive workloads, and the security team wants alerts if a running container spawns an unexpected reverse shell or executes a known-malicious binary. Which detector provides this runtime signal?
options: Binary Authorization, which monitors running containers for malicious processes
Container Threat Detection, which detects runtime threats like added binaries and reverse shells in GKE workloads
Vulnerability scanning in Artifact Registry, which inspects running containers continuously
GKE audit logs, which analyze process behavior inside containers
explain: Container Threat Detection instruments GKE nodes to spot runtime attacks such as reverse shells and malicious binaries. Binary Authorization gates deployment admission rather than monitoring runtime, registry scanning checks images at rest, and audit logs record API calls, not process activity.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A noisy but benign Security Command Center finding reappears every week, and the SOC wants it suppressed automatically going forward instead of muting each occurrence manually. What should they create?
options: A log exclusion, which deletes the finding from Security Command Center
A Pub/Sub notification, which suppresses findings as a side effect
A mute rule, which automatically mutes future findings matching its criteria
A firewall rule, which prevents the finding's underlying activity
explain: Mute rules automatically suppress findings matching filters, unlike one-off manual mutes. Pub/Sub notifications only route findings, firewall rules do not manage SCC findings, and log exclusions affect log ingestion, not findings, which cannot be deleted.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A data-governance team must scan a BigQuery dataset weekly for new columns containing credit card numbers and notify the data owner when found. Which DLP feature automates this recurring inspection?
options: Manual DLP inspections, because DLP cannot schedule recurring scans
Cloud Scheduler invoking the DLP API, which is the only way to repeat inspections
BigQuery scheduled queries, which natively detect sensitive data patterns
DLP job triggers, which run scheduled inspection jobs over BigQuery tables on a recurring basis
explain: DLP job triggers natively schedule recurring inspection of BigQuery (and other) data sources with actions like Pub/Sub notifications. DLP does support scheduling, Cloud Scheduler workarounds are unnecessary, and scheduled queries do not perform sensitive-data detection.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A company worries attackers could spoof DNS responses to redirect employees from the corporate VPN portal to a phishing clone. Which DNS security control counters cache poisoning and spoofing for their Cloud DNS zone?
options: DNSSEC, which cryptographically signs DNS records so resolvers can validate authenticity
DNS peering, which encrypts responses between zones
A longer TTL on records, which prevents spoofing by caching longer
Private Google Access, which signs DNS responses automatically
explain: DNSSEC adds cryptographic signatures that let resolvers verify responses, defeating spoofing and cache poisoning. Peering connects zone namespaces without signing, longer TTLs do not authenticate anything, and Private Google Access is about API reachability, not DNS authenticity.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A company wants an egress firewall rule allowing VMs to reach only api.partner.com on HTTPS, but partner IPs change frequently. What modern firewall construct matches traffic by domain name instead of static CIDRs?
options: Network tags named after the domain, because tags resolve domain names dynamically
FQDN objects in Cloud NGFW firewall policies, which match egress traffic by fully qualified domain name
VPC Service Controls perimeters, which filter egress by domain name
Cloud DNS forwarding zones, which enforce egress firewall policy
explain: Cloud NGFW supports FQDN objects that resolve domain names for firewall matching, avoiding brittle IP lists. Network tags are static VM selectors, VPC Service Controls govern API perimeters not general egress, and DNS forwarding only routes queries rather than enforcing policy.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A team needs Google-managed TLS certificates for a load balancer that renew automatically, with domain ownership proven via DNS. Which Certificate Manager authorization type should they use?
options: Self-signed certificates uploaded manually, which renew automatically
Load balancer authorization, because DNS proofs are not supported
DNS authorization, which proves domain control via a DNS record and enables auto-renewing Google-managed certificates
No authorization is needed; Google issues certificates for any domain on request
explain: DNS authorization places a CNAME record proving domain control, after which Certificate Manager provisions and auto-renews Google-managed certificates. Self-signed certs do not auto-renew, load-balancer authorization is the alternative HTTP-based method, and authorization is always required.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: An enterprise runs its own offline root CA and wants Google's Certificate Authority Service to issue workload certificates chained to that root, without exposing the root key. How should the CAS pool be set up?
options: Use a DevOps-tier pool, which automatically chains to any external root
Create a self-signed root CA in CAS, because subordinate CAs are not supported
Upload the root private key to CAS, which is the only supported hierarchy
Create a subordinate CA in CAS whose CSR is signed by the enterprise root, keeping the root key offline
explain: CAS supports subordinate CAs: generate a CSR from CAS and have the offline root sign it, so the root key never leaves the enterprise. Self-signed roots are only one option, uploading the root key defeats the purpose, and tier names do not create external chains.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A principal holds an IAM allow binding granting storage.objects.delete on a bucket, but an IAM deny policy also denies storage.objects.delete to all principals. Can the principal delete objects?
options: Yes, because allow bindings are evaluated before deny policies
No: IAM deny policies take precedence over any allow binding, so the denial wins regardless of the grant
Yes, because the more specific bucket-level allow overrides the broader deny
No, but only because deny policies require a matching allow to take effect
explain: Deny policies are evaluated first and override allow bindings unconditionally; a denied permission is refused no matter how many allows exist. Specificity does not rescue the allow, and deny policies need no accompanying allow to be effective.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: External auditors need to review IAM policies across the organization to verify least privilege, but must not be able to modify anything or read resource data. Which predefined role fits?
options: Project Owner, because auditors need broad visibility
Security Reviewer (roles/iam.securityReviewer), which grants read access to IAM policies and related security metadata without modification rights
Project Viewer, which includes full IAM policy read access at the organization level
Organization Administrator, the standard read-only audit role
explain: The Security Reviewer role is purpose-built for inspecting IAM allow and deny policies and effective access without granting data access or modification. Owner and Organization Administrator are far too broad, and basic Viewer does not reliably expose IAM policy details.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A company tags production VMs with env=prod and wants an IAM binding that lets the backup service account read disks only on VMs carrying that tag. How can the grant be scoped to tagged resources?
options: IAM bindings cannot reference tags, so the team must create a separate project for prod VMs
Apply the role at the folder level, because folders automatically filter by tags
Add an IAM Condition on the binding matching the resource's tag (resource.matchTag), limiting the grant to tagged resources
Use a label-based condition, because tags are not visible to IAM Conditions
explain: IAM Conditions support resource.matchTag expressions, so a binding can apply only to resources carrying specific tags. Tags are fully visible to IAM Conditions (labels are not), folder-level grants do not filter by tags, and no project split is needed.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A bank must use encryption keys generated inside its own on-premises HSM with Google Cloud KMS, rather than keys generated by Google. Which KMS feature supports importing externally generated key material?
options: Customer-supplied encryption keys, which store HSM keys in Cloud KMS permanently
External Key Manager, which is the only way to use non-Google keys
Automatic rotation, which imports external keys on each rotation
Key import jobs, which allow bringing externally generated key material into Cloud KMS (BYOK)
explain: KMS import jobs (BYOK) let customers wrap and import key material generated in their own HSM. External Key Manager keeps keys outside Google entirely, rotation generates new Google-side versions, and CSEK is a per-request mechanism where Google never stores the key.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A regulator requires that encryption keys never leave the company's own key management system, yet Google Cloud services must be able to use them for encryption operations. Which option satisfies both?
options: External Key Manager (EKM), where keys stay in the external system and Google calls out for each cryptographic operation
Customer-managed keys in Cloud KMS, because the key material stays on premises
Google-managed keys with a long rotation period, which approximates external custody
CSEK, because Google stores CSEK keys only in the customer's region
explain: EKM keeps key material in the customer's external key manager (on-premises or third-party cloud) while Google invokes it over the internet or VPC for operations. CMEK stores keys in Cloud KMS, Google-managed keys are Google-held, and CSEK keys are supplied per request but are not a persistent external-custody model.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A public-facing login page behind an external Application Load Balancer is hit by distributed credential-stuffing from Tor exit nodes and known-bad IPs. Which Cloud Armor feature specifically targets this threat-intelligence signal?
options: Preconfigured WAF rules, which block Tor exit nodes by default
Cloud Armor Threat Intelligence, which can deny traffic from known malicious sources such as Tor exit nodes
Rate limiting per IP, which is the only Cloud Armor defense against botnets
VPC firewall rules, which inspect at the load balancer layer
explain: Cloud Armor Threat Intelligence feeds identify traffic from Tor exit nodes, known attackers, and scanners for blocking at the edge. WAF rules target injection payloads rather than reputation, rate limiting is complementary but not reputation-based, and VPC firewall rules do not operate at the external load balancer.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A regulated workload on GKE must keep data encrypted even while being processed in memory, protecting against compromised hypervisors or host administrators. Which node option provides this?
options: Spot node pools, which isolate workloads on dedicated memory
Private GKE clusters, which encrypt node memory by removing public IPs
Shielded GKE nodes, which encrypt memory at runtime
Confidential GKE nodes, which use confidential computing to encrypt workload memory during processing
explain: Confidential GKE nodes run on Confidential VM hardware that encrypts memory in use, protecting against host-level threats. Shielded nodes verify boot integrity but do not encrypt RAM, Spot is a pricing model, and private clusters control network reachability, not memory encryption.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A junior administrator must attach existing service accounts to new VMs but must NOT be able to create service accounts, delete them, or modify their IAM policies. Which role pairing enforces this boundary?
options: Grant Project Owner, then rely on an IAM deny policy to remove the extra rights
Grant Service Account Token Creator, which is the attachment role
Grant Service Account Admin, because it excludes attachment rights
Grant Service Account User on the service accounts, which allows attaching (actAs) without account management rights
explain: Service Account User grants the iam.serviceAccounts.actAs permission to attach an account to resources, without create, delete, or policy-management rights. Service Account Admin is full management, Owner-plus-deny is convoluted and fragile, and Token Creator governs impersonation, not attachment.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A policy requires that only container images signed by the release pipeline's KMS key may run in production GKE clusters. Beyond enabling Binary Authorization, what must exist for each deployable image?
options: A vulnerability scan report in Artifact Registry, which Binary Authorization treats as a signature
An attestation: a signed statement (created with the KMS key, e.g., via an attestor) that the image met policy, which Binary Authorization verifies at admission
A Cloud Build trigger, which automatically signs every image without configuration
A public image registry, because Binary Authorization cannot verify private images
explain: Binary Authorization enforces policy by verifying attestations, cryptographically signed statements from trusted attestors, before admitting images. Vulnerability scans inform policy but are not signatures, builds do not auto-attest without setup, and Binary Authorization works with private registries.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A finance auditor must review monthly invoices and cost breakdowns for the company's billing account but must not be able to change payment methods, budgets, or project links. Which IAM role on the billing account follows least privilege?
options: Billing Account Viewer, which grants read-only access to invoices, cost tables, and budgets
Billing Account Administrator, which can modify payment instruments and link projects
Project Owner on the company's largest project
Organization Administrator
explain: Billing Account Viewer is the read-only billing role: it lets the auditor view invoices, cost tables, and budgets without any modification rights. Billing Account Administrator can change payment methods and link or unlink projects, which exceeds the requirement. Project Owner and Organization Administrator govern projects and the organization, not billing accounts, and both grant far broader powers than read-only cost review.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: Finance wants three alerts from a single monthly budget: at 50% and 90% of actual spend, plus a 100% alert that publishes to a Pub/Sub topic for automation. How should the budget be configured?
options: Create three separate budgets, one per threshold
Create one budget with three alert threshold rules, directing the 100% rule to the Pub/Sub topic
Create three billing accounts with one budget each
Use a Cloud Scheduler job to poll billing data
explain: A single budget supports multiple alert threshold rules, each with its own threshold percentage and notification channels, so the Pub/Sub action can be attached only to the 100% rule. Separate budgets or billing accounts would fragment what is logically one budget and complicate management. Cloud Scheduler polling reimplements a native feature with unnecessary operational overhead.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An engineer creates a new project, finishes the setup, and now wants to hand administration to the platform team and remove their own access entirely. What is true about the creator's access?
options: The project creator cannot be removed from the project
Only Google Cloud support can remove the project creator
The creator automatically received the Owner role, and that binding can be removed once another Owner exists
The project must be deleted and recreated to remove the creator
explain: Whoever creates a project is automatically granted the Owner role, but it is an ordinary IAM binding that can be removed once at least one other Owner remains. There is no permanent creator lock-in and no support ticket is required. Deleting the project would destroy all resources, which is unnecessary for an access change.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: During a corporate restructuring, a project is migrated from one organization node to another. What happens to the project's link to its billing account?
options: Billing is disabled and resources stop
The project automatically links to the new organization's billing account
All billing budgets on the project are deleted
The project keeps its existing billing account link because billing accounts are not tied to organization nodes
explain: Billing accounts exist outside the resource hierarchy, so moving a project between organizations does not change its billing link and resources keep running. There is no automatic relinking to a different billing account, and budgets defined on the billing account or project are unaffected by the move.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A billing budget's alert threshold is breached. By default, who receives the email notification?
options: The Billing Account Administrators and Billing Account Users on the billing account
All Project Owners in every linked project
Only the Organization Administrator
Nobody; recipients must always be configured manually
explain: Budget alerts are emailed by default to the Billing Account Administrators and Billing Account Users on the billing account, with optional additional recipients via notification channels. Project Owners and Organization Administrators do not receive budget emails unless explicitly added. Manual recipient configuration is optional, not required, for the default billing roles to be notified.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An administrator runs gcloud services disable on an API that other enabled services depend on. What happens?
options: The API is disabled silently along with its dependents
The command fails with an error listing the dependent services that must be disabled first
The project is deleted
Billing is disabled for the project
explain: Service Usage blocks disabling a service while enabled services depend on it, returning an error that names the dependents so they can be disabled first. It never cascades silently, and disabling a service affects neither the project nor billing. This guard prevents breaking running workloads that rely on the dependency chain.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: Finance needs to download the monthly invoice PDF for the company's billing account. What is the minimum IAM role required?
options: Project Viewer on any linked project
Billing Account Creator
Billing Account Viewer on the billing account
Organization Policy Administrator
explain: Billing Account Viewer grants read access to invoices, payments, and cost data on the billing account, which is exactly what downloading an invoice needs. Billing Account Creator can create new billing accounts but does not by itself grant read access to an existing account's invoices. Project and organization roles do not reach billing account documents.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A company uses Shared VPC: the network lives in a host project while application VMs run in service projects. Where do the Compute Engine VM charges appear?
options: In the host project that owns the network
Split evenly across all service projects
In the network administrator's project
In the service project that owns each VM
explain: Costs accrue to the project that owns the resource, so VM charges land in the service project even though the subnet belongs to the host project. The host project is not charged for service-project workloads, costs are never split automatically, and the administrator's identity is irrelevant to cost attribution.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A provisioning script must enable the Cloud SQL Admin API in each new project without changing the active gcloud configuration. Which flag targets a specific project?
options: --project=PROJECT_ID appended to gcloud services enable
--zone=us-central1-a
--async
Editing the Cloud SDK configuration file by hand
explain: The global --project flag overrides the active configuration for a single command, which is the standard pattern for scripts that operate across projects. --zone selects a compute zone and is meaningless for service enablement, --async only changes polling behavior, and hand-editing config files is fragile compared to an explicit flag.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: Two days before a major product launch, an engineer requests a large Compute Engine quota increase. What should the team understand about the request?
options: Increases apply instantly and automatically
Quota increase requests are reviewed and can take several days, so they should be requested well in advance
Quotas cannot be increased ahead of launches
Increases are applied within minutes via support chat
explain: Quota increases go through a review process that can take several days, so capacity planning must happen well before the event. They are neither instant nor chat-activated, and requesting an increase ahead of a launch is both allowed and recommended. Waiting until two days before risks hitting the limit during the launch.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A new finance team member must create additional billing accounts for new subsidiaries. What do they need?
options: Project Owner on one existing project
The billing account ID of the parent company
The Billing Account Creator role and a Google payments profile
Organization Viewer
explain: Creating a billing account requires the Billing Account Creator role plus a Google payments profile to back it. Project Owner governs a single project and grants no billing-account creation rights, the parent account's ID is not a permission, and Organization Viewer is read-only.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An administrator compares the list constraint compute.vmExternalIpAccess with the boolean constraint compute.disableSerialPortAccess. What is the practical difference?
options: There is no functional difference between them
Boolean constraints apply only to Compute Engine VMs
List constraints cannot be attached to organization policies
The list constraint manages allow lists and deny lists of values, while the boolean constraint simply enforces an on/off restriction
explain: List constraints define which values are permitted or denied, such as which VM configurations may use external IPs, while boolean constraints toggle a single restriction on or off, such as disabling serial port access. Both are organization policy constraints and both can target Compute Engine; the difference is in how the restriction is expressed, not where it applies.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: During an access review, an auditor wants the complete IAM allow policy of project analytics-prod as YAML from the command line. Which command returns it?
options: gcloud projects get-iam-policy analytics-prod
gcloud iam policies list
gcloud projects describe analytics-prod
gcloud asset search-all-resources
explain: gcloud projects get-iam-policy returns the project's full allow policy including all bindings. gcloud projects describe shows metadata like the parent and lifecycle state but not IAM bindings, and there is no gcloud iam policies list command. Asset search can find resources but is not the direct way to dump a project's IAM policy.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A team uses labels for cost reporting and also wants to use them in IAM Conditions for access control, but learns labels are not supported there. Which mechanism should they use for access-control attributes?
options: More labels with stricter naming
Resource Manager tags, which are supported in IAM Conditions
Network tags on the VMs
Project name prefixes
explain: Resource Manager tags are key-value pairs designed for access control and are supported in IAM Conditions, unlike labels which are for organization and billing. Network tags only target firewall rules and routes, and name prefixes are a convention with no policy enforcement. Keeping labels for cost reporting while adding tags for access control uses each mechanism for its intended purpose.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An engineer needs the billing account ID to link a project from the CLI. Which command lists the billing accounts they can access?
options: gcloud projects list
gcloud iam roles list
gcloud billing accounts list
gcloud organizations list
explain: gcloud billing accounts list returns the billing accounts visible to the caller, including their IDs and display names. gcloud projects list shows projects, not billing accounts, and the organizations and IAM commands query different resources. The billing account ID from this list is what gcloud billing projects link expects.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: Developers must be able to create new projects inside the dev folder without being able to modify the folder's IAM policy or settings. Which role should they receive on the folder?
options: Folder Admin
Project Owner
Organization Administrator
Project Creator on the dev folder
explain: The Project Creator role granted on the folder allows creating projects inside it without administering the folder itself. Folder Admin and Organization Administrator both permit modifying folder IAM and settings, which exceeds the requirement. Project Owner applies to an existing project and grants no ability to create new projects.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A security team requires that new projects never receive the default auto-mode VPC, so engineers must create networks deliberately. Which organization policy constraint enforces this?
options: constraints/compute.skipDefaultNetworkCreation
constraints/compute.vmExternalIpAccess
constraints/compute.disableSerialPortAccess
constraints/compute.requireOsLogin
explain: compute.skipDefaultNetworkCreation prevents the automatic creation of the default network in new projects, forcing deliberate network design. vmExternalIpAccess governs external IP assignment on VMs, disableSerialPortAccess blocks the serial console, and requireOsLogin enforces OS Login -- none of them controls whether the default VPC is created.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An administrator tries to delete a decommissioned project but the operation is blocked by a lien. What must happen before the project can be deleted?
options: Disable billing on the project
Remove the lien, then delete the project
Delete every resource in the project first
File a support ticket to override the lien
explain: Liens exist specifically to block project deletion, so the lien must be explicitly removed by someone with permission before deletion can proceed. Disabling billing or deleting resources does not lift the block, and no support override is needed since lien removal is a normal IAM-controlled operation.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A budget is configured to publish alerts to a Pub/Sub topic, but no messages arrive even though the threshold was breached. The topic exists. What is the likely cause?
options: Budgets cannot publish to Pub/Sub topics
The threshold percentage is misconfigured
The topic does not grant the Pub/Sub Publisher role to the Cloud Billing service account
Billing export to BigQuery must be enabled first
explain: Budget notifications to Pub/Sub require granting the Pub/Sub Publisher role to Google's Cloud Billing service account on the topic; without it, publishing silently fails. Budgets natively support Pub/Sub notifications, so the feature itself is not the problem, and neither threshold math nor the billing export affects topic publishing permissions.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An engineer needs to run a single gcloud command as a service account for testing, without downloading its key. Which flag enables impersonation for that command?
options: --service-account-key-file
--no-user-output-enabled
--print-access-token
--impersonate-service-account=SA_EMAIL
explain: The --impersonate-service-account flag makes gcloud obtain short-lived credentials for the service account for that invocation, provided the user has the Service Account Token Creator role. A key file would require downloading a long-lived key, which the scenario forbids. --print-access-token only displays the caller's own token and does not switch identities.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A platform team wants to manage billing budgets with Terraform instead of the console. Which API must be enabled for programmatic budget management?
options: The Cloud Billing Budget API (billingbudgets.googleapis.com)
The Cloud Billing API (cloudbilling.googleapis.com)
The Service Usage API
The Cloud Resource Manager API
explain: The Cloud Billing Budget API is the dedicated API for creating and managing budgets, and it is what Terraform's budget resources call. The Cloud Billing API manages billing accounts and project linkage rather than budgets, while Service Usage and Resource Manager cover API enablement and resource hierarchy respectively.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A team wants to remove the default auto-mode VPC from a project and use only deliberately created custom networks. Is this allowed?
options: No, the default VPC is protected and cannot be removed
Yes, the default network can be deleted like any other VPC network
Only through an organization policy
Only by deleting and recreating the project
explain: The default network is an ordinary auto-mode VPC and can be deleted; many organizations do so to enforce deliberate network design. Organization policies can prevent its creation in new projects, but deletion of an existing one is a standard network operation. Deleting the project would destroy all its resources unnecessarily.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An engineer wants to confirm a project's parent folder and lifecycle state from the CLI. Which command shows this metadata?
options: gcloud projects list
gcloud compute project-info describe
gcloud projects describe PROJECT_ID
gcloud asset search-all-resources --project=PROJECT_ID
explain: gcloud projects describe returns the project's metadata including its parent resource, lifecycle state, project number, and labels. gcloud projects list shows a summary table without full detail, compute project-info covers Compute Engine metadata and quotas, and asset search is for inventory queries rather than project metadata.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A holding company has two separate billing accounts and wants a single budget covering both. What is true?
options: One budget can span multiple billing accounts
Budgets apply automatically at the organization level
Labels can merge two billing accounts into one budget
A budget is scoped to a single billing account, so two budgets are needed
explain: Every budget is scoped to exactly one billing account, so spending across two billing accounts requires two budgets. Budgets do not automatically aggregate at the organization level, and labels filter within a budget's scope rather than merging accounts.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A script needs the list of Compute Engine zones as JSON for parsing. Which flag requests JSON output from a gcloud command?
options: --format=json (or --format json)
--json-output
--output-file=out.json
--parse-json
explain: The --format flag controls gcloud output rendering, and --format=json produces machine-readable JSON for any command. The other flags do not exist; scripts that need a file should combine --format with shell redirection instead of inventing output flags.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A database team needs block storage with independently configurable IOPS and throughput beyond what persistent disks offer, for new Compute Engine VMs. Which disk family should they evaluate?
options: Standard persistent disk
Hyperdisk (Balanced or Extreme), which allows independent performance provisioning
Local SSD
A Cloud Storage bucket mounted with gcsfuse
explain: Hyperdisk is the newer persistent disk family that lets teams provision IOPS and throughput independently of capacity, with Balanced and Extreme variants for different performance needs. Standard persistent disks couple performance to size, local SSDs are ephemeral and tied to the VM's lifecycle, and Cloud Storage is object storage rather than block storage.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A legacy web application keeps session state in instance memory, so repeat requests from the same client must reach the same backend. Which load balancer feature provides this stickiness?
options: Cloud CDN caching
Autoscaling based on CPU
Session affinity using client IP or a generated cookie
Connection draining
explain: Session affinity directs requests from the same client to the same backend, using the client IP or a generated cookie, which keeps in-memory sessions working. Cloud CDN caches content rather than pinning sessions, autoscaling changes capacity rather than routing, and connection draining only affects how existing connections close during backend removal.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: Two VPCs are peered, and VMs in VPC-A must resolve private DNS names hosted in a private zone attached to VPC-B. What enables this name resolution?
options: A public Cloud DNS zone
Cloud NAT in VPC-A
A VPC firewall rule allowing DNS
A DNS peering zone in VPC-A that targets VPC-B's network
explain: DNS peering lets one VPC resolve names from a private zone authorized in another VPC, which is exactly the cross-VPC private DNS need. A public zone would expose internal names to the internet, Cloud NAT handles outbound traffic rather than DNS, and firewall rules filter packets but do not provide name resolution.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A company configures Cloud NAT in us-central1, but VMs in europe-west1 still cannot reach the internet. What is the reason?
options: Cloud NAT gateways are regional, so europe-west1 needs its own NAT configuration
Cloud NAT requires external IPs on every VM
A firewall rule is blocking Cloud NAT
Cloud NAT only works with Shared VPC
explain: Cloud NAT is a regional resource: a gateway in us-central1 only serves subnets in that region, so each region needs its own NAT gateway and router. Cloud NAT is specifically designed for VMs without external IPs, firewall rules do not block the NAT gateway itself, and it works in any VPC including Shared VPC service projects.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A SaaS provider on Google Cloud wants to expose its managed application to customer VPCs privately, with no public IPs and no VPC peering. What should the provider create?
options: A Cloud VPN gateway per customer
A Private Service Connect published service backed by a service attachment
An external passthrough Network Load Balancer
A public DNS zone for the service
explain: Private Service Connect lets a producer publish a service through a service attachment that consumers reach via private endpoints, with no peering or public IPs on either side. Per-customer VPNs add operational overhead, an external load balancer exposes the service to the internet, and DNS alone provides no private connectivity.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: VMs in a custom-mode VPC subnet cannot reach the internet even though Cloud NAT is configured. The subnet's route table has no 0.0.0.0/0 route. What is the fix?
options: Assign an external IP to each VM
Create a VPC firewall rule allowing egress
Add a default route for 0.0.0.0/0 with the default internet gateway as the next hop
Enable Private Google Access on the subnet
explain: Without a default route, packets for the internet have nowhere to go, and Cloud NAT only translates traffic that is already routed toward it. Adding the 0.0.0.0/0 route with the default internet gateway next hop restores the path. External IPs would bypass NAT unnecessarily, firewall rules filter rather than route, and Private Google Access only reaches Google APIs, not the public internet.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: Developers need to connect to a Cloud SQL instance from laptops with changing home IP addresses, without opening broad authorized networks. Which approach is recommended?
options: Assign the instance a public IP and share the database root password
Add 0.0.0.0/0 to authorized networks
A dedicated Cloud VPN tunnel per developer
The Cloud SQL Auth Proxy, which opens a secure tunnel authenticated with IAM
explain: The Cloud SQL Auth Proxy establishes an encrypted tunnel to the instance using the developer's IAM credentials, avoiding IP allowlisting entirely. Sharing root passwords or opening 0.0.0.0/0 exposes the database to the internet, and per-developer VPNs add heavy operational overhead for a problem the proxy solves natively.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A team must synchronize a local directory of website assets to a Cloud Storage bucket, uploading only new or changed files. Which command does this efficiently?
options: gcloud storage rsync --recursive local-dir gs://bucket/
gcloud storage cp --recursive local-dir gs://bucket/
gcloud storage buckets create gs://bucket/
gcloud compute scp --recurse local-dir vm:/tmp
explain: gcloud storage rsync compares source and destination and transfers only new or changed files, making repeated syncs fast. gcloud storage cp would re-upload everything each run, buckets create only provisions the bucket, and compute scp copies to a VM rather than Cloud Storage.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A team hardened a VM's boot disk and wants to stamp out many identical VMs from it. What should they create from the disk?
options: A snapshot schedule on the disk
A custom image from the boot disk, then an instance template referencing it
A new machine type
A Cloud Storage bucket with the disk contents
explain: A custom image captures the boot disk into a reusable, bootable template, and an instance template referencing it lets managed instance groups stamp out identical VMs. A snapshot schedule only automates backups rather than producing a bootable template, machine types define CPU and memory rather than disk contents, and a bucket cannot boot a VM.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A GKE Deployment's pods saturate CPU during traffic spikes but sit mostly idle at night. Which Kubernetes mechanism adjusts the replica count automatically based on CPU utilization?
options: The cluster autoscaler
The Vertical Pod Autoscaler
The Horizontal Pod Autoscaler
Node auto-provisioning
explain: The Horizontal Pod Autoscaler scales the number of pod replicas up and down based on observed metrics such as CPU utilization, matching capacity to demand. The cluster autoscaler and node auto-provisioning adjust node count rather than pod replicas, and the Vertical Pod Autoscaler adjusts per-pod resource requests rather than replica counts.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A private GKE cluster's control plane should be administrable only from the corporate office's public IP range. Which setting restricts control-plane endpoint access?
options: A VPC firewall rule on the nodes
Enabling private nodes
Workload Identity
Control plane authorized networks
explain: Control plane authorized networks restrict which source CIDR ranges can reach the Kubernetes API server, which is exactly the office-only administration requirement. VPC firewall rules govern node traffic rather than the control plane endpoint, private nodes control node IPs rather than API access, and Workload Identity governs pod-to-Google-API authentication.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: An App Engine standard application suffers latency spikes when new instances start because initialization happens on the first user request. Which feature loads application code before live traffic arrives?
options: Warmup requests, which App Engine issues to new instances before routing live requests
Traffic splitting between versions
Firewall rules blocking abusive IPs
Minimum idle instances alone
explain: Warmup requests give new instances a chance to load code and initialize before they receive user traffic, eliminating cold-start latency spikes. Traffic splitting divides traffic between versions rather than warming instances, firewall rules filter attackers rather than improving startup, and idle instances keep capacity warm but do not preload application code on newly created instances.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A Cloud Run service must reach a Memorystore Redis instance that has only an internal IP address. What connects the serverless service to the VPC?
options: Assigning an external IP to the Redis instance
A Serverless VPC Access connector attached to the service
Cloud NAT
IAP TCP forwarding
explain: A Serverless VPC Access connector bridges Cloud Run to the VPC so the service can reach internal IPs such as Memorystore. Giving Redis a public IP would expose the cache to the internet, Cloud NAT provides outbound internet access rather than VPC ingress, and IAP TCP forwarding is for human administrative access rather than service-to-service traffic.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A media rendering farm needs a shared NFS file system with very high throughput for hundreds of simultaneous clients. Which Filestore service tier is designed for this scale?
options: Basic HDD
Basic SSD
High Scale SSD
Enterprise
explain: Filestore High Scale SSD is built for throughput-intensive workloads with hundreds of clients, far beyond the Basic tiers. Basic HDD and Basic SSD suit smaller general-purpose shares, and Enterprise targets high availability with replication rather than maximum scale-out throughput.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A team wants a Cloud Scheduler job to publish a message to a Pub/Sub topic every hour as a fan-out trigger. Which Scheduler target type should the job use?
options: HTTP
App Engine HTTP
Compute Engine instance metadata
Pub/Sub
explain: Cloud Scheduler natively supports Pub/Sub targets, publishing the configured message body to the topic on schedule with no intermediary service. HTTP targets would require a publicly reachable endpoint to receive the call, and App Engine HTTP targets only invoke App Engine services rather than publishing messages.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A team wants Pub/Sub to reject malformed event messages at publish time based on a defined structure. Which feature enforces message structure?
options: Pub/Sub schemas using Avro or Protocol Buffers with message validation
Dead-letter topics
Ordering keys
Exactly-once delivery
explain: Schemas define the expected message structure in Avro or Protocol Buffers, and Pub/Sub validates published messages against the schema, rejecting malformed ones. Dead-letter topics handle undeliverable messages rather than validating structure, ordering keys sequence messages, and exactly-once delivery addresses duplicate processing.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A team loads daily staging tables into BigQuery and wants them automatically deleted after 7 days to control storage cost. What should they set?
options: A Cloud Scheduler job that drops old tables
Default table expiration on the dataset so new tables expire automatically
Partitioning by ingestion date
A Cloud Storage lifecycle rule
explain: Dataset default table expiration automatically deletes tables a set time after creation, which handles the daily staging-table churn with no ongoing work. A Scheduler job reimplements native functionality, partitioning organizes data rather than deleting tables, and Cloud Storage lifecycle rules apply to objects rather than BigQuery tables.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A compliance policy requires Cloud SQL instance data to be encrypted with customer-managed keys. What must be configured on the instance?
options: Nothing; Cloud SQL only supports Google-managed encryption
A VPC firewall rule
A customer-managed encryption key (CMEK) from Cloud KMS assigned to the instance
TLS certificates on the database clients
explain: Cloud SQL supports customer-managed encryption keys from Cloud KMS, giving the customer control over key lifecycle while Google still performs the encryption. The claim that only Google-managed keys are supported is false, firewall rules filter network traffic rather than encrypting data, and TLS protects data in transit rather than data at rest.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A company serves non-HTTP, TLS-encrypted traffic globally and wants Google to terminate TLS at the edge with centrally managed certificates. Which load balancer fits?
options: External passthrough Network Load Balancer
Internal Application Load Balancer
Global external Application Load Balancer
External proxy Network Load Balancer using an SSL proxy
explain: The external proxy Network Load Balancer with an SSL proxy terminates TLS at Google's edge for non-HTTP TCP traffic and supports Google-managed certificates. The passthrough variant preserves encryption end to end without terminating it, the Application Load Balancer only handles HTTP(S), and the internal variant is not internet-facing.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: After deploying updated images to a Cloud Storage origin behind Cloud CDN, users still receive stale cached copies. What forces the edge caches to fetch fresh content?
options: Cache invalidation for the affected paths
Deleting and recreating the bucket
Changing the bucket's storage class
Disabling Cloud CDN entirely
explain: Cache invalidation explicitly evicts the stale objects from edge caches so the next request fetches the updated origin content. Recreating the bucket or changing storage class does not purge cached copies, and disabling Cloud CDN would remove caching benefits for all content rather than refreshing specific paths.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A mobile game must read a player's current balance and then update the balance and inventory documents atomically. Which Firestore feature guarantees all-or-nothing updates with consistent reads?
options: Two separate set() calls in sequence
Firestore transactions, which provide atomic read-write operations
Real-time listeners on the documents
TTL policies on the collections
explain: Firestore transactions perform reads and writes atomically, so the balance check and both updates either all commit or all fail. Sequential set() calls can partially succeed and leave inconsistent state, listeners only observe changes, and TTL policies delete old documents rather than coordinating writes.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A Cloud Tasks queue must invoke an authenticated Cloud Run service. How should the tasks authenticate to the service?
options: Embed a service account key in each task payload
Open the Cloud Run service to unauthenticated invocations
Configure the HTTP target with an OIDC token minted from a service account
Share the developer's personal credentials with the queue
explain: Cloud Tasks supports OIDC tokens on HTTP targets, letting the queue authenticate as a service account without handling keys. Embedding keys or sharing personal credentials creates long-lived secrets to protect and rotate, while opening the service to unauthenticated traffic abandons access control entirely.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A company wants the same hostname to resolve to EU backends for European users and Asian backends for Asian users. Which Cloud DNS feature enables location-based answers?
options: DNS peering zones
Forwarding zones
Private DNS zones
Routing policies with geolocation routing
explain: Cloud DNS routing policies support geolocation-based responses, returning different answers for the same name depending on the resolver's location. Peering and forwarding zones control where queries are resolved rather than varying answers by geography, and private zones serve internal names rather than steering public traffic.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: After ordering Dedicated Interconnect, what must be configured to connect a specific VPC to the interconnect connection?
options: A VLAN attachment (interconnect attachment) on the VPC
A Cloud VPN tunnel
A Cloud NAT gateway
A VPC firewall rule
explain: A VLAN attachment logically connects a VPC to the Dedicated Interconnect connection, carrying the private traffic between on-premises and Google Cloud. Cloud VPN is a separate encrypted-over-internet product, Cloud NAT provides outbound internet for private VMs, and firewall rules filter traffic rather than establishing the interconnect link.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A Cloud Run job processes nightly files but occasionally fails on transient downstream errors. How can failed task executions be retried automatically?
options: They cannot be retried; jobs run exactly once
Configure the job's max retries so failed tasks are retried automatically
Convert the workload to a Cloud Run service
Add a second Cloud Scheduler job as a backup
explain: Cloud Run jobs support a configurable maximum retry count, so tasks that fail on transient errors are retried without manual intervention. Jobs are not strictly run-once, converting to a service changes the execution model unnecessarily, and a duplicate scheduler job would double-process files rather than retrying failures.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: An administrator's workstation cannot reach a VM's external IP directly, but IAP TCP forwarding is permitted. Which gcloud flag tunnels the SSH session through IAP?
options: --no-tunnel
--zone=us-central1-a
--tunnel-through-iap
--plain-text
explain: The --tunnel-through-iap flag on gcloud compute ssh routes the SSH connection through Identity-Aware Proxy TCP forwarding, working even when the VM has no reachable public IP. --zone only selects the VM's zone, and the other flags do not exist. The VM still needs the IAP firewall allowance, but the client side needs no direct network path.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A team investigates a performance regression from two months ago in Cloud Monitoring, but the metric data is no longer available. What is the retention limit for metric data?
options: 13 months
1 year
400 days
6 weeks
explain: Cloud Monitoring retains metric data for 6 weeks, so investigations older than that need data exported elsewhere, such as a metrics sink to BigQuery. The longer retentions listed belong to other systems: 400 days is the _Required audit log bucket, not metrics. Planning around this limit avoids surprises during post-incident reviews.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: Compliance requires Cloud Logging log buckets to be encrypted with customer-managed keys. What can be configured on a log bucket?
options: CMEK encryption for the log bucket using a Cloud KMS key
Nothing; log buckets only support Google-managed encryption
Customer-supplied encryption keys (CSEK) per log entry
TLS certificates on the logging agents
explain: Log buckets support customer-managed encryption keys from Cloud KMS, giving the customer control over key rotation and destruction. The claim that only Google-managed keys are available is false, CSEK is a Cloud Storage concept rather than a Logging one, and TLS protects data in transit rather than stored logs.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: Before a critical launch, a team wants to verify that their VMs survive host maintenance through live migration. Which command simulates a maintenance event on a running VM?
options: gcloud compute instances reset
gcloud compute instances simulate-maintenance-event
gcloud compute instances stop
gcloud compute instances delete
explain: simulate-maintenance-event triggers the same live-migration path as real host maintenance, letting the team validate their workload beforehand. Reset, stop, and delete are destructive or disruptive operations that test nothing about maintenance behavior and would cause the very downtime the team wants to avoid.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: Compliance requires Admin Activity logs from every project in the organization aggregated into one central log bucket. What should be created?
options: A separate sink in each project pointing at the bucket
A longer retention on every project's _Default bucket
An aggregated sink at the organization (or folder) level
A new folder for each project
explain: Aggregated sinks created at the organization or folder level automatically capture logs from all current and future child projects into one destination. Per-project sinks require ongoing maintenance as projects are added, retention alone does not centralize anything, and folders organize resources rather than routing logs.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A team deletes an old snapshot that newer snapshots were based on. What happens to the newer snapshots?
options: They are deleted automatically as well
They become corrupt and unusable
The delete is blocked until the newer ones are deleted
Nothing; snapshots are logically independent, so the newer ones remain fully usable
explain: Snapshot dependencies are logical rather than physical chains, so deleting an older snapshot never affects newer ones. There is no cascade deletion, no corruption, and no blocking -- each snapshot remains a complete, restorable point-in-time copy regardless of what happens to snapshots created before or after it.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A Cloud Build pipeline is CPU-bound and builds are slow. Which build configuration option provides more compute for the build steps?
options: Setting a higher-performance machine type (such as N1_HIGHCPU_8) in the build config
Increasing the build timeout
Adding more build triggers
Using a private worker pool only
explain: The machineType field in the build configuration selects larger build VMs, directly addressing CPU-bound builds. Raising the timeout only allows slow builds to run longer without failing, additional triggers multiply builds rather than speeding them, and private pools provide network access rather than more CPU.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A Cloud Scheduler job's HTTP target occasionally returns 500 errors. How can the scheduler automatically retry failed executions?
options: It cannot; failed executions must be retriggered manually
Configure retry settings (maximum retry attempts and backoff) on the job
Create a duplicate job as a fallback
Replace the job with a Cloud Tasks queue
explain: Cloud Scheduler jobs support retry configuration with backoff, so transient 500s are retried automatically. Manual retriggering adds operational burden, a duplicate job would double-fire rather than retry failures, and Cloud Tasks is a different service suited to application-driven task dispatch rather than cron scheduling.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A Cloud Run service throws unhandled exceptions in production. Where do these automatically appear, grouped by root cause and counted?
options: Cloud Trace
VPC Flow Logs
Error Reporting
Cloud Build history
explain: Error Reporting automatically captures unhandled exceptions from serverless platforms including Cloud Run, grouping identical stack traces and counting occurrences. Cloud Trace follows request latency rather than exceptions, Flow Logs record network packets, and Build history covers CI/CD runs rather than runtime errors.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A repository holds frontend and backend code, but the backend Cloud Build trigger should fire only when backend files change. How should the trigger be scoped?
options: Split the code into two repositories
Use manual builds only
Filter by branch name only
Configure included files with glob patterns on the trigger
explain: Build triggers support included-files (and ignored-files) glob filters, so the backend trigger fires only when matching paths change. Splitting repositories is a heavyweight reorganization for a filtering problem, branch filters cannot distinguish directories, and manual builds abandon automation entirely.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: An alerting policy must evaluate CPU utilization across all VMs carrying the label env=prod as a single group. How should the policy scope the metric?
options: Use a monitoring group filtered by the env=prod label as the alert scope
Create one alerting policy per VM
Use an uptime check per VM
Use a log-based metric
explain: Monitoring groups collect resources by criteria such as labels, and alerting policies can evaluate the group's aggregate metrics as one scope. Per-VM policies multiply maintenance effort, uptime checks probe endpoints rather than CPU metrics, and log-based metrics derive from log entries rather than system metrics.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A VM's data disk is 90% full. The team wants more space without stopping the VM. What can they do?
options: Nothing; attached disks cannot be resized
Resize the persistent disk while it is attached, then grow the filesystem in the guest OS
Only snapshots can be resized, not live disks
Create a new VM with a larger disk and migrate
explain: Persistent disks support online growth: the disk can be resized while attached and in use, followed by a filesystem resize inside the guest to use the new space. Disks cannot shrink, which is why the operation is grow-only, and migrating to a new VM would cause the very downtime the team wants to avoid.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A team wants to test a new Cloud Run revision with internal traffic before shifting production traffic to it. How can the revision be addressed directly?
options: Deploy a second Cloud Run service
Send traffic to the latest revision only
Assign a revision tag, which provides a direct URL for that revision
Use gradual traffic splitting immediately
explain: Revision tags give a specific revision its own URL, so internal testers can validate it without affecting the production traffic split. A second service duplicates configuration and cost, latest-only routing cannot isolate the new revision, and immediate traffic splitting sends real user traffic before testing is complete.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A team wants to run SQL queries over recent logs without building a BigQuery sink. Which feature enables SQL directly on log buckets?
options: The Logs Explorer query language only
A BigQuery sink is mandatory for SQL
Exporting logs to Cloud Storage
Log Analytics on an upgraded log bucket
explain: Log Analytics, enabled by upgrading a log bucket, allows SQL queries directly against stored logs with no sink required. The Logs Explorer uses its own query language rather than SQL, a BigQuery sink is one valid path but not mandatory, and Cloud Storage exports produce flat files rather than a queryable SQL interface.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A disk fills steadily and the team wants an alert three days before it is projected to fill, based on the growth trend. Which alerting condition type predicts this?
options: A metric forecast condition, which alerts when the trend projects a threshold breach
A metric absence condition
An uptime check
A log-based metric
explain: Forecast conditions use trend analysis to predict when a metric will cross a threshold within a configurable window, enabling proactive alerts days ahead. Metric absence fires when data stops arriving rather than predicting growth, uptime checks probe endpoints, and log-based metrics count log entries rather than forecasting metric trends.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A fleet of VMs must all have the same monitoring package installed and pinned to a specific version. Which VM Manager feature enforces this package state across the fleet?
options: Patch management
OS policies (guest policies) that declare the desired package state
Startup scripts on each VM
VPC firewall rules
explain: OS policies declaratively enforce package installation, version, and removal across fleets, converging non-compliant VMs automatically. Patch management applies OS updates on a schedule rather than pinning specific packages, startup scripts run once at boot and do not enforce ongoing state, and firewall rules filter network traffic rather than managing software.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A Deployment Manager deployment manages a production database that must survive even if the deployment itself is deleted. Which setting preserves the database?
options: The default deletion behavior
Deleting the database first
Setting the resource's deletion policy to ABANDON
Removing the database from the YAML template
explain: The ABANDON deletion policy tells Deployment Manager to leave the resource in place when the deployment is deleted, protecting the database. The default policy deletes managed resources with the deployment, pre-deleting the database defeats the purpose, and editing the YAML does not change what deletion does to already-managed resources.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A team wants distributed traces that include custom application operations, not just automatic HTTP spans. What should they add to their services?
options: More log statements
Larger machine types
A Cloud Monitoring dashboard
Instrumentation with OpenTelemetry (or Cloud Trace client libraries) creating custom spans
explain: OpenTelemetry instrumentation and the Cloud Trace client libraries let code create custom spans around application operations, enriching traces beyond automatic HTTP instrumentation. Logs record events but do not join the trace timeline, larger VMs do not add observability, and dashboards visualize metrics rather than capturing spans.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: New GKE pods are stuck in the Pending state. Which command shows the scheduler events explaining why they cannot be placed?
options: kubectl get events (optionally sorted by creation timestamp)
kubectl get nodes
gcloud logging read
kubectl logs
explain: kubectl get events surfaces cluster events including the scheduler's reasons for not placing pods, such as insufficient CPU or unsatisfiable affinity. kubectl get nodes shows node inventory without the scheduling rationale, and kubectl logs requires a running container, which Pending pods do not have.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: During a regional outage drill, the team promotes a cross-region Cloud SQL read replica. What does promotion do to the replica?
options: It deletes the original primary instance
It converts the replica into an independent, read-write standalone instance
It creates a backup of the replica
It enables high availability on the replica
explain: Promoting a read replica detaches it from the primary and converts it into a standalone read-write instance that can serve production traffic. The original primary is untouched, no backup is created by the operation, and high availability is a separate configuration rather than a result of promotion.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: An engineer wants the current traffic allocation and latest ready revision of a Cloud Run service from the CLI. Which command shows this?
options: gcloud run revisions list
kubectl get services
gcloud run services describe SERVICE
gcloud builds list
explain: gcloud run services describe returns the service's full configuration including traffic allocation across revisions and the latest ready revision. revisions list shows revision history without the traffic split, kubectl targets GKE clusters rather than Cloud Run, and builds list covers Cloud Build runs.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A Pub/Sub subscriber may be offline for up to 3 days, and its messages must not be lost. What should be configured on the subscription?
options: Nothing; Pub/Sub retains messages indefinitely
A dead-letter topic
Ordering keys
A message retention duration covering the outage (up to 7 days by default)
explain: Subscriptions retain unacknowledged messages for a configurable duration, 7 days by default, so a 3-day outage is covered without message loss. Retention is not indefinite, dead-letter topics handle repeatedly undeliverable messages rather than offline subscribers, and ordering keys sequence messages rather than extending retention.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: An engineer tries to delete the _Default log bucket to reduce ingestion costs. What happens?
options: The _Default bucket cannot be deleted; use exclusion filters or routing to control cost
The bucket is deleted immediately
Cloud Logging is disabled for the project
Ingestion billing stops but historical logs remain
explain: The _Default and _Required log buckets are system-protected and cannot be deleted; cost control comes from exclusion filters that drop unwanted logs before ingestion or sinks that route logs elsewhere. Deleting the bucket is not possible, logging cannot be disabled by this path, and billing continues for ingested logs.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: Docker image builds in Cloud Build are slow because every layer rebuilds from scratch. Which feature caches image layers between builds?
options: Increasing the build timeout
Kaniko cache, which stores and reuses previously built layers
Adding more build triggers
Using a private worker pool
explain: The Kaniko executor's cache option persists image layers between builds so unchanged layers are reused, dramatically speeding up Docker builds. Longer timeouts only prevent failures without accelerating anything, more triggers increase build volume, and private pools address network access rather than layer caching.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A team must monitor a non-HTTP TCP service, such as a database port, from outside the VPC. Which uptime check type works?
options: An HTTP check
A content-matching check
A TCP check against the port
A metric absence alert
explain: Uptime checks support TCP checks that verify a port accepts connections, which suits non-HTTP services like databases. HTTP and content checks require an HTTP response the service does not speak, and metric absence alerts on missing monitoring data rather than probing the endpoint.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: Analysts must run queries against a BigQuery dataset but must not create datasets or manage IAM. Which role combination follows least privilege?
options: BigQuery Admin on the project
Project Editor
BigQuery Data Viewer on the dataset only
BigQuery Data Viewer on the dataset plus BigQuery Job User on the project
explain: Running a query requires both data access (BigQuery Data Viewer on the dataset) and the bigquery.jobs.create permission (BigQuery Job User on the project) to execute the query job. Data Viewer alone cannot run jobs, while BigQuery Admin and Project Editor grant far broader powers including dataset and IAM management.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: An application service account needs to read the payload of one specific secret. Which role grants exactly that access?
options: Secret Manager Secret Accessor on the secret
Secret Manager Admin on the project
Project Viewer
Cloud KMS CryptoKey Decrypter
explain: Secret Manager Secret Accessor grants permission to access secret payloads and can be scoped to a single secret, matching the requirement precisely. Secret Manager Admin can manage all secrets including deletion, Project Viewer is read-only across the project without secret payload access, and the KMS decrypter role applies to encryption keys rather than secrets.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A developer needs to view Cloud SQL instances and connect to them, but must not administer instances. Which predefined role fits?
options: Cloud SQL Admin
Cloud SQL Client
Cloud SQL Instance User
Project Owner
explain: Cloud SQL Client grants the ability to view instances and connect to them without instance administration rights. Cloud SQL Admin can create and delete instances, Instance User is specifically for IAM database authentication logins rather than general viewing, and Project Owner is far broader than needed.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A company wants Kubernetes RBAC in GKE tied to Google Groups so that group membership controls cluster access. Which feature enables this?
options: Workload Identity
Binary Authorization
Google Groups for RBAC
Private clusters
explain: Google Groups for RBAC integrates Google Workspace or Cloud Identity groups with Kubernetes RBAC, so adding or removing someone from a group changes their cluster access. Workload Identity maps Kubernetes service accounts to Google service accounts, Binary Authorization governs image admission, and private clusters control network exposure rather than identity.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: After creating a GKE cluster, an engineer's kubectl commands fail to authenticate. What configures kubectl to use the cluster's credentials?
options: gcloud auth login
Manually editing the kubeconfig file
gcloud compute ssh to a node
gcloud container clusters get-credentials CLUSTER --zone=ZONE
explain: gcloud container clusters get-credentials fetches the cluster's credentials and writes them to kubeconfig, which is the standard way to authenticate kubectl. gcloud auth login authenticates the user to Google Cloud generally but does not configure cluster access, manual kubeconfig editing is error-prone, and SSHing to a node does not set up local kubectl.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: An internal application behind IAP must be reachable only from the corporate office's public IP range. How can this be enforced in IAM?
options: An IAM Condition on the IAP-secured Web App User binding restricting request.ip to the office CIDR
A VPC firewall rule
Cloud NAT
A billing budget
explain: IAM Conditions support the request.ip attribute, so the IAP role binding can be limited to the office's public IP range regardless of which valid user signs in. VPC firewall rules filter network traffic but cannot express per-user IAM decisions, Cloud NAT handles outbound traffic, and budgets are unrelated to access control.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: After a key-leak scare, the team must inventory all user-managed keys for a service account. Which command lists them?
options: gcloud iam service-accounts describe
gcloud iam service-accounts keys list SA_EMAIL
gcloud auth list
gcloud kms keys list
explain: gcloud iam service-accounts keys list enumerates the user-managed keys on a service account so each can be audited or rotated. describe shows the account's metadata without its keys, auth list shows the caller's own credentials, and kms keys list covers Cloud KMS keys rather than service account keys.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: Compliance requires secrets in Secret Manager to be encrypted with customer-managed keys. What must be configured?
options: Nothing; Secret Manager only supports Google-managed encryption
Customer-supplied encryption keys (CSEK) on every API call
A customer-managed encryption key (CMEK) from Cloud KMS on the secret
A VPC Service Controls perimeter around the project
explain: Secret Manager supports CMEK, letting the customer control key lifecycle for secret encryption at rest. The claim of Google-managed-only encryption is false, CSEK is a Cloud Storage mechanism rather than a Secret Manager one, and a service perimeter restricts data movement rather than changing the encryption key.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A service account was accidentally deleted yesterday. What is true about recovering it?
options: It is permanently gone and must be recreated
Only Google Cloud support can restore it
It can be recovered only from a backup
Deleted service accounts can be undeleted within 30 days
explain: Deleted service accounts remain recoverable for 30 days via the undelete operation, restoring the account with its original identity and bindings. Immediate recreation would produce a new identity that does not inherit the old bindings, and no support ticket or external backup is required within the recovery window.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A VPC Service Controls perimeter must allow the corporate office's IP range to reach protected resources while blocking everything else. Which mechanism defines these source conditions?
options: Access levels, which express conditions such as IP ranges and device attributes
VPC firewall rules
IAM allow policies
Budget alerts
explain: Access levels define conditions like source IP ranges that permit requests to cross the perimeter, which is exactly the office-only requirement. VPC firewall rules govern VM network traffic rather than service perimeters, IAM allow policies grant permissions rather than network conditions, and budgets are unrelated to access.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A team wants to test a new Cloud Armor WAF rule against production traffic without blocking legitimate requests. How should they evaluate it safely?
options: Deploy the rule directly and watch for complaints
Enable preview mode on the rule so matches are logged without being enforced
Disable the security policy during the test
Test with a VPC firewall rule instead
explain: Preview mode evaluates the rule against live traffic and logs what would have been blocked without enforcing the action, allowing safe tuning. Deploying directly risks false-positive outages, disabling the policy removes all protection, and firewall rules operate at the network layer rather than testing WAF expressions.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A team enables automatic rotation on a Cloud KMS key. What happens to data encrypted with the previous key version?
options: It becomes unreadable immediately
It is automatically re-encrypted with the new version
It remains decryptable; new encryptions use the new primary version
The old key version is destroyed on rotation
explain: Rotation creates a new primary key version for future encryptions while previous versions remain available for decryption, so existing data keeps working. Nothing is re-encrypted automatically, old versions are not destroyed, and destroying a version still in use would cause data loss -- which is why versions persist until explicitly destroyed.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A security team wants to prevent users from uploading their own public keys to service accounts, allowing only Google-generated keys. Which organization policy constraint enforces this?
options: constraints/iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation
constraints/compute.requireOsLogin
constraints/iam.allowServiceAccountCredentialLifetime
constraints/iam.disableServiceAccountKeyUpload
explain: iam.disableServiceAccountKeyUpload specifically blocks uploading user-provided public keys while still permitting Google-generated keys. disableServiceAccountKeyCreation blocks key creation entirely including Google-generated keys, which is stricter than required, while the OS Login and credential-lifetime constraints address unrelated concerns.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: The SOC wants to tag Security Command Center findings with internal ticket IDs for tracking. Which feature adds custom metadata to findings?
options: Security marks
Muting findings
Notification configs
Log sinks
explain: Security marks let teams attach custom key-value metadata, such as ticket IDs, to findings for workflow tracking. Muting suppresses findings rather than annotating them, notification configs route findings to Pub/Sub, and log sinks export logs rather than enriching findings.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security
