explain: Cloud Asset Inventory's search-all-resources queries resource metadata across the whole organization in one command, including network interfaces. gcloud compute instances list is scoped to a single project, projects list shows projects rather than VMs, and Logging searches log entries instead of current inventory.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A developer's local Python app uses Application Default Credentials, but API calls fail with quota errors even though the target project has quota available. What is the likely fix?
options: Run gcloud auth login again to refresh the user credentials
Enable the API in the developer's personal project
Set a quota project with gcloud auth application-default set-quota-project
Download a service account key for the application
explain: User-based ADC has no billing or quota project attached by default, so quota-attributed API calls fail until set-quota-project designates one. Re-authenticating does not attach a quota project, enabling the API elsewhere misses the cause, and downloading keys works against least privilege.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A team is tempted to build production automation on a gcloud beta command. What is the documented risk of doing so?
options: Beta commands require a paid support plan to run
Beta features are pre-GA and may change or break without notice
Beta commands cannot be scripted in non-interactive shells
Beta features are only available in Cloud Shell
explain: Beta release track features are pre-general-availability, so their flags and behavior can change without the stability guarantees of GA commands. They run without special support plans, work fine in scripts, and are available in any SDK installation with the components installed.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An auditor needs read-only access to resources in every project in the organization, including projects created in the future. Where should the role be granted?
options: At the organization level, so inheritance carries it to all current and future projects
On each existing project individually, repeated for new projects
On the billing account, which covers all linked projects
In each project's VPC firewall rules
explain: IAM policies inherit downward, so a grant at the organization level automatically covers every current and future child project and folder. Per-project grants require constant upkeep, billing accounts govern billing rather than resource access, and firewall rules filter traffic rather than granting IAM visibility.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An engineer needs to list all service accounts in the current project from the command line. Which command does this?
options: gcloud auth list
gcloud projects get-iam-policy
gcloud compute instances list
gcloud iam service-accounts list
explain: gcloud iam service-accounts list enumerates the project's service accounts and their emails. gcloud auth list shows signed-in user identities, get-iam-policy shows role bindings rather than accounts, and compute instances list shows VMs.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: Before granting it, an engineer wants to see exactly which permissions are bundled in the predefined role roles/compute.viewer. Which command shows this?
options: gcloud iam service-accounts get-iam-policy roles/compute.viewer
gcloud iam roles describe roles/compute.viewer
gcloud projects list --filter=roles/compute.viewer
gcloud auth print-access-token roles/compute.viewer
explain: gcloud iam roles describe prints a role's title, description, and included permissions. The other commands inspect service account policies, list projects, or mint tokens, and none of them describe a role's permission set.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A VM's attached service account holds the correct IAM roles, yet the application on the VM gets permission errors calling Google Cloud APIs. What should be checked?
options: Whether the project's billing account is in good standing
Whether the organization policy allows the API
The VM's access scopes, which can block API calls regardless of IAM roles
Whether the service account key has expired
explain: Access scopes are a legacy per-VM gate that can deny API access even when IAM grants the permission; Google recommends the broad cloud-platform scope with IAM as the real control. Billing standing does not produce permission errors, org policies rarely gate API calls this way, and attached service accounts do not use expiring keys.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A team wants to add a time-based IAM Condition to an Editor role binding. What is true?
options: Conditions cannot be added to basic roles; use a predefined or custom role instead
Conditions work on basic roles but require policy version 1
Conditions on basic roles apply only at the organization level
Basic roles support conditions only for service accounts
explain: Google Cloud does not support IAM Conditions on the basic roles (Owner, Editor, Viewer), so the time restriction must be attached to a predefined or custom role binding. Policy version 3 is what enables conditions generally, and the limitation concerns the role type rather than the level or principal.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: Finance wants each month's budget to automatically track what was actually spent the previous month, without manually updating the amount. How can the budget be configured?
options: Set the budget amount to zero and rely on forecast alerts
Create a new budget manually on the first of each month
Scope the budget to the billing account's credit balance
Set the budget amount to last month's spend
explain: Billing budgets support using the prior month's actual spend as the budget amount, so the target tracks reality automatically. A zero amount alerts constantly, manual recreation adds toil, and credit balances are not a budget baseline.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: Google adds a new permission to the predefined Storage Object Viewer role. What happens to projects that already grant this role?
options: Nothing changes until an administrator re-applies the role
The new permission is automatically included, because Google manages predefined roles
The role is converted to a custom role to preserve its old definition
All existing bindings are revoked pending re-approval
explain: Predefined roles are Google-managed, so permission updates flow to every existing binding automatically. No re-application is needed, roles are never silently converted to custom, and bindings are not revoked by role updates, which is also why custom roles exist for frozen permission sets.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An engineer must create a new project already placed inside the dev folder, rather than at the organization root. Which flag does this?
options: gcloud projects create my-proj --organization=dev
gcloud projects move my-proj --folder=dev
gcloud projects create my-proj --folder=FOLDER_ID
gcloud resource-manager folders create --project=my-proj
explain: The --folder flag on gcloud projects create places the project under the specified folder at creation time, using the folder's numeric ID. The --organization flag takes an organization ID rather than a folder name, projects move is a separate operation after creation, and folders create makes folders rather than placing projects.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: After migrating every project out, an administrator tries to delete the now-empty organization resource. What happens?
options: Organization resources cannot be deleted
The organization is deleted after a 30-day recovery window
The organization can be deleted by the Organization Administrator
The organization is deleted automatically once empty
explain: Google Cloud does not support deleting an organization resource; it persists as the root of the hierarchy even when empty. There is no recovery-window deletion flow for organizations, and no role grants a deletion capability that does not exist.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A developer authenticated with gcloud auth login and wants their local client libraries to reuse those same user credentials as Application Default Credentials. Which flag does this?
options: gcloud auth login --no-launch-browser
gcloud config set auth/adc true
gcloud iam service-accounts keys create --adc
gcloud auth login --update-adc
explain: The --update-adc flag writes the authenticated user credentials into the ADC file that client libraries discover automatically. The no-launch-browser flag only changes the auth flow for headless machines, there is no such config property, and creating a service account key is the discouraged alternative.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A company needs a Google Cloud organization node for centralized IAM and policy management, with no other Google Workspace needs. Which is the most cost-effective identity setup?
options: Google Workspace Business, which is required for any organization
Cloud Identity Premium, the minimum edition for organizations
Cloud Identity Free, which supports creating an organization node
No identity product is needed; organizations work with consumer Gmail accounts
explain: Cloud Identity Free provides the managed domain needed to create an organization node at no cost. Neither Workspace nor the Premium edition is required for this, and consumer Gmail accounts cannot anchor an organization.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: From the command line, an engineer needs the project's common instance metadata and quota information in one view. Which command provides this?
options: gcloud projects describe PROJECT_ID
gcloud compute project-info describe
gcloud compute instances describe --all
gcloud info --project
explain: gcloud compute project-info describe returns project-level Compute Engine metadata, including common instance metadata and quotas. projects describe shows resource-manager metadata rather than compute quotas, and the other two commands do not exist in that form.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A network appliance VM must forward packets between subnets, which requires IP forwarding enabled on the instance. Which organization policy constraint centrally gates whether VMs can be created with IP forwarding?
options: constraints/compute.vmCanIpForward
constraints/compute.vmExternalIpAccess
constraints/compute.disableSerialPortAccess
constraints/compute.requireOsLogin
explain: The vmCanIpForward list constraint controls which projects or instances may enable IP forwarding. vmExternalIpAccess governs external IPs rather than forwarding, the serial port constraint controls console access, and requireOsLogin governs SSH identity management.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A team wants to run a KVM-based hypervisor inside Compute Engine VMs for testing. Which organization policy constraint must permit this?
options: constraints/compute.disableSerialPortAccess
constraints/compute.vmExternalIpAccess
constraints/compute.requireOsLogin
constraints/compute.disableNestedVirtualization, which must not be enforced
explain: Nested virtualization is gated by the disableNestedVirtualization boolean constraint, so it must be left unenforced for KVM-in-VM scenarios. The serial port, external IP, and OS Login constraints govern unrelated settings and do not affect hypervisor capability.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: During an access review, an auditor needs to find every IAM binding granting the Owner role anywhere in the organization, from the command line. Which command does this?
options: gcloud projects get-iam-policy for each project in a loop
gcloud iam roles describe roles/owner
gcloud asset search-all-iam-policies scoped to the organization
gcloud logging read on Admin Activity logs
explain: Cloud Asset Inventory's search-all-iam-policies searches allow policies across the organization in a single query. Looping get-iam-policy is slow and error-prone, roles describe shows permissions rather than bindings, and audit logs show changes rather than current effective grants.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An automation pipeline needs its own dedicated identity in the project. Which command creates a new service account?
options: gcloud auth activate-service-account --create
gcloud iam service-accounts create SA_NAME --display-name="Pipeline"
gcloud projects create --service-account
gcloud iam roles create --service-account
explain: gcloud iam service-accounts create provisions a new service account identity in the project. activate-service-account authenticates as an existing account, projects create makes projects rather than accounts, and roles create defines custom roles.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: Finance wants cost attribution by department across 60 projects without labeling every individual resource. What is the most efficient approach?
options: Apply department labels to the projects themselves; project labels appear in the billing export
Create one billing account per department
Rename each project with a department prefix
Export billing data and manually tag rows in a spreadsheet
explain: Projects support labels, and project labels flow into the billing export, so one label per project attributes all of its spend. Separate billing accounts fragment invoicing, renaming projects changes nothing in billing data, and manual tagging does not scale.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A script must call an IAP-protected web application as the currently signed-in user, passing an OIDC identity token in the request. Which command mints that token?
options: gcloud auth print-access-token
gcloud iam service-accounts keys create
gcloud auth application-default print-access-token
gcloud auth print-identity-token
explain: gcloud auth print-identity-token returns an OIDC identity token for the active user account, which is what IAP expects. print-access-token mints an OAuth access token for API calls rather than identity assertions, and creating service account keys is unnecessary and discouraged here.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A high-performance computing workload is CPU-bound and needs the highest per-core performance available on Compute Engine. Which machine family should be selected?
options: E2, the cost-optimized general-purpose family
C2 or C3, the compute-optimized families built for CPU-intensive workloads
M3, the memory-optimized family
A2, the accelerator-optimized family without GPUs attached
explain: Compute-optimized machine types (C2/C3) offer the highest per-core performance for CPU-bound workloads like HPC. E2 is cost-optimized with lower sustained performance, M3 targets memory-heavy workloads, and A2 is designed around attached GPUs.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A Cloud Run service should be reachable only from resources inside the VPC and from other Google Cloud services, never directly from the public internet. Which ingress setting enforces this?
options: Ingress set to all, with a firewall rule blocking the public IP
Ingress set to all, relying on IAM to reject anonymous callers
Ingress set to internal, restricting traffic to VPC and internal sources
Ingress set to internal, which also blocks Cloud Scheduler
explain: The internal ingress setting limits the service to traffic from the VPC, other Google Cloud services, and authorized internal sources, with no public endpoint. Firewall rules do not apply to Cloud Run's managed ingress, IAM alone still leaves a public endpoint, and internal ingress does not block legitimate internal callers like Scheduler.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A Cloud Run service uses Serverless VPC Access, and compliance requires ALL of its outbound traffic, including internet destinations, to flow through the VPC for inspection. Which egress setting is needed?
options: Route all traffic through the VPC connector (egress = all-traffic)
Keep the default private-ranges-only egress setting
Assign the service a public IP address
Disable the VPC connector for external destinations
explain: Setting VPC egress to all-traffic sends every outbound request through the connector into the VPC, where inspection and controls apply. The default private-ranges-only mode sends internet traffic directly out, Cloud Run services do not get public IPs, and disabling the connector removes VPC access entirely.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: An App Engine standard service has bursty traffic with long idle periods, and the team wants instances to scale to zero when idle. Which scaling type should be configured?
options: Manual scaling with one resident instance
Basic scaling, which keeps instances warm indefinitely
Automatic scaling with min_instances set to 5
Automatic scaling, which can scale standard environment instances to zero
explain: Automatic scaling in the standard environment scales instances to zero during idle periods and spins them up on demand. Manual scaling keeps fixed instances running, basic scaling does not scale to zero, and setting min_instances to 5 forces five instances to stay resident.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: An App Engine application has separate services for the web frontend and the API, and requests to api.example.com/* must route to the API service. Which configuration file defines this routing?
options: cron.yaml
dispatch.yaml
app.yaml of the default service only
queue.yaml
explain: dispatch.yaml defines URL-based routing rules that direct requests to specific App Engine services. cron.yaml schedules tasks, queue.yaml configures task queues, and a single app.yaml describes one service rather than cross-service routing.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: An App Engine application needs a cleanup task to run every hour without any external scheduler. Which App Engine configuration provides this?
options: A Cloud Scheduler job targeting the app's public URL
A startup script in app.yaml
cron.yaml, which defines scheduled tasks for the application
A warmup request handler
explain: cron.yaml declares scheduled tasks that App Engine runs on the defined schedule with no external components. Cloud Scheduler is the external alternative rather than the native answer, startup scripts run once per instance boot, and warmup requests only prepare instances for traffic.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: GKE pods are frequently OOM-killed or wasting memory because their resource requests were guessed at deploy time. Which Kubernetes mechanism automatically adjusts container resource requests based on observed usage?
options: The Vertical Pod Autoscaler, which recommends and applies right-sized requests
The Horizontal Pod Autoscaler, which changes replica counts
The cluster autoscaler, which adds or removes nodes
PodDisruptionBudgets, which control voluntary evictions
explain: The Vertical Pod Autoscaler analyzes historical usage and adjusts CPU and memory requests, recreating pods as needed to right-size them. The Horizontal Pod Autoscaler scales replica counts, the cluster autoscaler manages node counts, and PodDisruptionBudgets govern availability during disruptions rather than sizing.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A GKE cluster has a GPU node pool, but general workloads keep landing on the expensive GPU nodes. How can the team reserve those nodes for GPU workloads only?
options: Delete the GPU node pool when it is not in use
Set the GPU nodes to use Spot VMs
Increase the GPU pods' CPU requests
Apply a taint to the GPU nodes and add matching tolerations only to GPU workloads
explain: Taints repel pods that lack the matching toleration, so only GPU workloads scheduled with the toleration land on GPU nodes. Deleting the pool removes capacity entirely, Spot pricing does not control scheduling, and CPU requests do not steer pods away from specific nodes.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A team is deploying an internal Application Load Balancer, which requires a dedicated subnet for its Envoy proxies. Which subnet purpose should they select?
options: PRIVATE_RFC_1918, the purpose for regular workload subnets
REGIONAL_MANAGED_PROXY, the proxy-only subnet purpose for load balancer proxies
PRIVATE_NAT, the purpose for NAT gateway subnets
PRIVATE_SERVICE_CONNECT, the purpose for published service subnets
explain: Envoy-based load balancers require proxy-only subnets with the REGIONAL_MANAGED_PROXY purpose to host their proxies. Regular workload subnets cannot host the proxies, while the NAT and Private Service Connect purposes serve entirely different functions.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: Analysts across regions query one shared BigQuery table, but each analyst must see only rows belonging to their own region. Which native feature enforces this?
options: Column-level security with policy tags
Separate datasets per region
Row-level security with a row access policy filtering on the region column
Authorized views per analyst
explain: Row-level security applies a filter predicate so each query only returns rows the caller's group is entitled to, enforced by BigQuery itself. Column-level security hides columns rather than rows, separate datasets duplicate data and management, and per-analyst views multiply maintenance.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A team needs to restore a Firestore database to its state at any minute within the last 7 days after an accidental bulk delete. Which feature enables this?
options: Point-in-time recovery, which retains a 7-day change history for minute-level restores
Scheduled daily backups, which restore to midnight boundaries
Exporting collections to Cloud Storage hourly
Firestore TTL policies on documents
explain: Firestore point-in-time recovery keeps seven days of history and restores the database to any minute in that window. Scheduled backups only capture daily snapshots, manual exports add operational overhead, and TTL policies delete documents rather than recovering them.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A subscriber should receive only the Pub/Sub messages carrying the attribute region=eu, ignoring everything else on the topic. How should this be configured?
options: Publish eu messages to a separate topic
Acknowledge and discard non-eu messages in the subscriber
Enable exactly-once delivery on the subscription
Add a subscription filter matching attributes.region="eu"
explain: Subscription filters evaluate message attributes server-side and deliver only matching messages, so the subscriber never sees the rest. A separate topic duplicates publishing logic, client-side discarding wastes delivery and processing, and exactly-once delivery addresses duplicates rather than filtering.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A datacenter must migrate 500 TB to Cloud Storage, but its internet uplink is only 100 Mbps. Which offline option handles this?
options: Storage Transfer Service over the public internet
Transfer Appliance, a high-capacity device shipped to Google with the data
gsutil rsync with parallel transfers
A Cloud VPN tunnel with increased bandwidth
explain: Transfer Appliance is the offline bulk-ingest device for hundreds of terabytes where network transfer is impractical. Storage Transfer Service and gsutil still traverse the slow uplink, and a VPN tunnel does not raise the physical uplink's capacity.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: An engineer copies 50,000 small files to Cloud Storage and the transfer is very slow because files upload one at a time. Which flag parallelizes the operation?
options: gsutil -q for quiet mode
gsutil -u to specify a quota project
gsutil -m for multi-threaded parallel operations
gsutil -r for recursive copy
explain: The -m flag enables multi-threaded, parallel transfers so many small files move concurrently. Quiet mode only suppresses output, -u designates a quota project, and -r recurses directories without adding parallelism.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A GKE cluster's pods and services need their own IP ranges (alias IPs) from the subnet. What must the subnet provide?
options: Secondary IP ranges reserved for pods and services
A larger primary CIDR range only
A second subnet in another region
External IP addresses for every pod
explain: GKE uses alias IPs drawn from the subnet's secondary ranges, one range for pods and one for services. Enlarging only the primary range leaves no pod or service space, another region's subnet does not attach to this cluster's subnet, and pods do not receive external IPs.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A company needs private, dedicated connectivity to Google Cloud but has no presence in a colocation facility with Google peering. Which option fits?
options: Dedicated Interconnect, which requires the company's own colocation equipment
Cloud VPN, which provides dedicated private bandwidth
Carrier Peering, which is for public Google services
Partner Interconnect through a supported service provider
explain: Partner Interconnect delivers private connectivity via a partner's existing infrastructure, requiring no colocation presence of your own. Dedicated Interconnect needs your equipment in a peering facility, Cloud VPN runs over the public internet, and Carrier Peering targets public services rather than VPC connectivity.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A Bigtable cluster faces unpredictable traffic spikes, and the team wants nodes added and removed automatically based on CPU utilization. Which feature does this?
options: Manual node changes through the console
Bigtable autoscaling, which adjusts node count against CPU targets
Replication to a second cluster
Switching the storage type from SSD to HDD
explain: Bigtable autoscaling adds or removes nodes automatically to hold CPU utilization near the configured target. Manual changes do not react to spikes, replication improves availability rather than elasticity, and storage type affects cost and latency rather than node count.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: Compliance requires that data traveling between the application and its Memorystore for Redis instance be encrypted in transit. Which setting meets this?
options: Private service access, which encrypts automatically
A larger Redis tier
Transit encryption enabled on the Memorystore instance
Customer-managed encryption keys on the VPC
explain: Memorystore for Redis offers a transit encryption setting that encrypts client-to-instance traffic with TLS. Private service access provides private connectivity rather than encryption, tier size affects capacity, and CMEK on the VPC does not encrypt the Redis protocol traffic.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A legacy TCP application inside the VPC needs load balancing that preserves client source IPs, with backends addressed by internal IPs only. Which load balancer fits?
options: Internal passthrough Network Load Balancer
Global external Application Load Balancer
External proxy Network Load Balancer
Cloud DNS round robin
explain: The internal passthrough Network Load Balancer distributes TCP/UDP traffic within the VPC while preserving client source IPs. The external options expose backends to the internet, and DNS round robin lacks health checking and true load distribution.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: An HPC workload needs jumbo frames to reduce packet-processing overhead between VMs. What can be configured on the VPC network?
options: Enable Cloud NAT with jumbo frame support
Create a firewall rule allowing large packets
Attach GPUs to the VMs
Set the VPC's maximum transmission unit (MTU) to 8896
explain: VPC networks support raising the MTU to 8896 bytes for jumbo frames, reducing per-packet overhead for throughput-heavy workloads. Cloud NAT does not change frame sizes, firewall rules filter rather than resize packets, and GPUs are unrelated to networking.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: An analytics workload performs folder-level renames and listings over billions of objects, and flat bucket namespaces make these operations slow. Which bucket feature optimizes this?
options: Object versioning
Hierarchical namespace, which organizes objects into folders as first-class entities
Dual-region replication
Requester Pays
explain: Hierarchical namespace gives buckets a true folder hierarchy so folder operations like renames execute efficiently at scale. Versioning retains old object copies, dual-region improves availability, and Requester Pays shifts download billing, while none of them accelerate folder-level operations.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A team must run scheduled Apache Spark batch jobs without provisioning or managing Dataproc clusters. Which option fits?
options: A Dataproc cluster with autoscaling node pools
Dataflow with Spark templates
Dataproc Serverless for Spark, which runs jobs without cluster management
GKE with manually installed Spark
explain: Dataproc Serverless executes Spark batch workloads on managed infrastructure with no clusters to create, size, or maintain. An autoscaling cluster still requires cluster lifecycle management, Dataflow is a different processing engine, and self-installed Spark on GKE is fully manual.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A Cloud Run service needs private access to a Memorystore instance, but the team does not want to create or manage a Serverless VPC Access connector. Which connectivity option should they use?
options: Cloud NAT with a static IP
Direct VPC egress from Cloud Run
A public IP on the Memorystore instance
VPC peering between Cloud Run and the VPC
explain: Direct VPC egress lets Cloud Run send traffic into the VPC without provisioning a connector. Cloud NAT provides outbound internet rather than VPC routing, Memorystore has no public IP option, and Cloud Run does not participate in VPC peering.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A Cloud Run service suffers slow container initialization during cold starts, delaying the first request. Which setting allocates extra CPU specifically during startup?
options: Increasing max instances
Setting concurrency to 1
Enabling CPU throttling
Startup CPU boost
explain: Startup CPU boost grants additional CPU during container initialization so cold starts complete faster, then returns to the configured allocation. Max instances caps scale rather than speeding startup, concurrency 1 limits request parallelism, and CPU throttling restricts rather than boosts CPU.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A team must tune a Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL instance's max_connections setting. How should this be configured?
options: Set a database flag on the instance
SSH into the instance and edit postgresql.conf
Use a Cloud Storage lifecycle rule
Modify the instance's maintenance window
explain: Cloud SQL exposes supported server settings as database flags that can be set per instance without host access. Customers cannot SSH into the managed database hosts, lifecycle rules manage object storage, and maintenance windows control update timing rather than configuration.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A team wants to extract request latencies from application logs into a Cloud Monitoring metric that supports percentile calculations. Which log-based metric type should they create?
options: A distribution metric, which records values into histogram buckets for percentile math
A counter metric, which only counts matching log entries
An uptime check on the log bucket
A custom metric written directly by the application
explain: Distribution log-based metrics bucket extracted numeric values so Cloud Monitoring can compute percentiles and heatmaps. Counter metrics only count occurrences, uptime checks probe endpoints rather than parsing logs, and rewriting the app to emit custom metrics is unnecessary when the data already exists in logs.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: An SRE needs an alerting policy on the ratio of 5xx responses to total requests, which requires dividing one metric by another. Which Cloud Monitoring query language supports this?
options: PromQL, which only queries Prometheus data
The Logs Explorer query language
Cloud Trace query syntax
Monitoring Query Language (MQL), which supports ratio and arithmetic across metrics
explain: MQL expresses arithmetic and ratios across time series, enabling error-ratio alerting directly in Cloud Monitoring. PromQL here applies to Google-managed Prometheus data with different syntax, Logs Explorer queries log entries rather than metrics, and Trace has no metric-ratio alerting.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A team wants a new instance template rolled out to 10% of a managed instance group's VMs first, with the remainder updated only after validation. Which update approach does this?
options: A rolling update replacing all instances at once
A canary update targeting a fixed percentage of instances first
An opportunistic update with no proactive rollout
Deleting the group and recreating it
explain: MIG canary updates apply the new template to a configured fraction of instances so the change can be validated before the full rollout. A standard rolling update progresses through the whole group, opportunistic updates wait for manual instance recreation, and deleting the group causes an outage.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A retailer must guarantee that no Cloud SQL maintenance occurs during the December holiday freeze. Which setting enforces this?
options: A longer automated backup retention
A maintenance window set to December
A deny maintenance period covering the freeze dates
Disabling automated backups for December
explain: Deny maintenance periods block Google-initiated maintenance during the specified dates, which is exactly the freeze requirement. Maintenance windows choose preferred timing rather than forbidding dates, backup retention is unrelated to maintenance scheduling, and disabling backups reduces recoverability.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A team wants to see packet loss and latency between Google Cloud regions over the past week to diagnose cross-region slowness. Which tool shows this?
options: The Network Intelligence Center Performance Dashboard
VPC Flow Logs for one subnet
Cloud Trace
The Cloud Billing reports
explain: The Performance Dashboard visualizes Google-measured network latency and packet loss between regions over time. VPC Flow Logs show per-connection records for one VPC rather than aggregate inter-region health, Trace follows application requests rather than network paths, and billing reports contain no network performance data.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A team wants a Cloud Build pipeline to start whenever a message arrives on a Pub/Sub topic carrying artifact metadata. Which trigger type should they create?
options: A GitHub push trigger
A Cloud Scheduler cron trigger
A manual gcloud builds submit
A Pub/Sub trigger on the topic
explain: Cloud Build supports triggers that fire on Pub/Sub messages, starting builds from event metadata. GitHub triggers respond to repository events, Scheduler triggers are time-based, and manual submit requires a human or script invocation rather than reacting to the topic.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: Compliance requires application logs kept for exactly one year with a guarantee that no administrator can shorten the retention afterward. How should the log bucket be configured?
options: Set a 365-day retention that any admin can edit later
Create the bucket with a locked 365-day retention policy
Export the logs to Cloud Storage instead
Rely on the default _Default bucket retention
explain: A locked retention policy on a log bucket prevents anyone, including administrators, from reducing the retention period, satisfying the immutability requirement. An unlocked retention can be shortened at any time, Cloud Storage exports move rather than lock the bucket policy, and the _Default bucket retains only 30 days.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A critical bastion VM must be protected from accidental deletion through the console or gcloud. Which setting provides this?
options: An organization policy constraint
A lien on the VM
Deletion protection enabled on the instance
Removing all IAM roles from administrators
explain: The deletionProtection flag on a Compute Engine instance blocks delete calls until it is explicitly disabled, guarding against accidents. Organization policies constrain configuration rather than deletion of single VMs, liens apply at the project level, and stripping admin roles breaks legitimate administration.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: An alerting policy must dynamically target all current and future VMs carrying the label env=prod, without updating the policy when VMs change. Which feature defines this dynamic membership?
options: A Cloud Monitoring group based on the label
A Google Cloud folder named prod
A static list of instance names in the policy
A Pub/Sub topic per environment
explain: Monitoring groups evaluate label-based membership dynamically, so policies targeting the group automatically follow fleet changes. Folders organize projects rather than monitoring targets, static name lists require constant maintenance, and Pub/Sub topics carry messages rather than defining alert scope.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A Cloud Deploy release promoted to production is causing errors, and the team must return to the previously deployed release quickly. What should they do?
options: Delete the Cloud Deploy pipeline
Manually edit the Kubernetes manifests
Promote the faulty release again
Roll back the release to the previous revision in Cloud Deploy
explain: Cloud Deploy supports rolling back a release, redeploying the prior known-good revision through the managed pipeline. Deleting the pipeline destroys the delivery setup, manual edits bypass the pipeline's controls and history, and re-promoting the faulty release repeats the problem.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: Critical alerts must POST to an internal incident webhook that requires HTTP basic authentication. How should the notification channel be configured?
options: An email channel forwarded to the webhook
A webhook notification channel with basic auth credentials configured
A Pub/Sub channel with the password in the message
An SMS channel to the on-call phone
explain: Cloud Monitoring webhook channels natively support basic authentication credentials for the POST request. Email cannot POST to a webhook, embedding passwords in Pub/Sub messages exposes secrets unnecessarily, and SMS delivers text rather than invoking the endpoint.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A log sink routes to BigQuery, and analysts want the tables partitioned by date for cheaper, faster queries. How should the sink be configured?
options: Create a new sink for each day
Route to Cloud Storage instead of BigQuery
Enable partitioned tables on the BigQuery sink destination
Increase the log bucket retention
explain: Log sinks support writing to date-partitioned BigQuery tables, which prunes query scans to relevant days. Daily sinks multiply management overhead, Cloud Storage loses SQL queryability, and retention controls storage duration rather than table layout.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A Cloud Run job must process 1,000 files with up to 50 running in parallel. How should the job be configured?
options: Set tasks to 1000 and parallelism to 50
Set max instances to 1000
Create 50 separate Cloud Run services
Set concurrency to 1000 on a Cloud Run service
explain: Cloud Run jobs use tasks for total work items and parallelism for how many run concurrently, matching this requirement exactly. Max instances caps service scaling rather than defining job work, separate services add pointless overhead, and service concurrency governs requests per instance rather than batch task counts.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A company must guarantee VM capacity in us-central1-a for a product launch event, even during a regional capacity crunch. What should they create in advance?
options: A snapshot schedule for the launch VMs
A larger quota request on launch day
Spot VMs for the launch workload
A Compute Engine reservation holding the required capacity
explain: Reservations hold specific capacity in a zone so it is available when needed, protecting against stock-outs during crunches. Snapshots back up disks rather than reserving capacity, quota increases permit usage without guaranteeing physical capacity, and Spot VMs are preemptible rather than guaranteed.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: Before a risky schema migration tonight, the DBA wants an immediate full backup without waiting for the automated backup window. What should they trigger?
options: A persistent disk snapshot of the VM
An on-demand backup of the Cloud SQL instance
A Cloud Storage lifecycle rule
A new read replica
explain: Cloud SQL supports on-demand backups taken immediately, independent of the automated schedule, which is ideal before risky changes. Disk snapshots apply to Compute Engine disks rather than managed Cloud SQL, lifecycle rules manage object storage, and a read replica copies data without creating a restorable backup.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: After a suspicious kubectl command ran against production, the team needs the GKE API server audit trail. Where is it available?
options: In the node's serial port output
In VPC Flow Logs
In Cloud Logging, where GKE control plane logs are collected
In the Cloud Billing export
explain: GKE writes control plane component logs, including API server audit events, to Cloud Logging. Serial output shows VM boot messages, Flow Logs record network packets, and billing data contains no API audit trail.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A team's Cloud Build jobs run with broad default permissions, violating least privilege. How should builds be constrained?
options: Configure the builds to use a custom service account with only the required permissions
Disable the Cloud Build API
Run builds as the developer's user account
Store a service account key in the repository
explain: Cloud Build can execute with a specified least-privilege service account instead of the default one, scoping every build step. Disabling the API stops all builds, user credentials do not belong in automation, and committed keys are a serious security risk.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A workload needs full Linux compatibility on Cloud Run, including mounting a Filestore NFS volume. Which execution environment supports this?
options: The first-generation execution environment
Cloud Run functions
App Engine standard
The second-generation execution environment
explain: The second-generation execution environment provides fuller Linux compatibility, including NFS volume mounts and direct VPC egress. The first-generation environment lacks these capabilities, Cloud Run functions are event-driven rather than service-based, and App Engine standard is a different platform.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A developer wants to build a container image from local source immediately, without committing or pushing to a repository. Which command does this?
options: gcloud container clusters create
gcloud builds submit --tag IMAGE
gcloud builds triggers run
kubectl apply -f build.yaml
explain: gcloud builds submit uploads local source and runs a Cloud Build immediately, tagging the resulting image. Cluster creation provisions GKE rather than building, triggers run executes an existing trigger, and kubectl applies Kubernetes manifests rather than building images.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A team wants a recurring breakdown of request latency distribution across their services without writing custom queries. Which Cloud Trace feature provides this?
options: Log-based metrics on trace IDs
Uptime checks with content matching
Trace analysis reports summarizing latency distribution
Cloud Profiler flame graphs
explain: Cloud Trace analysis reports automatically summarize latency distributions from sampled traces, requiring no query authoring. Log-based metrics count log entries rather than analyzing traces, uptime checks probe endpoints, and Profiler shows CPU and memory hotspots rather than request latency.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A VM must be relocated from us-central1-a to us-central1-b with its configuration intact. Which command performs this zonal move?
options: gcloud compute instances move VM_NAME --zone=us-central1-a --destination-zone=us-central1-b
gcloud compute instances update VM_NAME --zone=us-central1-b
gcloud compute disks snapshot followed by manual recreation
gcloud compute instances reset VM_NAME
explain: gcloud compute instances move relocates a VM between zones within the same region, preserving its configuration. There is no zone-changing update command, snapshot-based recreation is manual toil by comparison, and reset only reboots the VM in place.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: An engineer needs an interactive shell inside a running GKE pod to inspect its filesystem during an incident. Which command opens it?
options: kubectl get pod -o yaml
kubectl drain the node
gcloud compute ssh to the node
kubectl exec -it POD_NAME -- /bin/sh
explain: kubectl exec runs a command, here an interactive shell, inside the pod's container. get pod shows metadata rather than a shell, draining evicts pods instead of inspecting them, and SSHing to the node reaches the host rather than the container.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: An unresponsive VM must be power-cycled, but the team wants to keep its ephemeral external IP address. Which action should they take?
options: Stop and then start the VM
Reset the VM
Delete and recreate the VM
Suspend and resume the VM
explain: Resetting a VM performs a hard reboot in place, preserving its ephemeral IP, disks, and metadata. Stop/start may release the ephemeral external IP, deleting destroys the instance, and suspend is for pausing with memory state rather than recovering an unresponsive VM.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: After a downstream bug corrupted processed data, the team must replay Pub/Sub messages that were already acknowledged. Which subscription setting makes this possible?
options: Message ordering on the topic
A longer acknowledgement deadline
Retain acknowledged messages on the subscription
Exactly-once delivery
explain: Retaining acknowledged messages keeps them available for seek-based replay even after acknowledgement. Ordering controls delivery sequence, the acknowledgement deadline governs redelivery timing, and exactly-once delivery prevents duplicates rather than preserving history.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A managed instance group update only changes instance metadata, so the team wants VMs restarted rather than replaced. Which update setting controls how disruptive the update may be?
options: The minimal action (most disruptive allowed action), set to restart instead of replace
The max surge setting
The autohealing policy
The instance template's machine type
explain: The update policy's minimal action setting bounds how disruptive an update can be, so RESTART refreshes instances without replacing them. Max surge controls extra capacity during updates, autohealing reacts to health check failures, and the machine type does not govern update behavior.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A contractor's role binding must apply only to Cloud Storage buckets whose names start with finance-. How can this be enforced in IAM?
options: Create a folder for each bucket
Use a separate project per bucket
Add an IAM Condition on resource.name matching the prefix
Grant the role at the organization level
explain: IAM Conditions can evaluate resource.name with a prefix match, scoping the binding to finance-* buckets. Folders and projects are coarse boundaries that do not filter by name, and an organization-level grant would broaden rather than narrow access.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: Developers keep forgetting to specify customer-managed keys, leaving new resources on Google-managed encryption. Which feature automatically provisions CMEKs for resources?
options: Cloud KMS Autokey, which creates keys on demand for supported resources
A billing budget alert on unencrypted resources
Manual key rotation schedules
Default Google-managed encryption, which is already CMEK
explain: Autokey automatically creates and assigns customer-managed keys when supported resources are created, closing the gap left by manual key selection. Budget alerts notify on spend rather than encryption, rotation schedules manage existing keys, and Google-managed encryption is by definition not customer-managed.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: An application faces a novel Layer 7 DDoS attack with no known signature for WAF rules. Which Cloud Armor feature uses machine learning to detect and mitigate it?
options: Preconfigured WAF rules for SQL injection
A manually written rate-limit rule
Geo-based blocking of countries
Adaptive Protection, which learns baseline traffic and flags anomalies
explain: Adaptive Protection applies ML to traffic baselines to detect anomalous Layer 7 attack patterns and can suggest or auto-deploy mitigations. Preconfigured WAF rules match known payloads, manual rate limits need known thresholds, and geo-blocking filters by origin rather than detecting novel attacks.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A company serves content through Cloud CDN and wants WAF and rate-limiting enforced at the edge, close to users. Which policy type should they attach?
options: A VPC firewall rule
A Cloud Armor edge security policy on the backend service
An organization policy constraint
A hierarchical firewall policy
explain: Edge security policies apply Cloud Armor protections at Google's edge for CDN-served backends. VPC firewall rules govern VM traffic rather than the CDN edge, organization policies constrain resource configuration, and hierarchical firewalls filter network traffic rather than providing WAF.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A firewall rule must apply to every VM running as the backend service account, regardless of network tags that change frequently. How should the rule target the VMs?
options: By network tag, updated whenever tags change
By IP address range of the subnet
By service account, so the rule follows the identity
By applying it to the entire VPC with no targets
explain: VPC firewall rules can target service accounts, so membership follows the VM's identity even as tags change. Tag-based targeting requires constant tag upkeep, subnet ranges are too broad, and untargeted rules apply VPC-wide rather than to the backend set.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: Compliance requires VPC Flow Logs enabled on every subnet in the organization, including subnets created in the future. Which control enforces this centrally?
options: The organization policy constraint compute.requireVpcFlowLogs
A VPC firewall rule
A billing budget
An IAM deny policy on subnets
explain: The requireVpcFlowLogs boolean constraint mandates flow logs on all current and future subnets hierarchy-wide. Firewall rules filter traffic rather than enabling logging, budgets track spend, and IAM deny policies restrict permissions rather than enforcing logging configuration.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: VPC-A is peered with VPC-B, and VPC-B learns on-premises routes through its Cloud Router. How can VPC-A also learn those on-premises routes?
options: Create a second Cloud VPN tunnel from VPC-A
Rely on transitive routing through the peering
Add a static route on every VM in VPC-A
Enable custom route export on VPC-B's peering and import on VPC-A's peering
explain: Peered VPCs exchange custom (dynamic) routes only when export is enabled on the source peering and import on the receiving one. Peering is non-transitive so routes do not flow automatically, a second VPN duplicates infrastructure, and per-VM static routes do not scale.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: On-premises servers must resolve private DNS names hosted in Cloud DNS private zones. Which feature lets on-premises queries reach Cloud DNS?
options: A public DNS zone for the private names
Inbound DNS forwarding, which answers queries forwarded from on-premises
VPC peering with the on-premises network
Cloud NAT on the DNS subnet
explain: Inbound DNS forwarding provides Cloud DNS endpoints that on-premises resolvers forward queries to, resolving private zones without exposing them publicly. Public zones would leak private names, VPC peering does not connect on-premises networks, and Cloud NAT handles VM outbound traffic rather than DNS.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A company uses Dedicated Interconnect but compliance now requires all traffic over it to be encrypted. Which approach adds encryption?
options: Enable Cloud NAT on the Interconnect VLANs
Switch to Carrier Peering
Deploy HA VPN over Cloud Interconnect, encrypting traffic in IPsec tunnels
Add a Cloud Armor policy to the Interconnect
explain: HA VPN over Cloud Interconnect runs encrypted IPsec tunnels across the dedicated connection, satisfying the encryption requirement. Cloud NAT provides outbound translation rather than encryption, Carrier Peering serves public traffic, and Cloud Armor protects load balancers rather than interconnects.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: The SOC wants Security Command Center findings streamed into BigQuery for long-term trend analysis and custom queries. How should this be set up?
options: Enable the Security Command Center BigQuery export
Create a log sink filtering on firewall logs
Export Cloud Billing data to BigQuery
Manually download findings as CSV each week
explain: Security Command Center offers a native BigQuery export that streams findings for analysis. Firewall log sinks capture network logs rather than findings, billing exports contain cost data, and manual CSV downloads do not scale or stay current.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A sensitive subnet must have no internet access at all: no VM in it may initiate outbound connections to public IPs. Which firewall approach enforces this?
options: Delete the subnet's implied firewall rules
Remove Cloud NAT from the VPC
Assign no external IPs and rely on that alone
Create a high-priority egress deny rule for 0.0.0.0/0 targeting the subnet's VMs
explain: A high-priority egress deny rule for 0.0.0.0/0 overrides the implied allow-egress rule and blocks all outbound internet traffic. Implied rules cannot be deleted, removing Cloud NAT only affects NAT-routed traffic, and lacking external IPs does not stop traffic via NAT or other paths.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: Internal users must resolve partner.example.com to an internal IP, while external users resolve the same name to the public IP. Which Cloud DNS feature provides this split-horizon behavior?
options: A public zone with two A records
A DNS response policy zone overriding the answer for VPC networks
DNSSEC signing on the public zone
A forwarding zone to the on-premises resolver
explain: Response policy zones let Cloud DNS return different answers for queries from specified VPC networks, enabling split-horizon DNS. Two A records would round-robin rather than split by source, DNSSEC validates authenticity rather than varying answers, and forwarding zones delegate rather than override.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A company needs its Cloud KMS keys usable in two regions so workloads fail over without key availability issues. What should they create?
options: Two single-region key rings with the same key name
A global key ring for all workloads
A dual-region key ring spanning the two regions
A software-protection key in each zone
explain: Dual-region key rings replicate key material across two specified regions, keeping keys available during a regional failover. Two separate single-region rings hold different key material, global rings suit global resources rather than regional failover pairs, and protection level is unrelated to regional availability.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A SaaS provider publishes a managed service through Private Service Connect. Which subnets must the provider allocate on the producer side?
options: PSC NAT subnets, used to translate consumer connections to the producer backends
Public subnets with external IP ranges
The consumers' VPC subnets
Cloud NAT gateway subnets in each consumer project
explain: Private Service Connect producers allocate NAT subnets whose addresses represent consumer connections to the backend service. Public subnets would expose the service, consumer subnets live in the consumer's VPC, and Cloud NAT is unrelated to PSC publishing.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: An automation service account must call Google Workspace APIs on behalf of individual users, with admin consent. Which mechanism grants this?
options: Workload Identity Federation
An IAM allow policy on the Workspace domain
A user-managed service account key
Domain-wide delegation authorized by the Workspace admin
explain: Domain-wide delegation lets a service account impersonate Workspace users for API calls after the admin authorizes its scopes. Workload Identity Federation handles external workforce authentication rather than Workspace impersonation, IAM policies do not govern Workspace APIs, and a key alone grants no user impersonation rights.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A Cloud Armor security policy denies specific malicious patterns in higher-priority rules, but all other traffic must be allowed. Which rule ensures the allow-by-default behavior?
options: A priority 0 allow rule
The default rule at the lowest priority, set to allow
An edge security policy
A preview-mode rule
explain: Every Cloud Armor policy ends with a default rule at the lowest priority whose action catches traffic unmatched by earlier rules. Priority 0 is invalid since lower numbers mean higher priority, edge policies are a different policy type, and preview mode only logs rather than enforcing.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A project fails when creating its 101st service account, with a quota error. What is the cause and fix?
options: IAM Conditions are blocking creation; remove them
The billing account is suspended; restore it
The default quota of 100 service accounts per project is exhausted; request a quota increase
Service accounts require organization-level creation
explain: Projects default to 100 service accounts, and exceeding that requires a quota increase request. IAM Conditions do not impose count quotas, billing suspension produces different errors, and service accounts are project-level resources.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: The SOC wants a benign Security Command Center finding muted for 30 days during a migration, then automatically active again. How should this be configured?
options: Create a mute config with an expiry time set 30 days out
Delete the finding and wait for it to reappear
Disable Security Command Center for 30 days
Mark the finding inactive permanently
explain: Mute configurations support an expiry timestamp after which findings become active again automatically. Findings cannot be deleted manually, disabling SCC loses all detection, and marking inactive is a permanent state change rather than a timed suppression.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A team suspects a firewall rule is causing an outage and wants to stop it from applying immediately, without losing its configuration. What should they do?
options: Delete the rule and recreate it later
Set the rule's priority to 65535
Remove all targets from the rule
Disable the rule, which stops enforcement while preserving its definition
explain: Firewall rules support a disabled state that halts enforcement while keeping the full configuration for quick re-enablement. Deleting loses the definition, changing priority does not stop matching, and removing targets is a clumsy workaround rather than the supported toggle.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: Auditors need a record of who read a sensitive secret in Secret Manager last month. Which logs contain this?
options: VPC Flow Logs
Data Access audit logs for the Secret Manager API
Cloud Build history
The billing export to BigQuery
explain: Data Access audit logs record read operations on secrets when enabled, showing who accessed which secret version. Flow Logs capture network packets rather than API reads, build history covers CI jobs, and billing data contains no access records.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A security review must find firewall rules that are overly permissive, unused, or shadowed by higher-priority rules. Which tool generates these recommendations?
options: VPC Flow Logs, which record every packet
Cloud Armor WAF rules
Firewall Insights, which analyzes rules and suggests tightening
Cloud DNS logging
explain: Firewall Insights evaluates firewall configurations and produces recommendations such as tightening overly broad rules or removing shadowed ones. Flow Logs provide raw packet records rather than recommendations, Cloud Armor protects load balancers rather than analyzing VPC rules, and DNS logging covers name resolution.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: An internal API sits behind the external Application Load Balancer but must accept traffic only from the corporate office's public IP range. How should the Cloud Armor policy be configured?
options: A high-priority allow rule matching the office CIDR, with the default rule set to deny
A VPC firewall rule on the backend VMs
An IAM Condition on the office IP range
A geo-block rule for every other country
explain: Cloud Armor evaluates rules by priority, so an allow rule for the office CIDR plus a deny-by-default rule restricts the API to the office range. VPC firewall rules do not filter load-balanced traffic at the edge, IAM Conditions do not filter by source IP, and geo-blocking every other country is impractical and imprecise.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: Security policy requires user-managed service account keys to be rotated every 90 days. What is the correct rotation process?
options: Keys rotate automatically; no action is needed
Delete the service account and create a new one
Enable automatic rotation in the IAM console
Create a new key, update applications to use it, then delete the old key
explain: Google Cloud does not auto-rotate user-managed service account keys, so rotation means creating a replacement key, migrating workloads to it, and deleting the old one. There is no automatic rotation toggle, and deleting the service account would break every workload using it.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A nightly job running as a service account must call an IAP-protected web application. How should the job authenticate?
options: Embed a user-managed service account key in the job
Present an OIDC ID token minted for the service account, which holds the IAP-secured Web App User role
Add the job's IP to the IAP firewall rule
Disable IAP during the job's run window
explain: IAP accepts OIDC identity tokens, so the job mints an ID token for its service account and needs the IAP-secured Web App User role on the protected resource. Embedded keys are unnecessary and risky, firewall rules do not bypass IAP identity checks, and disabling IAP removes protection for everyone.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A regional external Application Load Balancer needs Cloud Armor WAF protection. Which policy scope should be used?
options: A global security policy, which covers all load balancer types
An edge security policy
A regional security policy, matching the load balancer's scope
A VPC firewall rule instead
explain: Cloud Armor policy scope must match the load balancer: regional security policies attach to regional load balancers, while global policies attach to global ones. Edge policies target CDN-served backends specifically, and VPC firewall rules do not provide WAF inspection.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A team creates a project with the ID acme-billing-prod and the display name 'Acme Billing'. After a company rebrand, marketing wants both the name and the ID updated. What is possible?
options: The display name can be changed at any time, but the project ID is permanent
Both the display name and the project ID can be edited freely
The project ID can be changed, but the display name is fixed at creation
Neither can be changed; a new project must be created
explain: The project ID is globally unique and permanent once the project is created, so it can never be edited or reused. The display name is only a human-readable label and can be updated at any time without affecting APIs, which tests the common misconception that IDs are editable.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A fault-tolerant batch workload runs on Spot VMs and must flush in-progress work to Cloud Storage before the VM is reclaimed. How much advance warning does Compute Engine provide before preempting a Spot VM?
options: No warning; the VM is terminated immediately
Five minutes via the guest OS shutdown script
30 seconds, signaled through the metadata server
24 hours through a Cloud Monitoring alert
explain: Compute Engine delivers a preemption notice 30 seconds before reclaiming a Spot VM, giving the workload a brief window to checkpoint. There is no multi-minute or day-long warning, and the notice arrives via the metadata server rather than Monitoring alerts or OS scripts alone, which is why designs must checkpoint quickly.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A team must monitor the health of an internal API that is only reachable from inside the VPC and has no public endpoint. Which uptime check type should they create?
options: A public uptime check against the internal IP address
A private uptime check running from inside the VPC
A log-based alert on the API's access logs
A Cloud Scheduler job that pings the endpoint
explain: Private uptime checks run from within the VPC, so they can reach internal-only endpoints that public checkers cannot. Public uptime checks originate from Google's external probers and cannot reach private IPs, while log-based alerts and Scheduler jobs are workarounds that lack the dedicated check semantics and alerting integration.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A compliance policy requires the keys protecting cardholder data to rotate every 90 days. The team wants rotation to happen automatically with no manual steps. What should they configure on the Cloud KMS key?
options: Manually create a new key version every 90 days
A Cloud Scheduler job that calls the KMS API quarterly
Nothing; keys rotate automatically by default
A rotation schedule so KMS generates a new primary version automatically
explain: Cloud KMS supports a rotation period on each key, after which it automatically creates a new primary key version on schedule. Keys do not rotate by default, and manual rotation or Scheduler-driven scripts add operational burden and failure modes that the built-in schedule eliminates.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: An external accountant needs to view invoices and billing account details for the company's Google Cloud usage, but must not be able to modify anything. Which IAM role should they be granted?
options: Billing Account Administrator
Billing Account Viewer
Project Billing Manager
Billing Account User
explain: The Billing Account Viewer role grants read-only access to billing account information including invoices, with no ability to change payment instruments or link projects. Billing Account Administrator can modify everything, Billing Account User can attach projects to the account, and Project Billing Manager controls project billing links, all of which exceed read-only needs.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A developer needs a single always-on, low-traffic web server at the lowest possible cost. Which machine type is the cheapest option?
options: e2-micro
f1-micro
n2-standard-1
e2-small
explain: The e2-micro is the current-generation shared-core machine type, and one instance per month in eligible US regions is covered by the free tier, making it the cheapest always-on option. The f1-micro is the older previous-generation shared-core type that it replaced, while e2-small and n2-standard-1 provision more capacity at higher hourly cost.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A DBA needs to identify the slowest queries on a Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL instance without installing any third-party tooling. Which built-in feature provides query-level performance data?
options: Cloud Trace
Database Migration Service
Query Insights
Cloud Profiler
explain: Query Insights is built into Cloud SQL and surfaces per-query latency, load, and execution statistics directly in the console. Cloud Trace follows request latency across services rather than database queries, Profiler samples application CPU and memory, and Database Migration Service handles migrations, none of which provide query-level database telemetry.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A login endpoint faces credential-stuffing attacks from rotating IP addresses. Each abusive IP should be blocked for 30 minutes after exceeding 100 requests per minute. Which Cloud Armor feature implements this?
options: Rate limiting with an enforce-on-key rule and a ban duration
Adaptive Protection
A VPC firewall rule blocking the attacker IPs
Preconfigured WAF rules for SQL injection
explain: Cloud Armor rate limiting can throttle requests per client key and impose a ban duration that blocks the offender for a fixed period after the threshold is crossed. Adaptive Protection detects novel Layer 7 attacks but does not configure explicit per-IP bans, VPC firewall rules cannot see load-balanced traffic at the edge, and WAF rules target payload signatures rather than request rates.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A startup's Free Trial credits are exhausted, but the team wants to keep its VMs and databases running without interruption. What must they do?
options: Request additional trial credits from support
Nothing; resources continue running for free
Delete the resources and recreate them
Upgrade to a paid Cloud Billing account
explain: When Free Trial credits run out, continued use of Google Cloud requires upgrading to a paid Cloud Billing account; otherwise resources will be stopped. Trial credits cannot be extended on request, and recreating resources does not restore free usage, which tests the misconception that the trial is renewable.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A Cloud Run service connects to a Cloud SQL instance limited to 100 concurrent connections. During traffic spikes, new instances exhaust the connection pool and queries fail. Which setting protects the database?
options: Increase the Cloud SQL connection limit indefinitely
Set a maximum instance limit on the Cloud Run service
Increase the container concurrency setting
Set a minimum instance count
explain: Capping the maximum number of Cloud Run instances bounds the total connections the service can open against the database. Raising concurrency increases connections per instance and worsens exhaustion, minimum instances keep idle capacity warm but do not cap peaks, and endlessly raising the database limit is not always possible or safe.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: EU data-residency rules require application logs to be stored only in the EU. The default log buckets do not satisfy this constraint. What should the team create?
options: A log sink routing to a BigQuery dataset
An exclusion filter for non-EU logs
A regional log bucket in an EU region, with a sink routing logs to it
A locked retention policy on the _Default bucket
explain: Log buckets are regional resources, so creating one in an EU region and routing logs to it via a sink keeps the data resident in the EU. A BigQuery sink does not itself guarantee EU residency unless the dataset is also EU-located, exclusion filters only drop entries, and locked retention controls duration rather than location.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: EU data-residency rules require the company's secrets to be stored only in the EU, but the current secrets replicate automatically across regions. What should the team use?
options: A global secret with a CMEK key
Regional secrets pinned to an EU region
Environment variables on the VMs
A VPC Service Controls perimeter
explain: Secret Manager supports regional secrets whose data stays within the chosen region, satisfying EU residency requirements. Global secrets replicate across regions by design, environment variables are insecure and unmanageable, and VPC Service Controls restricts data movement between projects rather than controlling where secret material is stored.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: Finance wants a third-party monitoring tool billed on the same invoice as the company's Google Cloud usage, with a single payment flow. How should they procure it?
options: Pay the vendor separately with a corporate card
Ask the vendor for a reseller discount
Purchase it through Google Cloud Marketplace, which bills through the Cloud Billing account
Link the vendor's billing account to the project
explain: Google Cloud Marketplace lets customers procure third-party solutions that are billed directly through their existing Cloud Billing account on one invoice. Paying the vendor separately splits billing, reseller discounts do not consolidate invoices, and a project can only link to one Cloud Billing account at a time, which cannot be the vendor's account.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A legacy application on App Engine must accept traffic only from the corporate office's public IP range. Which mechanism enforces this?
options: VPC firewall rules on the App Engine instances
A Cloud Armor security policy
An IAM Condition on the App Engine service
App Engine firewall rules allowing the office CIDR and denying the rest
explain: App Engine has its own firewall with prioritized allow and deny rules evaluated before requests reach the application, making it the right place to restrict by source IP. VPC firewall rules do not apply to App Engine's managed infrastructure, IAM Conditions control who can call the service rather than network source, and Cloud Armor attaches to load balancers rather than App Engine directly.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: Finance needs cost attribution broken down by Kubernetes namespace for GKE workloads, but the billing export only shows cluster-level totals. What provides namespace-level data?
options: Enable GKE usage metering, which exports resource consumption to BigQuery
The standard billing export alone
Running kubectl top on each cluster
The Cloud Console billing dashboard
explain: GKE usage metering records per-namespace and per-workload resource consumption and exports it to BigQuery for cost analysis. The standard billing export aggregates at the cluster or SKU level, kubectl top shows live utilization without cost data, and the console dashboard cannot break spend down by namespace.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: Employees access Google Cloud through a workforce identity pool federated with Okta. Only members of the Okta 'prod-oncall' group should be able to administer production projects. How is this enforced?
options: Create a Google account for every employee
Grant the roles to the entire workforce pool
Map the Okta group attribute and add an attribute condition to the IAM binding
Create an organization policy blocking the other groups
explain: Workforce identity federation maps external IdP attributes into Google Cloud, and IAM Conditions can then restrict a binding to principals whose mapped attributes match, such as group membership. Granting roles to the whole pool over-provisions everyone, creating Google accounts defeats the purpose of federation, and organization policies constrain resource configuration rather than granting identity-based access.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A project is moved from billing account A to billing account B on May 15. How are that month's usage charges divided?
options: All of May's usage is billed to account B
Usage before the move is billed to account A; usage after the move goes to account B
All of May's usage stays on account A
Mid-month moves are blocked; the change takes effect next month
explain: Charges are billed to whichever billing account was linked when the usage was incurred, so pre-move usage stays on the former account and post-move usage goes to the new one. Google documents this exact split, which tests the misconception that the new account absorbs the whole month or that moves only take effect at month boundaries.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment
