q: A team needs Cloud Functions with longer execution times (up to 60 minutes), larger memory, and concurrent request handling per instance. Which should they choose?
options: 1st gen Cloud Functions
App Engine standard
Cloud Run jobs
2nd gen Cloud Functions
explain: Second-generation Cloud Functions raise the maximum timeout to 60 minutes, support larger instances, and allow multiple concurrent requests per instance. First-generation functions are limited to 9-minute timeouts with one request per instance, while App Engine and Cloud Run jobs are different compute models that do not provide the Functions event-driven programming model.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: Production releases must require a human approval click before a Cloud Deploy release can be promoted from staging to production. What enforces this gate?
options: An IAM deny policy on the production cluster
A Cloud Build trigger with manual invocation
A required approval on the promotion in the delivery pipeline
A GKE maintenance exclusion window
explain: Cloud Deploy delivery pipelines support requiring explicit approval before promotion or rollout proceeds, creating a human gate in the release process. IAM deny policies block access entirely rather than gating a step, manual Build triggers do not integrate with Deploy's promotion flow, and maintenance exclusions only pause GKE upgrades rather than approving releases.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: The SOC wants managed, network-based threat detection that inspects traffic mirrored from production VPCs for intrusions and malware. Which Google Cloud service provides this?
options: Cloud IDS
Cloud Armor
VPC Flow Logs
Packet Mirroring alone
explain: Cloud IDS is a managed intrusion detection service that analyzes traffic mirrored from the VPC for network threats. Cloud Armor protects load-balanced applications at the edge rather than inspecting VPC traffic, Flow Logs record connection metadata without threat analysis, and Packet Mirroring only delivers the traffic without detecting anything itself.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A platform team automates the creation of 50 ephemeral test projects per day through a provisioning pipeline. Which API does the automation call to create projects?
options: The Cloud Billing API
The IAM API
The Service Usage API
The Cloud Resource Manager API
explain: The Cloud Resource Manager API exposes the projects.create method used to programmatically create projects. The Billing API manages billing accounts, the IAM API manages policies and service accounts, and the Service Usage API enables or disables services, none of which create the project resource itself.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A team wants Pub/Sub messages delivered to a Cloud Run service over HTTPS as they arrive. What must be configured?
options: A pull subscription polled by the service
A push subscription to the service URL, with the run.invoker role granted to the Pub/Sub service account
An Eventarc trigger on the topic
A Cloud Scheduler job invoking the service
explain: A push subscription delivers each message to the Cloud Run service URL, and the Pub/Sub service agent needs the run.invoker role so delivery requests are authorized. Pull subscriptions require the service to poll, Eventarc routes events differently with its own trigger model, and Scheduler is for cron-style invocation rather than per-message delivery.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A GKE deployment processes a Pub/Sub backlog and must scale on queue depth rather than CPU utilization. What enables autoscaling on this custom signal?
options: The Horizontal Pod Autoscaler with a custom metric from Cloud Monitoring via the Stackdriver adapter
The cluster autoscaler
The Vertical Pod Autoscaler
Manually changing the replica count
explain: The Horizontal Pod Autoscaler can scale on custom metrics exported to Cloud Monitoring, such as Pub/Sub backlog, through the custom metrics adapter. The cluster autoscaler adds nodes rather than scaling pods, the Vertical Pod Autoscaler adjusts resource requests instead of replica counts, and manual scaling cannot react to backlog changes automatically.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: The team wants automated detection of threats such as crypto-mining malware running on Compute Engine VMs, without deploying agents. Which capability provides this?
options: OS patch management
VPC firewall rules
Cloud Armor
Security Command Center threat detection
explain: Security Command Center's threat detection analyzes Google Cloud logs to surface threats like crypto mining, malware, and data exfiltration without agents. OS patching reduces vulnerabilities but does not detect active threats, firewall rules filter traffic without threat intelligence, and Cloud Armor protects load-balanced apps rather than monitoring VM activity.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: During scheduled host maintenance, a VM with attached GPUs restarts instead of live-migrating like the rest of the fleet. What explains this behavior?
options: The maintenance policy was misconfigured on that VM
The zone ran out of capacity during maintenance
VMs with GPUs or local SSDs cannot be live-migrated and are terminated during host maintenance
The VM was preempted as a Spot instance
explain: Live migration is not supported for VMs with GPUs or local SSDs, so Compute Engine terminates and restarts them during host maintenance events. This is documented platform behavior rather than a misconfiguration or capacity problem, which is why GPU workloads must be designed to tolerate restarts.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A team must grant access to buckets based on data classification, enforced by IAM itself. Labels cannot be referenced in IAM Conditions. What should they use?
options: More granular labels on each bucket
Resource tags combined with IAM Conditions
Legacy bucket ACLs
Folder-level IAM grants for each classification
explain: Resource tags are designed for attribute-based access control and can be referenced in IAM Conditions, unlike labels which are for organization and billing. Legacy bucket ACLs bypass IAM auditing, and folder-level grants cannot express per-bucket classification, while adding more labels still leaves IAM unable to evaluate them.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A compliance framework requires the company's VMs to run on dedicated physical hardware with no shared tenancy. What should the team provision?
options: Confidential VMs
Preemptible VMs
Shielded VMs
Sole-tenant nodes
explain: Sole-tenant nodes are dedicated physical servers that host only the customer's VMs, satisfying no-shared-tenancy requirements. Confidential VMs encrypt memory in use and Shielded VMs verify boot integrity, but both still run on shared hosts, while preemptible VMs are a pricing model unrelated to tenancy.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: The team needs MySQL query metrics from its VMs visible in Cloud Monitoring, without writing or maintaining a custom exporter. What should they deploy?
options: The Ops Agent with its MySQL integration enabled
The legacy Stackdriver monitoring agent
A self-managed Prometheus server on each VM
Cloud Trace with custom spans
explain: The Ops Agent includes third-party application integrations, including MySQL, that collect database metrics directly into Cloud Monitoring. The legacy agents are deprecated, self-managed Prometheus adds operational overhead the team wants to avoid, and Cloud Trace records request latency rather than database metrics.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A checkout page faces automated carding attacks from bots that rotate IPs and user agents. Which service adds bot risk scoring that integrates with the WAF?
options: Cloud Armor rate limiting alone
VPC firewall rules
reCAPTCHA Enterprise
Identity-Aware Proxy
explain: reCAPTCHA Enterprise scores traffic for bot-like behavior and integrates with Cloud Armor to challenge or block automated abuse at the checkout. Rate limiting alone cannot distinguish bots from legitimate bursts, VPC firewall rules cannot inspect application-layer bot signals, and IAP gates on user identity rather than detecting automation.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A platform team wants a single Cloud Monitoring dashboard showing request latency from services running in 30 different projects. What enables this cross-project view?
options: A Cloud Monitoring metrics scope spanning the projects
A log sink aggregating all projects
Copying metrics between projects nightly
An organization policy
explain: A metrics scope lets Cloud Monitoring read and chart metrics from multiple projects in one place, which is exactly what cross-project dashboards need. Log sinks centralize logs rather than metrics, copying metrics is unnecessary and lossy, and organization policies constrain configuration rather than enabling observability.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A company shares a 50 TB public dataset with external researchers and does not want to pay for the egress when researchers download it. What should they enable on the bucket?
options: Signed URLs for each researcher
Requester Pays
Cloud CDN in front of the bucket
A dual-region bucket location
explain: Requester Pays shifts data access charges, including network egress, to the requester's project instead of the bucket owner. Signed URLs control access without shifting costs, Cloud CDN adds caching but the origin still pays for cache fills, and dual-region placement improves availability rather than changing who pays for downloads.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: An application must report its internal queue depth directly to Cloud Monitoring for alerting, rather than having it parsed from logs. What should the application use?
options: A log-based metric
An uptime check
Cloud Trace custom spans
The Cloud Monitoring custom metrics API
explain: The custom metrics API lets applications write time-series data points directly into Cloud Monitoring for charting and alerting. Log-based metrics require the value to appear in logs first, uptime checks probe endpoints from outside, and Trace spans record latency rather than gauge values like queue depth.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: The CISO asks for a map of every exploitable route an external attacker could take to reach the payment database, to prioritize firewall hardening. Which Security Command Center feature produces this?
options: Security Health Analytics
Attack path simulations
Event Threat Detection
Mute rules
explain: Attack path simulations in Security Command Center model how an attacker could move through the cloud topology to reach high-value resources. Security Health Analytics flags misconfigurations without modeling attacker movement, Event Threat Detection finds active threats rather than hypothetical paths, and mute rules only suppress findings.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A project was accidentally created at the organization root, but it belongs under the dev folder. The project must keep running throughout. What is the fix?
options: Delete the project and recreate it in the folder
Projects cannot be moved once created
Move the project into the dev folder; moves within the same organization are allowed
Migrate the project to a new organization
explain: Projects can be moved between folders, or between the organization root and a folder, within the same organization without downtime. Deleting and recreating loses the project ID and all resources, organization migration is a heavier cross-org operation, and the claim that projects cannot move is simply false.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: Analysts want to train and evaluate a customer-churn prediction model using only SQL, with no ML infrastructure to manage. What should they use?
options: BigQuery ML
Vertex AI custom training
Dataproc with Spark MLlib
Cloud Data Fusion
explain: BigQuery ML lets analysts create, train, and run models with SQL statements directly on warehouse data. Vertex AI custom training and Dataproc require ML engineering and cluster management, while Data Fusion is a visual ETL tool rather than a model-training service.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A new Cloud Run revision is throwing errors in production. The team wants all traffic back on the previous revision immediately, without deploying anything new. What should they do?
options: Delete the faulty revision
Update the service's traffic allocation to send 100% to the previous revision
Rebuild the container image
Disable the Cloud Run service
explain: Cloud Run keeps prior revisions available, so shifting the traffic split back to 100% on the previous revision instantly restores the working version. Deleting the revision does not reroute traffic by itself, rebuilding takes time and risks new issues, and disabling the service causes a full outage rather than a rollback.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A BigQuery dataset holding PII must be encrypted with a customer-managed key controlled by the security team. Where is the key assigned?
options: On each individual table after creation
On the project's default settings
In each query's job configuration
On the dataset as its default encryption setting
explain: BigQuery accepts a customer-managed encryption key at the dataset level, which then protects all tables created in it. Setting keys per table is unnecessary when the dataset default covers them, project defaults do not exist for this purpose, and queries cannot override dataset encryption.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: An engineer must authenticate the gcloud CLI on a headless build server that has no web browser. Which approach completes the login?
options: Reinstall the Cloud SDK with a GUI installer
Create a long-lived service account key on the server
Open a browser port through the firewall
Run gcloud auth login --no-browser and complete the flow on another device
explain: The --no-browser flag prints a URL and verification code so the engineer can authorize on a separate device and paste the code back, which is the documented headless flow. Reinstalling changes nothing about the missing browser, opening firewall ports does not create a browser, and minting a long-lived key is less secure than the intended OAuth flow.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An ML training job expects a POSIX filesystem path for its training data, but the data lives in Cloud Storage. What lets the job access the bucket as a local directory?
options: gsutil rsync before each training run
Filestore
Cloud Storage FUSE
Storage Transfer Service
explain: Cloud Storage FUSE mounts a bucket as a local filesystem so applications can read and write objects with standard file operations. Copying with rsync duplicates data and adds sync steps, Filestore is a separate NFS service rather than a view of the bucket, and Transfer Service moves data between locations instead of presenting it as a filesystem.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A team is migrating its Prometheus dashboards and wants to keep writing PromQL queries against Google Cloud metrics. What supports this?
options: Only a self-hosted Grafana instance
Cloud Monitoring's PromQL support
Monitoring Query Language (MQL)
Log-based metrics
explain: Cloud Monitoring natively accepts PromQL queries against Google Cloud metrics, so existing Prometheus dashboards and alerts can be reused. MQL is a separate Google-specific language, log-based metrics derive metrics from logs rather than accepting PromQL, and Grafana is a visualization layer rather than the query engine.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: An application must mint short-lived access tokens as a service account to call Google Cloud APIs, but downloading the service account's key is prohibited. Which IAM role on the service account enables this?
options: Service Account Token Creator
Service Account User
Service Account Key Admin
Service Account Admin
explain: The Service Account Token Creator role grants permission to impersonate the account for signing blobs and minting short-lived tokens without ever handling its keys. Service Account User only allows attaching the account to resources, Key Admin manages keys rather than tokens, and Service Account Admin is full administration, which exceeds the need.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: An engineer on the Free Trial hits a limit of 8 vCPUs, and the quota increase request option is unavailable. What explains this, and what is the fix?
options: A billing misconfiguration; contact support to fix it
The Free Trial has reduced quotas; upgrade to a paid account to request increases
The Compute Engine API is not enabled
The region is out of capacity; switch regions
explain: The Free Trial intentionally caps quotas below paid-account levels, and quota increases require upgrading to a paid Cloud Billing account first. Enabling the API does not raise quota ceilings, switching regions does not escape trial limits, and this is documented trial behavior rather than a billing error.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A Redis cache must survive a zonal failure with automatic failover and no data loss. Which Memorystore for Redis tier provides this?
options: Basic tier
A self-managed Redis VM
Memorystore for Memcached
Standard tier, with its replica and automatic failover
explain: The Standard tier provisions a primary with a replica in another zone and fails over automatically, protecting against zonal outages. The Basic tier has no replica, a self-managed VM adds operational burden without built-in failover, and Memcached is a different engine without Redis persistence semantics.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: The security team needs to query audit logs from 50 projects in one place for incident response. What is the recommended architecture?
options: Grant logs viewer on each project individually
Export each project's logs to CSV files
An aggregated organization-level sink routing audit logs to a central project's log bucket
A separate dashboard per project
explain: An aggregated sink at the organization or folder level routes matching logs from all current and future child projects into one central bucket for unified querying. Per-project grants force analysts to switch context constantly, CSV exports are stale and unqueryable, and per-project dashboards fragment the investigation.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A team wants every container image pushed to Artifact Registry automatically scanned for known OS vulnerabilities. Which feature does this?
options: Artifact Registry vulnerability scanning
Binary Authorization
Cloud Build
Manual scanning with local tools
explain: Artifact Registry's built-in vulnerability scanning analyzes images on push and reports known OS package vulnerabilities. Binary Authorization enforces deploy-time policy on attestations rather than scanning, Cloud Build compiles images without vulnerability analysis, and manual scanning does not scale across every push.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: An audit must list all projects that are missing the cost-center label. Which gcloud filter finds them?
options: --filter='labels.cost-center:*'
--filter='-labels.cost-center:*'
--filter='labels:NULL'
List all projects and grep the output
explain: The minus prefix negates the filter expression, so -labels.cost-center:* matches projects where the label key is absent. The positive form matches projects that have the label, labels:NULL is not valid filter syntax, and grepping raw output is fragile compared to server-side filtering.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A team wants serverless Kubernetes with GPU acceleration for ML training, without managing node pools, drivers, or upgrades. Which GKE mode supports this?
options: GKE Autopilot, which supports GPU workloads
GKE Standard without node pools
Cloud Run with GPUs
A managed instance group of GPU VMs
explain: GKE Autopilot manages nodes, drivers, and upgrades while supporting GPU workload requests, giving serverless Kubernetes with acceleration. GKE Standard always requires node pool management, Cloud Run does not expose GPUs as a standard offering, and a MIG of GPU VMs is unmanaged infrastructure rather than Kubernetes.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A Cloud Scheduler HTTP job occasionally fails because a downstream service is flaky. The team wants automatic retries with backoff instead of manual reruns. What should they configure?
options: A second schedule as a backup
A Cloud Function wrapper around the job
Manual reruns from the console
The job's retry configuration with max attempts and backoff settings
explain: Cloud Scheduler jobs support configurable retry policies with maximum attempts and backoff, so transient downstream failures are retried automatically. A duplicate schedule doubles invocations rather than retrying failures, a wrapper function adds unnecessary complexity, and manual reruns do not scale with intermittent flakes.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: An auditor needs to list every principal with access to a Cloud KMS key in the security project. Which command shows the key's IAM policy?
options: gcloud kms keys list
gcloud projects get-iam-policy
gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy KEY --keyring=KEYRING --location=LOCATION
gcloud iam roles list
explain: The get-iam-policy subcommand on the key resource returns exactly the bindings attached to that KMS key. Listing keys shows inventory without permissions, the project-level policy omits key-specific grants, and listing roles shows role definitions rather than who holds them on the key.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: An application receives 429 rateLimitExceeded errors from the Compute Engine API, but the Quotas page shows plenty of CPU and disk headroom. What is the most likely cause?
options: The CPU allocation quota is exhausted
Billing was disabled on the project
A per-minute API request rate quota is exhausted
The service account lacks IAM permissions
explain: Google Cloud enforces per-minute API rate quotas separately from resource allocation quotas, so heavy API callers can hit 429s while CPU headroom remains. Exhausted allocation quotas would show on the Quotas page, disabled billing stops resources rather than returning rate errors, and missing IAM permissions produce 403s rather than 429s.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: The dev folder allows external IP addresses for testing, but the prod folder must deny them. Where should the constraint be applied?
options: An organization policy on the prod folder
An IAM policy on the prod folder
A VPC firewall rule in each prod project
An IAM deny policy on the organization
explain: Organization policies can be attached at the folder level, so the constraint applies to the prod folder and inherits to its projects without affecting dev. IAM policies grant access rather than restricting resource configuration, per-project firewall rules do not scale centrally, and an organization-level deny would incorrectly block dev as well.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A company wants EU users resolved to EU backends and US users to US backends at the DNS level. Which Cloud DNS feature provides this?
options: Private DNS zones
DNS peering
Routing policies with geolocation rules
Round-robin records only
explain: Cloud DNS routing policies support geolocation-based answers, returning different record sets depending on the resolver's location. Private zones serve internal names rather than steering public traffic, DNS peering shares zones between VPCs, and plain round-robin records cannot distinguish client geography.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: After a suspected breach, the team needs a forensic copy of a VM's boot disk for analysis, isolated from production and without touching the running VM. What is the correct approach?
options: Detach the production disk and attach it to a forensic VM
Create a snapshot, then create a new disk from it in an isolated project
Copy the files over SSH while the VM runs
Enable Shielded VM on the instance
explain: Snapshots capture a point-in-time copy of the disk, and a new disk created from the snapshot can be analyzed in an isolated project without disturbing production. Detaching the disk causes downtime and risks evidence, SSH copying is slow and incomplete, and Shielded VM is a preventive boot-integrity feature rather than a forensic tool.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: Engineers occasionally need elevated access to production, but standing admin grants violate policy. The company wants just-in-time elevation with manager approval and automatic expiry. Which service provides this?
options: IAM Conditions with time windows
Service account impersonation
OS Login with 2FA
Privileged Access Manager
explain: Privileged Access Manager provides just-in-time privileged access with approval workflows, time bounds, and full auditing. IAM Conditions can time-box a binding but lack approvals and request workflows, impersonation grants standing ability to act as the account, and OS Login only governs SSH access rather than privilege elevation.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: An engineer has two accounts authenticated with gcloud and wants to run a single command as the second account, without changing the active configuration. Which flag does this?
options: --account
--project
--impersonate-service-account
--configuration
explain: The --account flag overrides the active account for a single command invocation, leaving the configuration untouched. The --project flag changes the target project rather than the identity, --impersonate-service-account is for service account impersonation rather than switching user accounts, and --configuration switches the whole named configuration.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: After updating product images in Cloud Storage, customers still see the old versions served through Cloud CDN. What clears the stale cached copies?
options: Delete and recreate the bucket
Rename all the objects
Wait for the 30-day default TTL to expire
Issue a cache invalidation for the affected paths
explain: Cache invalidation explicitly purges the specified paths from Cloud CDN edge caches so the next request fetches the fresh objects. Recreating the bucket or renaming objects is disruptive and unnecessary, and waiting for TTL expiry leaves stale content served for days, which is the operational trap this tests.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: Pods take several minutes to start because they must pull multi-gigabyte container images onto each node. Which GKE feature lets containers start before the full image is downloaded?
options: Node auto-provisioning
Vertical Pod Autoscaling
Image streaming
Larger node machine types
explain: GKE image streaming fetches image data on demand, so containers can start while the remaining layers download in the background. Node auto-provisioning adds capacity rather than speeding pulls, Vertical Pod Autoscaling tunes resource requests, and larger machines do not change how long a full image pull takes.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A sensitive subnet must reach Google APIs and services, but no VM in it may initiate connections to any other public internet destination. Which firewall approach enforces this?
options: A high-priority deny-all egress rule, with higher-priority allow rules for the Google API address ranges
A Cloud NAT gateway on the subnet
Private Google Access alone
A VPC Service Controls perimeter
explain: Firewall rules are evaluated by priority, so allowing the Google API ranges at higher priority while denying all other egress achieves exactly this selective outcome. Cloud NAT provides outbound connectivity rather than restricting it, Private Google Access enables API reachability without filtering other destinations, and VPC Service Controls governs service-to-service data movement rather than VM egress.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A team shuts down project test-env-123 and, after it is fully deleted, tries to create a new project with the same ID. The ID is rejected. Why?
options: The 30-day recovery window has not elapsed yet
Project IDs of fully deleted projects cannot be reused
The project name is still reserved
A new billing account is required first
explain: Project IDs are unique and permanent, and once a project is fully deleted its ID can never be reused, which is why the creation is rejected. The 30-day window only governs restoration of the deleted project, the display name is not unique and carries no reservation, and billing accounts have no bearing on ID availability.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A PostgreSQL workload needs strong transactional consistency plus real-time analytical queries over the same data, without maintaining a separate warehouse. Which database fits?
options: AlloyDB, with its columnar engine for analytical queries
Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL
Bigtable
Firestore in Datastore mode
explain: AlloyDB is PostgreSQL-compatible and adds a columnar engine that accelerates analytical queries on the same transactional data. Cloud SQL lacks the columnar engine for HTAP workloads, Bigtable is a NoSQL wide-column store without SQL transactions, and Firestore is a document database unsuited to relational analytics.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: The security team wants an alert whenever a VM is deleted in the production project, for timely review. What should they create?
options: An uptime check on each VM
A quota alert for instance counts
A Pub/Sub topic for the team
A log-based alert on Admin Activity audit logs for compute.instances.delete
explain: VM deletions are recorded in Admin Activity audit logs, so a log-based alert matching the delete operation fires exactly when it happens. Uptime checks detect unreachability without identifying deletions, quota alerts track limits rather than security events, and a Pub/Sub topic alone has no detection logic attached.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: An application uses envelope encryption for sensitive records stored in Cloud Storage. Where should the data encryption keys (DEKs) be kept?
options: Hardcoded in the application source
In Secret Manager as plaintext secrets
Encrypted (wrapped) by a Cloud KMS key and stored alongside the data
In the VM's instance metadata
explain: Envelope encryption wraps each DEK with a key-encryption key in Cloud KMS, so the encrypted DEKs can safely sit next to the data while only KMS can unwrap them. Hardcoding keys in source or metadata exposes them to anyone with read access, and storing raw DEKs in Secret Manager misses the point of envelope encryption, which is to avoid per-record KMS calls.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: An automation script needs a project's full resource details — labels, parent, lifecycle state — as JSON for further processing. Which command provides this?
options: gcloud config list
gcloud projects describe PROJECT_ID --format=json
gcloud projects list
gcloud info
explain: The describe command returns the full resource representation of one project, and --format=json renders it as machine-readable JSON. The config list shows local CLI settings rather than project resources, projects list returns a tabular summary of many projects, and gcloud info describes the SDK installation itself.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A Bigtable instance must remain available with no data loss during a full zonal outage. What provides this protection?
options: Add a second cluster in another zone so data replicates
Take daily manual backups
Increase the node count in the existing cluster
Export the data to BigQuery nightly
explain: Bigtable replication across clusters in different zones keeps copies of the data available, so a zonal failure does not cause data loss or downtime. Backups and exports are point-in-time copies that cannot serve live traffic, and adding nodes to the same zone does not protect against the zone itself failing.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A cloudbuild.yaml must tag each built image with the SHA of the commit that triggered the build. Which built-in substitution provides it?
options: $BRANCH_NAME
$PROJECT_ID
$BUILD_ID
$COMMIT_SHA
explain: Cloud Build populates the $COMMIT_SHA default substitution with the commit that triggered the build, making it the correct tag source. $BRANCH_NAME gives the branch without identifying the exact commit, $PROJECT_ID identifies the project, and $BUILD_ID is a unique build UUID rather than the source commit.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: The team wants to evaluate a new Cloud Armor WAF rule's impact on real traffic without blocking any legitimate requests yet. How should the rule be deployed?
options: At the highest priority so it runs first
In a separate security policy
In preview mode, which logs matches without enforcing
With the policy disabled
explain: Preview mode evaluates the rule against live traffic and logs what would have matched, without taking any blocking action. Priority only controls evaluation order rather than enforcement, a separate policy still enforces its rules, and a disabled policy evaluates nothing, so none of them provide safe observation.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A Terraform module provisions new projects and must ensure the Compute Engine API is enabled in each one. Which Terraform resource does this?
options: google_project_service
google_project_iam_binding
google_compute_instance
google_service_account
explain: The google_project_service resource enables a specific API in a project, which is exactly what the module needs for the Compute Engine API. The IAM binding manages role grants, google_compute_instance creates VMs, and google_service_account creates identities, none of which enable APIs.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A company wants a hub-and-spoke topology connecting 40 VPCs and its on-premises network, without building a full mesh of VPC peerings. Which service provides this?
options: A full mesh of VPC peering connections
Network Connectivity Center
Shared VPC
One Cloud VPN tunnel per VPC
explain: Network Connectivity Center acts as a hub that spokes, including VPCs and on-premises networks, attach to for transitive connectivity. A peering mesh scales poorly and lacks transitivity, Shared VPC shares one VPC rather than connecting many, and per-VPC VPN tunnels multiply management overhead without a central hub.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: New GKE pods stay Pending with IP allocation errors, even though the nodes have free CPU and memory. What should the team check?
options: Whether the node pool needs more nodes
The pods' disruption budgets
Node taints and tolerations
Whether the subnet's secondary Pod IP range is exhausted
explain: GKE assigns pod IPs from the subnet's secondary range, so exhausting that range blocks scheduling even with free node capacity. Adding nodes does not help when the IP range itself is empty, disruption budgets govern voluntary evictions, and taints affect placement rather than IP allocation.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: An IAP-protected internal tool must be accessible only to members of the eng-team Google Group. What is the correct grant?
options: Add the group to a VPC firewall rule
Grant the group the Compute Viewer role
Grant the IAP-secured Web App User role to the group on the IAP-secured resource
Share the IAP OAuth client secret with the group
explain: Access to IAP-protected resources is governed by the IAP-secured Web App User role, so granting it to the group on the backend service restricts access to members. Firewall rules filter network traffic rather than IAP identity, Compute Viewer grants console visibility without IAP access, and sharing the OAuth secret undermines the identity check entirely.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: The security team wants every new bucket in the organization to use uniform bucket-level access, with no exceptions. Which organization policy constraint enforces this?
options: constraints/storage.uniformBucketLevelAccess
constraints/iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation
constraints/compute.requireOsLogin
constraints/compute.vmExternalIpAccess
explain: The storage.uniformBucketLevelAccess constraint forces new buckets to use uniform IAM-based access instead of legacy object ACLs. The key-creation constraint governs service account keys, requireOsLogin governs SSH authentication, and vmExternalIpAccess governs external IPs, none of which control bucket access models.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A team wants malformed messages rejected at publish time so subscribers only ever receive well-formed JSON. What enforces the message format on the topic?
options: A dead-letter topic
A Pub/Sub schema with validation enabled
An IAM Condition on the topic
A Cloud Function that validates each message
explain: Pub/Sub schemas define the expected Avro or Protobuf format and can validate messages at publish time, rejecting malformed ones. Dead-letter topics quarantine failed deliveries rather than validating format, IAM Conditions control access rather than content, and a validator function adds latency and cost to every message.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: Messages on a subscription fail processing repeatedly and must be quarantined for inspection after 5 failed delivery attempts. What should be configured?
options: Longer message retention on the topic
Exactly-once delivery
A longer acknowledgement deadline
A dead-letter topic with max delivery attempts set to 5
explain: Dead-letter topics capture messages that exhaust their delivery attempts, preserving them for inspection instead of redelivering forever. Retention keeps acknowledged messages available but does not quarantine failures, exactly-once delivery prevents duplicates rather than handling poison messages, and longer ack deadlines only delay the inevitable redelivery.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: Compliance requires application logs to be archived to Cloud Storage for long-term, low-cost retention. What should the team create?
options: A BigQuery dataset for the logs
A log exclusion filter
A log sink routing to a Cloud Storage bucket
A Cloud Monitoring dashboard
explain: A log sink with a Cloud Storage destination continuously exports matching log entries into the bucket for cheap long-term archival. BigQuery sinks serve analytics rather than low-cost archiving, exclusion filters discard entries instead of preserving them, and dashboards visualize metrics rather than storing logs.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A Cloud Function outside the VPC Service Controls perimeter must write to a BigQuery dataset inside it. Which perimeter configuration allows this specific flow?
options: Remove the analytics project from the perimeter
An ingress rule allowing the function's service account to the protected resources
Expand the perimeter to include the function's project
Temporarily disable perimeter enforcement
explain: VPC Service Controls ingress rules permit specific identities from outside the perimeter to reach protected resources, enabling exactly this cross-boundary flow. Removing the project or disabling enforcement destroys the protection, while expanding the perimeter to include the function may be impossible if it lives in an untrusted project.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A CI pipeline must build with an exact, reproducible Cloud SDK version rather than whatever is latest. Which approach guarantees the version?
options: Run gcloud components update before each build
Install the SDK with apt-get on every run
Use the floating latest tag of the SDK
Use the versioned google/cloud-sdk container image
explain: The google/cloud-sdk image is published with explicit version tags, so pinning a tag guarantees the exact SDK release in every build. Updating components or apt-getting latest floats with upstream releases, and the latest tag is explicitly non-reproducible, which is the trap this tests.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A legacy .NET Framework application requires Windows containers and must run on GKE. What must the cluster have?
options: A Windows Server node pool
GKE Autopilot mode
A Linux node pool with a compatibility layer
Cloud Run instead of GKE
explain: GKE supports Windows Server node pools that can schedule Windows containers alongside Linux pools in the same cluster. Autopilot does not support Windows nodes, Linux nodes cannot run Windows containers even with compatibility layers, and Cloud Run is a Linux-based serverless platform.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A production VM's data disk is nearly full, but the VM cannot be stopped. How can capacity be added without downtime?
options: Create a snapshot and restore it to a bigger disk
Stop the VM, resize, and restart it
Resize the persistent disk while attached, then grow the filesystem
Attach a local SSD for the extra space
explain: Persistent disks support online resize while attached to a running VM; the guest filesystem is then grown to use the new space. Snapshot-and-restore requires downtime to swap disks, stopping the VM violates the no-downtime requirement, and local SSDs are ephemeral scratch space rather than durable capacity expansion.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A contractor's engagement ends abruptly, and all of their Google Cloud access must stop immediately. What is the fastest action?
options: Remove each of their IAM bindings one by one
Suspend or delete their Cloud Identity account
Rotate every secret they might have seen
Disable the APIs in their projects
explain: Suspending or deleting the identity disables all of its Google Cloud access at once, since every IAM grant resolves through the account. Removing bindings individually is slow and error-prone, rotating secrets does not revoke access, and disabling APIs breaks everyone rather than just the departing contractor.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: An agency runs workloads for 10 clients, each requiring isolated billing and IAM boundaries. What is the recommended isolation unit?
options: One project with labels per client
Separate VPCs in one project
Separate folders under one project
Separate projects per client
explain: Projects are the fundamental isolation boundary for both billing and IAM in Google Cloud, so one project per client gives clean separation. Labels organize costs but do not isolate access, VPCs share the project's IAM and billing, and folders cannot exist inside a project, which tests the hierarchy misconception.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A Spanner database must remain available through a full regional outage. Which instance configuration provides this?
options: A multi-region instance configuration
A regional configuration with automated backups
A single region with more nodes
A larger node count in one zone
explain: Multi-region instance configurations replicate data across regions, so the database survives a regional failure. Regional configurations and larger node counts stay within one region's failure domain, and backups restore data after an outage rather than maintaining availability through it.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: During an incident, the team must list every API call a compromised service account made last week. Where should they look?
options: VPC Flow Logs
Cloud Audit Logs filtered by the service account as principal
Cloud Trace
The BigQuery billing export
explain: Cloud Audit Logs record who called which API and when, and filtering by the service account principal isolates its activity. Flow Logs capture network connections without API semantics, Trace follows request latency rather than IAM activity, and the billing export shows costs rather than API calls.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A service behind Identity-Aware Proxy needs the verified email of the caller for audit logging. Where does it get the caller's identity?
options: The X-Forwarded-For header
A query parameter passed by the client
The client's OAuth access token
The IAP JWT assertion header (X-Goog-IAP-JWT-Assertion)
explain: IAP validates the user's identity and passes it to the backend in a signed JWT in the X-Goog-IAP-JWT-Assertion header, which the app can verify. X-Forwarded-For carries client IPs rather than identity, query parameters are client-controlled and untrustworthy, and the access token belongs to the OAuth flow rather than the backend contract.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A platform engineer must create a folder named prod directly under the organization from the CLI. Which command does this?
options: gcloud projects create prod
gcloud organizations create prod
gcloud resource-manager folders create --display-name=prod --organization=ORG_ID
gcloud iam folders create prod
explain: Folders are managed through the resource-manager folders command collection, with the parent specified as the organization. The projects command creates projects rather than folders, organizations cannot be created this way, and there is no iam folders command, which tests knowing the correct command surface.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: Analysts need to build batch ETL pipelines with a visual drag-and-drop interface and no code. Which fully managed service fits?
options: Cloud Data Fusion
Dataflow
Dataproc
Cloud Composer
explain: Cloud Data Fusion provides a visual, code-free pipeline designer for ETL on a managed platform. Dataflow and Dataproc require writing pipeline or Spark code, while Cloud Composer orchestrates workflows with Python DAGs rather than offering a visual ETL builder.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: Log timestamps are drifting between VMs, complicating incident correlation. What keeps Compute Engine VM clocks synchronized by default?
options: Manually configuring ntpd on each VM
The application writing its own timestamps
Cloud Monitoring
Google's internal NTP service at metadata.google.internal
explain: Compute Engine VMs synchronize their clocks with Google's internal NTP service by default, keeping fleet timestamps consistent. Manual ntpd configuration is unnecessary and error-prone, applications should not invent their own time sources, and Cloud Monitoring collects metrics rather than disciplining clocks.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: Microservices on GKE must encrypt pod-to-pod traffic with mutual authentication. Which approach provides this?
options: VPC firewall rules
A service mesh with mutual TLS
Cloud Armor
Kubernetes NetworkPolicies
explain: A service mesh such as Istio injects sidecars that establish mutual TLS between pods, encrypting traffic with workload identity. Firewall rules and NetworkPolicies allow or deny traffic without encrypting it, and Cloud Armor protects edge load balancers rather than internal pod communication.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: Workload projects must launch VMs from a hardened image stored in the security project. What allows this without copying the image everywhere?
options: Make the image public
Copy the image into each workload project
Grant the Compute Image User role on the image to the workload identities
Set up a Shared VPC
explain: The Compute Image User role granted on the image lets specified identities in other projects create VMs from it, avoiding copies or public exposure. Making the image public exposes it to everyone, copying multiplies maintenance, and Shared VPC shares networks rather than images, which tests confusing the two sharing mechanisms.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A fault-tolerant ML training job needs GPUs at the lowest possible price and can tolerate interruptions with checkpointing. Which option minimizes cost?
options: On-demand GPU VMs
Reserved GPU capacity
Preemptible TPUs without checkpointing
Spot VMs with attached GPUs
explain: Spot VMs offer the deepest discounts on GPU capacity for workloads that checkpoint and tolerate preemption. On-demand GPUs cost the most, reservations trade flexibility for smaller discounts, and skipping checkpointing risks losing all progress on interruption, which defeats the fault-tolerant design.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: Developers need a copy of the production Cloud SQL database for load testing, without any impact on production performance or data. What should the DBA create?
options: A clone of the instance
A restore of a backup over production
A CSV export of every table
Point the test app at the production read replica
explain: Cloning creates an independent copy of the instance that load tests can hammer without touching production. Restoring over production destroys live data, CSV exports lose schema fidelity and take effort to reload, and pointing tests at the read replica risks degrading production read performance.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A retailer must store cardholder data on Google Cloud under PCI DSS. Which statement about compliance responsibility is true?
options: Google's PCI DSS certification removes all customer obligations
Google Cloud's PCI DSS-compliant infrastructure covers the platform; the retailer remains responsible for its own cardholder data environment
PCI DSS does not apply to cloud-hosted cardholder data
Only Assured Workloads projects can process cardholder data
explain: Google Cloud maintains PCI DSS compliance for its infrastructure, but customers share responsibility for securing their own applications, data, and access controls. Certification never transfers all obligations to the provider, PCI DSS fully applies in the cloud, and Assured Workloads is one sovereignty option rather than a PCI requirement.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: An engineer needs to see a project's full ancestry — its parent folders and organization — from the CLI. Which command shows this?
options: gcloud projects list
gcloud projects describe
gcloud projects get-ancestry
gcloud resource-manager folders list
explain: The get-ancestry command returns the chain of parents from the project up through folders to the organization. Projects list shows many projects without ancestry, describe shows the immediate parent only, and folders list enumerates folders rather than a specific project's lineage.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A real-time collaboration app needs long-lived WebSocket connections from a global user base through the load balancer. Which load balancer supports WebSockets?
options: Cloud VPN
The internal passthrough Network Load Balancer
Cloud DNS
The external Application Load Balancer
explain: The external Application Load Balancer is a Layer 7 proxy that supports WebSocket connections from global clients. Cloud VPN connects networks rather than balancing application traffic, the passthrough Network LB handles TCP/UDP without Layer 7 protocol support, and Cloud DNS resolves names rather than proxying connections.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A Cloud Run job occasionally hangs on bad input and must be forcibly terminated after 30 minutes. Which setting enforces this?
options: Set the job's task timeout to 30 minutes
Set a Cloud Scheduler deadline
Reduce the maximum retries
Set a minimum instance count
explain: Cloud Run jobs support a configurable task timeout that terminates executions exceeding the limit, which directly caps a hung run at 30 minutes. Scheduler deadlines govern the invocation rather than the execution, retries control re-attempts rather than duration, and minimum instances keep capacity warm without limiting runtime.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: An application needs third-party API keys at runtime, rotated quarterly, with the keys never appearing in source code or container images. Where should they be stored?
options: Baked into the container image
In Secret Manager
In the VM's instance metadata
In a config file in Cloud Storage
explain: Secret Manager is purpose-built for storing sensitive credentials with versioning, rotation, and IAM-controlled access. Baking keys into images exposes them to anyone with image access, instance metadata is visible to the VM broadly, and config files in buckets lack rotation and fine-grained access semantics.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A VM was created manually in the console and must now be managed by the team's Terraform configuration, without being recreated. Which command brings it under Terraform management?
options: terraform apply
terraform refresh
terraform import
terraform destroy
explain: The terraform import command associates an existing resource with a Terraform resource address so it can be managed going forward. Apply would try to create a duplicate, refresh only updates state for already-managed resources, and destroy deletes the VM, which is the opposite of the goal.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A network appliance requires a custom kernel module that managed platforms do not allow. Which compute option supports this?
options: Cloud Run
App Engine flexible environment
GKE Autopilot
Compute Engine VMs
explain: Compute Engine VMs give full control over the guest OS, including custom kernels and kernel modules. Cloud Run, App Engine, and GKE Autopilot all run on Google-managed host environments that prohibit custom kernel modifications, which is the key platform constraint this tests.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: Engineers want to jump from an error log entry directly to the full distributed trace for that request. What makes this correlation possible?
options: Including the trace ID in the log entry's trace field
A custom Cloud Monitoring dashboard
Extending log retention to one year
Enabling debug logging on the service
explain: When log entries carry the trace ID in the trace field, the Cloud Logging UI links each entry to its trace in Cloud Trace. Dashboards visualize aggregates without per-request linkage, longer retention preserves data without correlating it, and debug logging adds volume rather than trace context.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: GKE pods in one project must pull container images from an Artifact Registry repository in another project. What grants this?
options: Grant Artifact Registry Reader on the repository to the nodes' service account
Make the repository public
Copy the images into each consuming project
Grant Project Viewer on the registry's project
explain: The Artifact Registry Reader role on the repository lets the nodes' service account pull images across project boundaries without broader access. Making the repository public exposes images to everyone, copying multiplies maintenance, and Project Viewer grants wide read access far beyond pulling images.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: An auditor needs to list every principal allowed to impersonate a sensitive service account. Which command shows the service account's IAM policy?
options: gcloud iam service-accounts list
gcloud projects get-iam-policy
gcloud iam service-accounts get-iam-policy SA_EMAIL
gcloud auth list
explain: The get-iam-policy subcommand on the service account returns the bindings on that identity, revealing who can impersonate it. Listing service accounts shows inventory without permissions, the project-level policy omits account-level grants, and auth list shows the CLI's authenticated accounts rather than IAM bindings.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A startup created its Cloud Billing account while headquartered in Germany and is now relocating to the US, wanting all future invoices in USD instead of EUR. What is the correct way to change the billing currency?
options: Open a support case to convert the existing billing account to USD
Create a new Cloud Billing account in the desired currency and move the projects to it
Edit the currency field on the billing account in the Cloud Console
Update the Google payments profile country to change the currency
explain: A Cloud Billing account operates in a single currency that is fixed at creation and cannot be changed afterward, so the documented path is to create a new billing account in the desired currency and link the projects to it. Support cannot convert an existing account, the console exposes no editable currency field, and changing the payments profile country does not alter the account's currency.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A Google Cloud reseller wants to give each of its customers a separate invoice while managing all billing from one master account. Which approach supports this?
options: Create a billing subaccount for each customer under the master billing account
Create a separate organization for each customer
Enable a second currency on the master billing account
Move all customer projects into a single folder
explain: Billing subaccounts let a reseller's master billing account issue separate invoices per customer while keeping centralized management, and each subaccount automatically inherits the parent's currency. Separate organizations add no billing separation, a billing account supports only one currency, and folders organize resources without changing invoicing.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A FinOps analyst needs resource-level cost data with labels in BigQuery to build per-team chargeback reports. The current standard usage cost export lacks the needed granularity. What should they enable?
options: The detailed usage cost export to BigQuery
A longer retention period on the _Default log bucket
VPC Flow Logs on all subnets
Cloud Trace sampling at 100 percent
explain: The detailed usage cost export writes resource-level rows, including labels, to BigQuery, which is exactly what per-team chargeback reporting needs beyond the standard export's SKU-level rollups. Log retention, flow logs, and trace sampling capture operational telemetry rather than billing data and cannot produce cost breakdowns.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: After a project was accidentally shut down, the platform team realized nobody received the deletion notification email. Which configuration ensures the right people get security and technical notifications for a project?
options: Add the on-call engineers as Essential Contacts in the Technical category for the project
Grant the engineers the Project Owner role
Enable Data Access audit logs for the project
Create a log sink exporting Admin Activity logs to BigQuery
explain: Essential Contacts designate who receives notification emails by category, and Google sends project deletion notices to Technical category contacts, so registering the on-call engineers there fixes the gap. IAM roles grant permissions rather than notifications, and audit logs plus sinks record activity for later investigation instead of sending proactive emails.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A developer runs a data pipeline on a laptop using Application Default Credentials from gcloud auth application-default login, but API quota errors reference the wrong project. How should they attribute the API usage to the correct project?
options: Run gcloud auth application-default set-quota-project with the intended project ID
Run gcloud auth login again in the same terminal
Set the GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS environment variable
Delete the local ADC file and re-authenticate
explain: The quota project determines which project is billed for quota when ADC credentials are used, and gcloud auth application-default set-quota-project explicitly sets it. Re-authenticating changes identity rather than quota attribution, GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS only points at a key file, and deleting the ADC file forces a fresh login without fixing the quota project.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A team following an old tutorial tries to enable the Cloud Source Repositories API in a brand-new organization and gets a 'service not found or permission denied' error. What explains this?
options: Cloud Source Repositories reached end-of-sale for new customers on June 17, 2024, so new organizations cannot enable it
The API requires an organization policy exception before first use
Source Repositories now requires a VPC Service Controls perimeter
The team must enable the API at the folder level instead of the project level
explain: Google ended sale of Cloud Source Repositories to new customers on June 17, 2024, so organizations that never enabled the API cannot start using it now and should use alternatives like Cloud Build repositories or mirrored GitHub repos. No org policy exception or perimeter is required, and APIs are enabled per project rather than per folder.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An SRE is writing a bash script that lists all running Compute Engine instances and needs only their names and zones as plain text, one per line. Which gcloud feature produces script-friendly output?
options: The --format and --filter flags, for example gcloud compute instances list --filter=status=RUNNING --format='value(name,zone)'
Piping gcloud output through the Cloud Console
The gcloud interactive shell
Enabling the gcloud beta component
explain: The --format flag reshapes gcloud output into projections like value(name,zone) and --filter selects resources server-side, which together give clean scriptable text. The console cannot be piped, the interactive shell is for humans rather than scripts, and beta components add commands rather than output formatting.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A trainer wants every Cloud Shell session to start with the same extra packages installed without manual setup each time. Which mechanism automates this?
options: Rebuild the Cloud Shell container image manually
Add the installation commands to the $HOME/.customize_environment script, which Cloud Shell runs as root at boot
Store the packages in the 5 GB persistent home directory
Add the commands to .bashrc so they run at each login
explain: Cloud Shell automatically executes $HOME/.customize_environment once as root each time the environment boots, making it the supported way to preinstall packages for every session. The persistent home directory only stores files, .bashrc runs per shell login rather than once at boot, and users cannot rebuild the underlying Cloud Shell image.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A developer starts a test web server on port 8081 inside Cloud Shell and wants to open it in a browser tab. What is the correct approach?
options: Expose the server through a Cloud Load Balancer
Use Cloud Shell's Web Preview and change the port to 8081, since Web Preview supports ports 8080 through 8084
Assign a public IP address to the Cloud Shell VM
Open port 8081 in the VPC firewall rules
explain: Cloud Shell's Web Preview creates an authenticated HTTPS proxy to a service running in the session and can target ports 8080 through 8084, so switching it to 8081 is the intended workflow. The Cloud Shell VM has no assignable public IP, VPC firewall rules do not apply to Cloud Shell, and provisioning a load balancer for a throwaway test server is unnecessary.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A public-sector agency must run workloads under strict data-residency and personnel-access controls to meet regulatory requirements. Which Google Cloud offering packages these sovereignty controls at environment creation?
options: Preemptible VMs in a regional managed instance group
Assured Workloads, which enforces data residency, access controls, and support-personnel restrictions
A standard organization with default settings
Cloud Shell with a custom environment
explain: Assured Workloads creates folders with built-in compliance guardrails such as resource location restrictions and personnel controls for regulated workloads. A default organization applies no sovereignty controls, Cloud Shell is a personal terminal rather than a compliance boundary, and preemptible VMs address cost rather than regulatory requirements.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A security team wants an organization policy that only allows specific approved machine types across the company, but no predefined constraint covers machine types. What should they do?
options: Enable uniform bucket-level access on all buckets
Create a custom organization policy constraint that restricts the allowed machine types
Write an IAM deny policy for each project
Remove the Compute Admin role from all users
explain: Custom organization policy constraints let administrators define their own rules, such as an allowed list of machine types, where no predefined constraint exists. IAM deny policies control permissions rather than resource configuration, removing Compute Admin breaks legitimate administration, and bucket access settings have nothing to do with VM machine types.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An architect wants to grant developers the ability to start and stop only the VMs tagged environment=dev, without listing each instance. Which combination achieves this?
options: Add the developers to a Google Group with the Editor role
Bind Resource Manager tags to the VMs and use an IAM condition on the tag to scope the role binding
Apply labels to the VMs and reference the labels in an IAM policy
Put the VMs in a folder and grant Compute Admin on the folder
explain: Resource Manager tags support IAM conditions, so a binding conditioned on the environment=dev tag grants rights exactly on matching resources without enumerating them. Labels cannot be referenced in IAM policies, folder-level grants would cover every VM in the folder rather than just dev ones, and the Editor group would grant broad access across all services.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An engineer shuts down the wrong project and notices 20 days later. The project contained Cloud Storage buckets with soft delete disabled. What is the expected outcome of restoring the project now?
options: Only the IAM policies are restored, not the resources
The project can be restored within the 30-day recovery window, but buckets with soft delete disabled may already be unrecoverable
The project is permanently gone because 20 days have passed
The project restores automatically with billing re-enabled
explain: Shut-down projects can be restored with resourcemanager.projects.undelete during the 30-day recovery period, so day 20 is still within the window. However, some services delete data sooner than 30 days, and buckets with soft delete disabled may be deleted immediately, while billing is not automatically re-enabled on restore.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A CISO mandates that no team may create downloadable service account keys anywhere in the organization, pushing everyone toward short-lived credentials. Which control enforces this centrally?
options: Remove the iam.serviceAccountKeys.create permission from every custom role
Enable workload identity on every GKE cluster
Enforce the constraints/iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation organization policy at the organization node
Delete all existing service accounts
explain: The iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation boolean org policy blocks creation of external service account keys across everything beneath the organization node, which is the central preventive control. Deleting service accounts breaks workloads, editing every custom role is fragile and misses predefined roles, and workload identity helps GKE workloads but does not prevent key creation elsewhere.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A landing-zone team wants new projects to stop receiving the automatic Editor grant on the Compute Engine default service account. Which organization policy constraint achieves this?
options: constraints/iam.disableServiceAccountCreation
constraints/storage.publicAccessPrevention
constraints/iam.automaticIamGrantsForDefaultServiceAccounts set to not grant the default roles
constraints/compute.requireOsLogin
explain: The iam.automaticIamGrantsForDefaultServiceAccounts constraint controls whether default service accounts automatically receive broad roles like Editor at project creation, so enforcing it stops the overprivileged default. The OS Login constraint governs SSH access, the service account creation constraint blocks new accounts rather than their grants, and the storage constraint targets public bucket access.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A company wants to ensure IAM policies can only grant access to identities in its own corporate domain, never personal Gmail accounts. Which organization policy constraint enforces this?
options: constraints/gcp.resourceLocations
constraints/iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation
constraints/iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains with the corporate domain on the allow list
constraints/compute.vmExternalIpAccess
explain: The iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains list constraint, known as domain restricted sharing, limits which identity domains can appear in IAM allow policies, blocking consumer accounts when only the corporate domain is allowed. The external IP constraint governs VM networking, the resource locations constraint governs data geography, and the key creation constraint governs service account keys.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A bank's policy forbids any VM from having a public IP address. New VMs keep getting created with ephemeral external IPs by developers. Which preventive control stops this at creation time?
options: Remove the Compute Network Admin role from developers
Enable Private Google Access on every subnet
Enforce constraints/compute.vmExternalIpAccess as a deny list covering all instances
Delete the default VPC network
explain: The compute.vmExternalIpAccess list constraint can deny external IP assignment to all VM instances, so violating create requests fail at admission time. Deleting the default network does not stop external IPs on other networks, removing Network Admin still leaves instance creators able to request external IPs, and Private Google Access only provides private API reachability without blocking public IPs.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: An EU-based retailer must keep all new storage resources inside the EU to satisfy data-residency rules. Which organization policy constraint restricts where resources can be created?
options: constraints/iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains
constraints/sql.restrictPublicIp
constraints/gcp.resourceLocations limited to EU regions
constraints/compute.storageResourceUseRestrictions
explain: The gcp.resourceLocations constraint restricts the geographic locations where supported resources can be created, making it the central control for data-residency requirements. The storage resource use constraint governs cross-project storage use rather than geography, the domain constraint governs identity sharing, and the SQL constraint governs public IP assignment on databases.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A platform team is building an internal cost-estimation tool and needs programmatic access to current Google Cloud SKU prices. Which API provides the pricing catalog?
options: The Recommender API
The Service Usage API
The Cloud Billing Catalog API, which lists SKUs and their prices
The Cloud Asset Inventory API
explain: The Cloud Billing Catalog API exposes the full SKU catalog with pricing, which is designed for programmatic price lookups in custom tooling. Asset Inventory reports resource metadata rather than prices, the Recommender API suggests optimizations rather than listing SKUs, and the Service Usage API manages API enablement rather than billing data.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A company is setting up Google Cloud for the first time and learns it needs a Google Workspace or Cloud Identity account before creating an organization resource. Why?
options: Billing accounts can only be created from a Workspace admin console
Projects cannot use custom IAM roles without Workspace
The Cloud Console login page requires a Workspace subscription
An organization resource is tied to a Google Workspace or Cloud Identity domain, which provides the identity plane for the hierarchy
explain: The organization node is the root of the resource hierarchy and is bound to the company's Workspace or Cloud Identity domain, which supplies the users and groups that IAM policies reference. Billing accounts are created in the Cloud Console, custom IAM roles work with any identity, and the console accepts any Google identity for login.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A team automating project vending hits a 'project quota exceeded' error even though the console shows fewer active projects than the quota allows. What could explain the discrepancy?
options: Folders count as projects for quota purposes
The quota only resets at the start of each month
Billing accounts consume project quota
Projects pending deletion during the 30-day recovery window still count against the project quota
explain: A shut-down project remains recoverable for 30 days and continues to count toward the project quota until it is fully deleted, so recently deleted projects explain the gap. Folders are separate resources that do not consume project quota, the quota is not calendar-based, and billing accounts have their own limits unrelated to project count.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A startup on the included Basic support plan needs faster response targets and a technical account manager as it moves production workloads to Google Cloud. What should they do?
options: Open a feature request for faster Basic support responses
Purchase additional Cloud Billing subaccounts
Enable Premium Tier networking for the organization
Upgrade to a paid support plan such as Standard, Enhanced, or Premium, which add response targets and advisory services
explain: Google Cloud's paid support plans add defined response targets and, at higher tiers, technical account management beyond what the included Basic plan offers. Feature requests do not change support entitlements, billing subaccounts affect invoicing rather than support, and Premium Tier networking improves network routing rather than support coverage.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: The finance team needs read-only visibility into billing reports and invoices but must not be able to change payment methods or close the billing account. Which role fits?
options: Billing Account Administrator, scoped to the finance folder
Project Owner on all production projects
Organization Administrator
Billing Account Viewer, which grants read access to billing information without administrative rights
explain: The Billing Account Viewer role provides read-only access to billing accounts, costs, and invoices while withholding the permissions that modify payment instruments or close accounts. Billing Account Administrator can change payments and close accounts, Project Owner grants broad resource control without focused billing visibility, and Organization Administrator is the broadest administrative role.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A company enforces an organization policy at the organization node but one folder needs a stricter variation. How do organization policies behave down the hierarchy?
options: Policies apply only to the node where they are set and never inherit
Child policies are merged with parent policies and the loosest setting wins
Only boolean constraints inherit; list constraints do not
Policies inherit from parent to child, and a child node can define its own policy to override the inherited one
explain: Organization policies flow down the resource hierarchy by inheritance, and setting a policy at a folder or project overrides the inherited parent policy for that subtree. Policies are not confined to their own node, there is no loosest-wins merge, and both boolean and list constraints follow the same inheritance model.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A developer in a new organization gets 'permission denied' when creating a project from the console. Which IAM permission must an administrator grant to allow project creation?
options: compute.instances.create on the target project
billing.accounts.create on the billing account
iam.serviceAccounts.create on the organization
resourcemanager.projects.create on the organization or folder where the project will live
explain: Creating a project requires the resourcemanager.projects.create permission on the parent organization or folder resource, which is why the grant must land on the parent rather than a project that does not exist yet. The Compute permission governs VM creation inside an existing project, billing account creation is a separate concern, and service account creation does not authorize project creation.
domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

q: A company runs 40 development VMs that are only needed during business hours on weekdays. How can they automatically stop the VMs at night and restart them in the morning to cut costs?
options: Attach an instance schedule defined in a resource policy that stops the instances at night and starts them in the morning
Convert the VMs to preemptible instances
Enable automatic restart on all instances
Move the VMs to a regional managed instance group
