explain: Instance schedules, configured through resource policies, start and stop VMs on a recurring timetable, which is the purpose-built way to power down dev environments outside business hours. Preemptible instances address pricing rather than scheduling, automatic restart recovers crashed VMs rather than stopping them nightly, and a MIG manages availability rather than time-based power states.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: An engineer needs to clone a production VM that has four attached data disks plus its boot disk, preserving all disks and the VM's configuration in one artifact. Which resource should they create?
options: A machine image, which captures the VM's configuration and all attached disks in a single restorable resource
A snapshot of the boot disk
An instance template
A custom image of the boot disk
explain: A machine image stores a VM's complete configuration along with all of its attached disks, making it the right artifact for cloning multi-disk VMs. A boot-disk snapshot or custom image captures only one disk, and an instance template defines a VM's configuration for creating new instances without copying any disk data.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A team is rolling out a new instance template to a production managed instance group but wants each VM to pick up the new template only when it is next recreated by autohealing or a manual action, avoiding an immediate mass restart. Which update type should they choose?
options: An opportunistic update, which applies the new template only when instances are recreated
A proactive update, which replaces instances immediately
A canary update with maxUnavailable set to zero
A stateful update preserving all disks
explain: Opportunistic updates defer the new template until each instance is recreated for another reason, avoiding a disruptive rolling restart. Proactive updates replace instances right away, canary is not a MIG update type, and stateful configuration preserves disks rather than controlling update timing.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: During a rolling update of a managed instance group serving live traffic, the team must guarantee that at least 90 percent of serving capacity stays available. Which settings control this?
options: maxUnavailable to cap how many instances can be down, optionally combined with maxSurge for extra temporary capacity
The autohealing health check interval
The instance redistribution type
The target distribution shape
explain: maxUnavailable limits how many instances may be simultaneously unavailable during an update, and maxSurge provisions temporary extra instances above target size, together protecting serving capacity. The health check interval tunes autohealing detection speed, while redistribution type and target distribution shape govern regional instance placement rather than update safety.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A team wants a managed instance group whose VMs are automatically spread across multiple zones so a single zone failure does not take the whole tier down. Which MIG type provides this?
options: A regional managed instance group, which distributes instances across zones in the region
A zonal managed instance group with a regional load balancer
A stateful managed instance group pinned to one zone
An unmanaged instance group with autohealing
explain: Regional MIGs automatically spread instances across the region's zones for zonal-failure resilience. A zonal MIG keeps all instances in one zone, stateful MIGs preserve per-instance state rather than spreading zones, and unmanaged instance groups support neither autoscaling nor autohealing.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A genomics batch pipeline has individual tasks that can each run for up to 36 hours with checkpointing. The team wants the cheapest interruptible VMs that can run a single task to completion without a forced 24-hour cutoff. Which provisioning model fits?
options: Spot VMs, which have no maximum runtime unlike preemptible VMs that are limited to 24 hours
Preemptible VMs, which are cheaper than Spot VMs
Standard VMs with committed use discounts
Sole-tenant nodes for the batch workers
explain: Spot VMs impose no maximum runtime, so a 36-hour checkpointed task can run to completion, while preemptible VMs are forcibly terminated after 24 hours. Preemptible VMs share Spot pricing rather than beating it, standard VMs with CUDs cost more than interruptible capacity, and sole-tenant nodes serve compliance isolation rather than cheap batch compute.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A company has steady but shifting spend across Compute Engine, Cloud SQL, and GKE, and wants a discount commitment that is not tied to specific machine types or regions. Which commitment type fits?
options: Flexible committed use discounts, which commit to a spend amount that applies across eligible services
Resource-based committed use discounts tied to specific machine types
Sustained use discounts on preemptible VMs
Spot VMs with a one-year reservation
explain: Flexible committed use discounts are spend-based commitments that float across services and regions as usage shifts, matching variable-but-steady spend. Resource-based CUDs lock to specific machine families and regions, sustained use discounts apply automatically rather than by commitment and exclude preemptible VMs, and Spot VMs cannot be reserved for a term.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A high-frequency trading database needs the highest available provisioned IOPS for a single volume on Compute Engine. Which disk type should they choose?
options: A standard persistent disk, which has higher IOPS caps
Hyperdisk Extreme, which offers the highest provisioned IOPS of the Hyperdisk family
Hyperdisk Throughput, which maximizes IOPS per dollar
Hyperdisk Balanced, which is the best fit for most workloads
explain: Hyperdisk Extreme is the IOPS-optimized Hyperdisk type with the highest provisionable IOPS, designed for demanding databases. Hyperdisk Throughput optimizes cost-efficient throughput rather than IOPS, Balanced targets general workloads, and standard persistent disks have lower performance ceilings than Hyperdisk Extreme.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A rendering job needs very high local I/O for temporary scratch files during processing, and losing the data if the VM stops is acceptable. Which storage option fits best?
options: A Cloud Storage bucket mounted for scratch I/O
Local SSDs, which provide ephemeral high-performance NVMe storage that is lost when the VM stops
A Hyperdisk Balanced volume for scratch space
A regional persistent disk for temporary files
explain: Local SSDs are physically attached NVMe disks with very high IOPS for scratch and cache workloads, and their data does not survive a VM stop or termination. Hyperdisk and persistent disks are network-attached durable storage that persist independently, while Cloud Storage is object storage unsuited to high-IOPS scratch I/O.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A Cloud Run service must reach a Memorystore instance using private RFC 1918 addresses, and the team wants to avoid managing a Serverless VPC Access connector. What should they configure?
options: Cloud NAT with a static external IP
Direct VPC egress on the Cloud Run service, which routes traffic to the VPC without a connector
A Serverless VPC Access connector in each region
A public IP allowlist on the Memorystore instance
explain: Direct VPC egress lets second-generation Cloud Run services send traffic straight into a VPC network with no connector to provision or scale. A connector is the older approach this scenario wants to avoid, Memorystore has no public IP allowlisting, and Cloud NAT provides outbound internet access rather than private VPC reachability.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A Cloud Run service runs background threads that continue processing after the HTTP response is sent. Which CPU allocation setting keeps the instance's CPU available outside request handling?
options: Enabling minimum instances
CPU always allocated, so the instance keeps CPU even when not processing a request
CPU allocated only during request processing, which covers background threads
Setting concurrency to 1000
explain: With CPU always allocated, the container instance retains CPU outside the request lifecycle, which background work after the response requires. The default request-scoped allocation throttles CPU between requests, concurrency controls simultaneous requests rather than CPU availability, and minimum instances reduce cold starts without changing CPU allocation.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A team wants their Cloud Run service behind a global external HTTPS load balancer so they can use Cloud CDN caching and Cloud Armor policies in front of it. Which backend type connects the load balancer to Cloud Run?
options: A backend bucket referencing the service URL
A serverless network endpoint group (NEG) pointing at the Cloud Run service
An unmanaged instance group containing the Cloud Run revisions
A zonal NEG with the service's container IP addresses
explain: Serverless NEGs are the purpose-built backend for routing from a load balancer to Cloud Run, Cloud Functions, or App Engine, unlocking CDN and Armor features. Unmanaged instance groups only target VM instances, zonal NEGs target Compute Engine endpoints rather than serverless services, and backend buckets serve Cloud Storage content rather than dynamic services.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A team is migrating a long-running HTTP-triggered ETL function that needs up to 45 minutes per invocation. The current 1st gen function is killed at 9 minutes. Which change unblocks the migration?
options: Enable retries on the 1st gen function
Redeploy as a 2nd gen function, which supports up to 60 minutes for HTTP-triggered executions
Increase the 1st gen timeout setting to 45 minutes
Split the function across two 1st gen functions chained by Pub/Sub
explain: Second-generation Cloud Functions, built on Cloud Run and Eventarc, allow HTTP-triggered executions up to 60 minutes, comfortably covering a 45-minute ETL run. First-generation functions cap at 540 seconds with no override, chaining adds complexity without removing the per-invocation cap, and retries re-execute rather than extend the timeout.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: An order-processing system publishes events with an ordering key per customer and requires that each customer's messages are delivered in publish order. What must be true of the subscription?
options: The subscription must use a push endpoint with OIDC
The topic must use a schema with an ordering field
Message ordering must be enabled on the subscription, and publishers must set the ordering key
Exactly-once delivery must be enabled instead of ordering
explain: Pub/Sub delivers messages with the same ordering key in publish order only when message ordering is enabled on the subscription and publishers populate the ordering key. Exactly-once delivery is a separate redelivery guarantee, push with OIDC concerns endpoint authentication, and schemas validate payload structure rather than controlling delivery order.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A payment pipeline cannot tolerate processing the same Pub/Sub message twice, even at the cost of lower throughput. Which subscription setting provides the strongest deduplication guarantee?
options: Set the acknowledgment deadline to 600 seconds
Enable retain-acked-messages on the subscription
Enable exactly-once delivery on the subscription
Enable message ordering on the subscription
explain: Exactly-once delivery guarantees a message is not redelivered before its acknowledgment deadline expires and an acknowledged message is never resent, which is the strongest built-in deduplication. Ordering controls sequence rather than duplication, the ack deadline only tunes redelivery timing, and retaining acknowledged messages enables replay rather than preventing duplicates.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A team wants streaming event data to land directly in a BigQuery table without running Dataflow or a subscriber service. Which subscription type does this with no intermediary?
options: A pull subscription polled by a Cloud Scheduler job
A Cloud Storage subscription with a BigQuery external table
A BigQuery subscription that writes messages straight to the table
A push subscription to a Cloud Run service that loads BigQuery
explain: BigQuery subscriptions deliver Pub/Sub messages directly into a BigQuery table, with the Pub/Sub service agent needing write permission on the table. A push-to-Cloud-Run design adds a service to maintain, Scheduler polling is batch rather than streaming, and Cloud Storage subscriptions land files in buckets rather than native BigQuery rows.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A subscriber outage lasted 10 days, and the team wants to replay the unacknowledged messages published during the outage. The subscription used default settings. What is the outcome?
options: The dead-letter topic holds the messages indefinitely
Seek can recover messages regardless of the retention window
Messages older than the 7-day default retention are gone; extend message retention up to 31 days for future outages
All 10 days of messages are replayable because the backlog is unbounded
explain: Pub/Sub retains unacknowledged messages for 7 days by default and at most 31 days, so days 8 through 10 of the outage are already discarded. The backlog is bounded rather than unbounded, dead-letter topics only receive repeatedly undeliverable messages, and Seek can only travel within the retention window.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A media company stores assets with unpredictable access patterns and wants storage classes to adjust automatically instead of writing lifecycle rules per prefix. Which bucket feature does this?
options: Bucket Lock with a retention policy
Dual-region replication with turbo replication
Autoclass, which automatically transitions objects between storage classes based on access
Object Lifecycle Management with age-based rules
explain: Autoclass manages storage class transitions automatically per object based on access patterns, removing the need for hand-written lifecycle rules. Lifecycle rules require explicit conditions per prefix, Bucket Lock enforces retention rather than cost optimization, and turbo replication addresses cross-region RPO rather than storage classing.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: An engineer accidentally deletes a production object on Friday evening and discovers it Monday morning. The bucket uses default settings. Can the object be recovered?
options: Yes, but only if object versioning was also enabled
No, soft delete only protects buckets, not objects
Yes, soft delete is enabled by default with a 7-day retention, so the object can be restored within that window
No, deleted objects are permanently removed immediately
explain: Soft delete is on by default for new buckets with a seven-day retention duration, so a Friday deletion is restorable on Monday. Deleted objects enter a soft-deleted state rather than vanishing, versioning is a separate complementary feature rather than a prerequisite, and soft delete protects both objects and buckets.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A financial firm needs newly written objects replicated to a second region within 15 minutes for its disaster recovery target. Which configuration meets this?
options: A multi-region bucket with turbo replication enabled
A dual-region bucket with default replication
Two regional buckets synced by a transfer job
A dual-region bucket with turbo replication, which targets a 15-minute RPO
explain: Turbo replication is available on dual-region buckets and targets replication of new objects within 15 minutes. Turbo replication cannot be enabled on multi-region buckets, default replication targets a far longer window, and transfer jobs are scheduled copies rather than continuous replication with an RPO target.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A team creates a Firestore database in Datastore mode for a server backend, then later decides they want Native mode's real-time sync for a new mobile app in the same project. What is the correct path?
options: Run gcloud firestore databases update to switch the existing database to Native mode
Enable real-time sync as a per-collection setting on the Datastore mode database
Export and reimport the data into the same database to convert its mode
Create a new Firestore database in Native mode, since the mode is selected at creation and cannot be changed afterward
explain: The Firestore data access mode is chosen when the database is created and cannot be changed afterward, so the mobile app needs its own new Native mode database. The update command cannot convert a populated database's mode, real-time sync is a Native mode capability rather than a toggle, and reimporting into the same database does not change its mode.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A team wants a fully managed in-memory cache on Google Cloud using a permissively licensed open-source Redis alternative after the Redis licensing change. Which Memorystore option fits?
options: Memorystore for Redis with a custom license
A self-managed Redis on Compute Engine
Memorystore for Memcached with persistence enabled
Memorystore for Valkey, the managed service for the open-source Valkey engine
explain: Memorystore for Valkey is Google Cloud's managed offering for Valkey, the Linux Foundation open-source fork created after Redis changed its licensing. Memorystore for Redis remains the Redis-engine option rather than a licensing workaround, self-managing Redis forfeits the managed service benefits, and Memcached is a different engine without Valkey's data structures.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A healthcare company creates a BigQuery dataset in the EU multi-region for compliance, then later wants to move it to a US region to co-locate with analysts. What is possible?
options: Update the dataset location in the console and the data migrates automatically
Move the dataset with the bq update command
Change the location by editing the dataset's labels
The dataset location cannot be changed after creation; they must create a new dataset and copy the data
explain: A BigQuery dataset's location is immutable after creation, so meeting a new residency requirement means creating a dataset in the target location and copying tables over. The console offers no location migration, the bq CLI cannot relocate a dataset, and labels are metadata tags with no effect on data placement.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: Analysts need to query aggregated sales metrics, but compliance forbids them from accessing the raw customer tables the metrics are built on. How can they query the aggregates without raw-table access?
options: Grant the analysts the BigQuery Data Viewer role on the raw tables
Copy the raw tables into the analysts' project
Create a scheduled query that emails the analysts CSV files
Create an authorized view over the raw tables and grant the analysts access only to the view
explain: An authorized view lets users query its results when the view itself is authorized on the source dataset, without granting them any access to the underlying tables. Granting Data Viewer on raw tables violates the compliance constraint, copying tables duplicates sensitive data, and emailed CSVs bypass governance rather than enforcing it.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: Two engineers run Terraform against the same Google Cloud environment and want to prevent simultaneous applies from corrupting the shared state file. Which backend setup addresses this?
options: Store the state file on a shared Cloud Storage bucket without a backend block
Use the local backend with the state file in version control
Disable state locking to let both applies proceed in parallel
Use the GCS backend, which provides native state locking, and enable object versioning on the state bucket for recovery
explain: The Terraform GCS backend supports native state locking so concurrent operations serialize instead of corrupting state, and HashiCorp recommends object versioning on the bucket for recovery from accidental damage. A bare bucket without a backend block gives no locking, local state in version control cannot coordinate concurrent runs, and disabling locking invites the very corruption the team wants to avoid.
domain: Section 2: Planning and implementing a cloud solution

q: A managed service provider operates 12 customer projects and wants one alerting policy that fires when any VM across all customer projects exceeds 90 percent CPU for 5 minutes. Alerting policies can only see metrics in their scope. What should they configure?
options: Create the alerting policy in a monitoring project whose metrics scope includes all 12 customer projects
Create the same alerting policy separately in each of the 12 projects
Export CPU metrics from each project to BigQuery and alert there
Enable uptime checks from each customer project
explain: Alerting policies evaluate metrics visible in their project's metrics scope, so scoping all customer projects into one monitoring project lets a single policy cover every VM. Duplicating the policy per project creates 12 policies to maintain, BigQuery exports cannot drive Monitoring alerts, and uptime checks test external availability rather than VM CPU.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A team has a 99.9% availability SLO and wants to be paged only when the error budget is being consumed fast enough to exhaust it well before the 30-day window ends. Which alerting approach fits?
options: A burn-rate alert that pages when budget consumption over short and long windows exceeds the sustainable rate
A static threshold alert on total error count
An uptime check on the homepage every minute
A log-based metric counting 500 responses
explain: Burn-rate alerting compares error budget consumption against the rate that would exhaust the budget in the SLO window, using paired short and long windows to page only on genuinely fast burns. A static error count ignores the budget entirely, uptime checks measure availability from outside without budget math, and a log-based count is just an input signal without burn-rate logic.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A team wants to alert on the 99th percentile of request latency extracted from application logs, not just the average. Which log-based metric type supports percentile calculations?
options: A distribution log-based metric, which records values into histogram buckets for percentile computation
A counter log-based metric on the latency field
A gauge metric scraped by the Ops Agent
An uptime check with latency thresholds
explain: Distribution log-based metrics bucket extracted numeric values into histograms, enabling percentile and heatmap queries in alerting policies. Counter metrics only count matching log entries, Ops Agent gauges collect host metrics rather than log-derived latencies, and uptime checks measure synthetic probe latency rather than application log data.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: To reduce log storage costs, an admin creates an exclusion filter that drops DEBUG logs at ingestion. A week later a developer asks to search those DEBUG logs for an incident. What is the outcome?
options: The excluded logs were discarded before storage and cannot be searched; only future logs can be captured by removing the exclusion
The logs are still available in the _Default bucket for 30 days
The exclusion filter only hides the logs from the Logs Explorer
A log sink can retroactively recover the excluded logs
explain: Exclusion filters discard matching log entries before they are stored, so they incur no storage cost but are permanently unqueryable. They are not a view-level hide, the _Default bucket only holds what ingestion kept, and sinks route copies of ingested entries rather than resurrecting discarded ones.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A compliance team requires application logs to be retained for exactly 3 years with a guarantee that nobody, including administrators, can shorten the retention. Which log bucket configuration provides this?
options: Create a log bucket with a 3-year retention period and lock it
Set the _Default bucket retention to 3 years
Create a log sink to Cloud Storage with a 3-year lifecycle rule
Enable Data Access audit logs for 3 years
explain: Locking a log bucket prevents its retention period from being reduced or the bucket from being deleted until every retained entry ages out, which is the immutability guarantee compliance needs. The _Default bucket cannot be locked against retention reduction, a sink copy in Cloud Storage is a separate dataset rather than the logging store itself, and Data Access logs only control which audit entries exist.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A support vendor needs to see only error logs from one application, while the bucket also holds sensitive debug payloads the vendor must never see. How can the team grant this scoped access?
options: Create a log view on the bucket filtered to the application's error logs and grant the vendor access to the view
Grant the vendor the Logs Viewer role on the whole project
Create a log sink that copies errors to a second project
Add an exclusion filter for the debug payloads
explain: Log views expose an IAM-controllable subset of a bucket's entries defined by a filter, so the vendor sees only the application's error logs. Project-wide Logs Viewer would expose everything, a sink duplicates data into another project rather than scoping access in place, and exclusion filters destroy the debug logs for everyone rather than hiding them from one party.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: An analyst wants to run SQL queries joining error counts by service across millions of log entries without exporting anything. Which Cloud Logging capability supports this?
options: Stream the logs to Pub/Sub and query the topic
Upgrade the log bucket to use Log Analytics and query it with SQL
Write the queries in the Logs Explorer query language
Create a log-based metric for each service
explain: Log Analytics upgrades a bucket so its entries can be queried with BigQuery-standard SQL, supporting joins and aggregations over large log volumes in place. The Logs Explorer query language filters entries but is not SQL with joins, log-based metrics pre-aggregate single values rather than ad-hoc analysis, and Pub/Sub topics are streams that cannot be queried historically.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: An auditor asks how long Admin Activity audit logs are kept and whether anyone could have shortened that retention. What is accurate?
options: They are kept for 400 days but an admin can reduce it to 30 days
They are stored in the _Required bucket for 400 days with retention that cannot be changed or deleted
They are kept in the _Default bucket for 30 days unless extended
They follow the retention of whichever sink the admin configured
explain: The _Required bucket holds Admin Activity and other compliance logs with a fixed 400-day retention that is not configurable, and the bucket itself cannot be deleted. The _Default bucket's 30-day retention applies to other log types, sinks create separate copies rather than governing the originals, and no administrator can shorten the _Required retention.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A German company requires that all log data remain stored in the EU. The default log buckets replicate globally. What should they configure?
options: Create an exclusion filter for non-EU logs
Create user-defined log buckets in an EU region and route logs to them with sinks
Enable CMEK on the _Default bucket
Lock the _Default bucket
explain: User-defined log buckets can be created in a chosen region, and sinks route log entries into them, giving control over log data residency. CMEK changes encryption key management rather than storage location, locking affects retention immutability rather than geography, and exclusion filters discard entries instead of relocating them.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A team wants their uptime check to fail not only when the site is down but also when it serves an error page with HTTP 200. Which uptime check feature catches this?
options: Enabling alerting on check latency
Content matching, which validates that the response body contains expected text
Increasing the check frequency to every minute
Adding more geographic checkers
explain: Content matching inspects the response body for required text, so a 200 response serving an error page fails the check. Higher frequency only detects outages sooner, more checkers improve geographic coverage rather than response validation, and latency alerting measures speed rather than correctness.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A fleet still runs the legacy Monitoring and Logging agents, and the team wants to consolidate on the single modern agent. What is the recommended migration step?
options: Disable the Ops Agent and keep the legacy agents
Install the Ops Agent and remove the legacy agents, since running both causes duplicate data
Install the Ops Agent alongside the legacy agents for redundancy
Upgrade the legacy agents in place to the Ops Agent
explain: The Ops Agent is the unified successor to the legacy Monitoring and Logging agents, and Google recommends replacing them because running both produces duplicated metrics and logs. Side-by-side operation is the duplication problem rather than redundancy, there is no in-place upgrade path between the separate products, and staying on legacy agents forfeits current features.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: An engineer is troubleshooting a VM whose SSH daemon is broken and needs interactive shell access through the serial console. What must be in place for this to work?
options: The Ops Agent installed on the VM
Serial port access enabled via instance metadata and a project-wide SSH key, then connect with gcloud compute connect-to-serial-port
An external IP address on the VM
A firewall rule opening port 22 to the internet
explain: The interactive serial console requires serial port access enabled in metadata plus an SSH key in project metadata for authentication, and it works even when the network path or SSH daemon is broken. No external IP is needed since access goes through the Google Cloud API, firewall rules govern network SSH rather than the serial console, and the Ops Agent is unrelated to console access.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A VM has no public IP address, and corporate policy blocks opening SSH to the internet. The engineer still needs an SSH session from their laptop. Which command establishes it?
options: Adding a firewall rule allowing 0.0.0.0/0 on port 22
Assigning an ephemeral external IP temporarily
gcloud compute ssh with the --tunnel-through-iap flag
gcloud compute ssh with the --external-ip flag
explain: The --tunnel-through-iap flag tunnels the SSH session through Identity-Aware Proxy, reaching private VMs without any public IP or internet-exposed port. There is no --external-ip flag for this purpose, opening SSH to the world violates the stated policy, and assigning a public IP defeats the no-public-IP design.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A security team needs a centralized view of OS patch compliance across thousands of VMs and the ability to roll out patches on a schedule. Which service provides this?
options: Instance schedules on each VM
Cloud Build triggers on a cron schedule
VM Manager with OS policies and patch management
Cloud Deploy with a patch pipeline
explain: VM Manager's OS Config services provide patch compliance dashboards and scheduled patch deployments across fleets. Cloud Deploy releases applications rather than OS patches, instance schedules only start and stop VMs, and Cloud Build triggers build containers rather than managing OS patch state.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A company wants agentless, policy-based backup of Compute Engine VMs and Cloud SQL instances with centralized recovery vaults, without building their own backup infrastructure. Which service fits?
options: Cloud Storage versioning on backup buckets
Filestore backups for each instance
The Backup and DR service, which provides managed backup and recovery for VMs and databases
Persistent disk snapshots taken manually per VM
explain: The Backup and DR service is Google Cloud's managed backup offering with backup plans, vaults, and application-consistent recovery for supported workloads. Manual snapshots lack centralized policy management, GCS versioning protects objects rather than VM state, and Filestore backups cover file shares rather than VM or database recovery.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A team must keep monthly VM disk snapshots for 7 years for compliance but rarely restores them, and standard snapshot storage costs are too high. Which snapshot type reduces long-term cost?
options: Regional snapshots replicated to every zone
Disk clones instead of snapshots
Archive snapshots, which offer lower-cost storage for infrequently accessed snapshots
Instant snapshots, which are optimized for rapid cloning
explain: Archive snapshots are the low-cost tier for snapshot data kept beyond a year and accessed rarely, matching a 7-year compliance retention need. Instant snapshots optimize for fast disk creation rather than cost, snapshots are regional resources rather than per-zone copies, and clones are full-cost disks rather than cheaper snapshot storage.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A database VM needs crash-consistent disk snapshots every 6 hours with automatic deletion of snapshots older than 14 days. Which approach implements this?
options: An instance schedule that stops the VM every 6 hours
Manual snapshots taken during maintenance windows
A snapshot schedule with a 6-hour frequency and a 14-day retention policy attached to the disk
A Cloud Scheduler job that emails an admin every 6 hours
explain: Snapshot schedules automate recurring disk snapshots at a set interval and enforce a retention policy that deletes old snapshots. Cloud Scheduler cannot take disk snapshots, instance schedules control VM power state rather than data protection, and manual snapshots do not scale and lack retention enforcement.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A developer needs a trace for one specific failing request to debug latency, but the default sampling did not capture it. How can they force Cloud Trace to record that request's trace?
options: Restart the application with tracing disabled
Query Cloud Trace with a higher time range
Send the request with an X-Cloud-Trace-Context header requesting tracing
Increase the global sampling rate to 100 percent permanently
explain: The X-Cloud-Trace-Context header lets a caller force a trace for an individual request regardless of the configured sampling rate. Raising global sampling to 100 percent is wasteful for one request, restarting without tracing removes visibility, and widening the query window cannot surface a trace that was never recorded.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: After a deploy, the on-call engineer wants to see which new exceptions appeared in production, grouped by root cause, and mark them resolved after a fix. Which service provides this workflow?
options: Cloud Profiler, which groups stack samples
The Logs Explorer, which requires manual grouping
Error Reporting, which automatically groups exceptions and tracks resolution state
Cloud Trace, which groups latency spans
explain: Error Reporting parses exceptions from logs, groups occurrences by inferred root cause, and lets engineers mark issues resolved to track regressions across deploys. Cloud Trace analyzes request latency rather than exceptions, Profiler samples CPU and memory rather than errors, and Logs Explorer shows raw entries without automatic grouping or resolution tracking.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A security analyst needs to determine who read a sensitive object in Cloud Storage last week. Admin Activity logs show no read entries. What must be enabled to answer this going forward?
options: System Event audit logs, which record reads
VPC Flow Logs on the storage subnet
Cloud Trace on the storage bucket
Data Access audit logs for Cloud Storage, which record read operations but are disabled by default
explain: Data Access audit logs capture read and write data operations, but they are disabled by default for most services to control volume, so enabling them is required for future read investigations. Admin Activity logs record configuration changes rather than data reads, System Event logs record Google-initiated actions, flow logs capture network metadata rather than API reads, and Trace measures latency.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A VM cannot reach a database VM, and the team suspects a firewall rule is dropping the traffic. Which logging feature shows the allowed and denied flows for the subnet?
options: Cloud DNS query logging
Cloud NAT logging on the router
Serial port output of the VM
VPC Flow Logs enabled on the subnet, recording connection outcomes
explain: VPC Flow Logs record network flows with allow or deny verdicts per subnet, directly revealing firewall drops. DNS query logging shows name resolution rather than connection verdicts, NAT logging covers address translation rather than firewall decisions, and serial output shows boot logs rather than network flows.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A firewall rule is suspected of being unused, and the team wants evidence of how many connections it matched before deleting it. Which feature provides per-rule hit counts?
options: VPC Flow Logs, which attribute matches to specific rules by default
Cloud Audit Logs, which record firewall rule evaluations
The firewall rule's description field
Firewall Rules Logging, which logs connections matched by rules with logging enabled
explain: Firewall Rules Logging records an entry for each connection a logging-enabled rule allows or denies, giving per-rule usage evidence. Flow logs show subnet-level verdicts without rule attribution by default, audit logs record rule administration rather than traffic matches, and descriptions are free text with no telemetry.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A security team wants to feed a copy of production VM traffic to their third-party intrusion detection appliance without installing agents on the VMs. Which feature mirrors the traffic?
options: VPC Flow Logs, which forward full packet payloads
Cloud IDS, which is a third-party appliance
An internal load balancer in front of the VMs
Packet Mirroring, which copies traffic from selected instances to a collector destination
explain: Packet Mirroring duplicates raw traffic from mirrored sources to a collector such as an IDS appliance, with no agent required on the workloads. Flow logs export 5-tuple metadata rather than packet payloads, Cloud IDS is Google's managed IDS rather than a third-party appliance feed, and a load balancer distributes traffic rather than copying it.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: In a hybrid environment, applications need to discover service endpoints by name across VPCs and on-premises without hardcoding IP addresses. Which service provides this service registry?
options: Cloud DNS private zones for each service IP
A spreadsheet of IP addresses in Cloud Storage
VPC peering between every network
Service Directory, which offers a central registry for discovering services by name
explain: Service Directory is the managed service registry where services register endpoints and clients resolve them by name across networks. Private DNS zones map names to IPs but lack a service registration model, a spreadsheet is not a discovery mechanism, and peering provides connectivity rather than name-based discovery.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A team needs faster recovery than restoring from backups but cannot afford a fully running duplicate environment. Which disaster recovery strategy keeps minimal core services running and scales up on failover?
options: Backup and restore, which has the fastest recovery time
Multi-site active-active, which is the cheapest option
Archiving data to Coldline storage
Pilot light, which maintains a minimal live footprint that scales to full capacity during failover
explain: Pilot light keeps essential services running at minimal scale so failover mainly involves scaling up, landing between backup-restore and active-active on both cost and recovery time. Backup and restore is the cheapest but slowest strategy, active-active is the fastest but most expensive, and archival storage addresses retention rather than recovery speed.
domain: Section 3: Ensuring the successful operation of a cloud solution

q: A developer reports 'permission denied' when trying to publish to a Pub/Sub topic, and the admin needs to determine exactly which policy grants or denies the access. Which tool answers this?
options: Policy Troubleshooter, which evaluates why a principal does or does not have access to a resource
Policy Simulator, which tests hypothetical policy changes
The IAM recommender, which suggests least-privilege roles
Cloud Audit Logs, which show who changed the policy
explain: Policy Troubleshooter analyzes the effective IAM policies to explain an actual access decision for a specific principal, action, and resource. Policy Simulator previews the impact of proposed changes rather than diagnosing current denials, the recommender suggests role right-sizing rather than explaining a denial, and audit logs record who modified policies rather than evaluating access.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A contractor needs BigQuery Data Viewer access for exactly the two weeks of an audit, after which access must disappear automatically. Which approach enforces the expiry without manual cleanup?
options: Add an IAM condition with a time-bound CEL expression on the role binding
Grant the role and set a calendar reminder to remove it
Create a custom role that expires automatically
Enable the contractor's access through a service account key
explain: IAM Conditions support CEL expressions such as request.time comparisons, so a binding can automatically stop granting access after the audit window. Calendar reminders rely on humans and fail silently, IAM roles have no built-in expiry, and service account keys are long-lived credentials that worsen the problem.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A team wants to share a training video stored in Cloud Storage with the general public, including people without Google accounts. Which IAM grant makes the object publicly readable?
options: Grant allUsers the Storage Object Viewer role on the bucket or object
Grant allAuthenticatedUsers the Storage Object Viewer role
Grant the company's Google Group the Storage Object Viewer role
Enable uniform bucket-level access on the bucket
explain: The allUsers principal includes everyone on the internet, including people without Google accounts, while allAuthenticatedUsers only covers signed-in Google identities. A company group limits access to members, and uniform bucket-level access changes the access model rather than granting public read.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A team is about to enforce a new VPC Service Controls perimeter around BigQuery and Cloud Storage but fears breaking existing data pipelines. What is the recommended first step?
options: Create the perimeter in dry-run mode to log would-be violations without blocking traffic
Enforce the perimeter immediately and roll back if pipelines fail
Exclude BigQuery from the perimeter permanently
Disable VPC Service Controls for the projects
explain: Dry-run mode logs violations as though the perimeter were enforced while still allowing the traffic, letting the team find and fix pipeline issues before enforcement. Enforcing immediately risks production breakage, permanently excluding BigQuery defeats the data-protection goal, and disabling the control abandons the security objective.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A company wants its VPC Service Controls perimeter to allow access from corporate office IP ranges and compliant devices, but block everything else. Which Access Context Manager construct expresses these conditions?
options: An access level combining IP subnetworks and device policy conditions
A VPC firewall rule allowing the office CIDR ranges
An IAM condition on the perimeter projects
A Cloud Armor policy with IP allowlisting
explain: Access levels define contextual conditions such as IP ranges and device compliance that grant entry through a perimeter. VPC firewall rules govern VM traffic rather than perimeter API access, IAM conditions scope role bindings rather than perimeter entry, and Cloud Armor protects load balancers rather than VPC Service Controls perimeters.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: Two enforced VPC Service Controls perimeters host related projects, and a BigQuery job in one perimeter needs to read from a Cloud Storage bucket in the other. How can this be allowed without merging the perimeters?
options: Create a perimeter bridge permitting the specific cross-perimeter communication
Add all projects to a single perimeter
Copy the bucket into the first perimeter's project
Allow allUsers access to the bucket
explain: A perimeter bridge authorizes defined data flows between two perimeters while keeping their boundaries intact. Merging perimeters destroys the intended isolation, copying data duplicates it and complicates governance, and public access abandons the exfiltration protection entirely.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A regulated bank must keep its encryption keys in its own on-premises hardware security module while using BigQuery CMEK. Which key management option keeps the key material outside Google Cloud?
options: Google-managed encryption keys with rotation
External Key Manager (EKM), which stores keys in the external system and serves them over a connection
Cloud KMS with a software-protected key ring
Customer-supplied encryption keys (CSEK) for BigQuery
explain: EKM lets Cloud KMS use keys held in an external key management system, so key material never resides in Google Cloud. Software Cloud KMS keys live in Google's infrastructure, CSEK is not supported for BigQuery CMEK workflows, and Google-managed keys keep custody with Google.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A team encrypts individual Cloud Storage objects with keys they generate and manage entirely themselves, providing the key with each upload request. Which encryption option are they using?
options: External Key Manager (EKM)
Customer-supplied encryption keys (CSEK), where Google never stores the key
Customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) via Cloud KMS
Google-managed encryption keys
explain: With CSEK, the customer supplies the AES-256 key with each request and Google does not retain it, matching the described workflow. CMEK references keys stored in Cloud KMS, Google-managed keys are fully Google-controlled, and EKM serves keys from an external system rather than per-request customer supply.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A data science team needs realistic customer data for model training, but raw PII cannot leave the secure project. Which DLP technique preserves format and statistical properties while removing the real values?
options: A log sink that copies the raw tables
De-identification with format-preserving encryption or tokenization
Redaction that deletes the PII columns entirely
Inspection that only reports where PII exists
explain: DLP de-identification transforms sensitive values with techniques like format-preserving encryption and tokenization, keeping data useful for training without exposing real PII. Redaction destroys the columns' analytical value, inspection only finds PII without transforming it, and a log sink copies data rather than protecting it.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: New files land in a Cloud Storage bucket every hour, and the privacy team wants each file automatically inspected for credit card numbers on arrival. Which DLP feature schedules recurring inspections?
options: A Pub/Sub notification without any DLP job
A DLP job trigger that runs inspection jobs on the bucket on a schedule
A one-time DLP inspection job run manually
A Cloud Scheduler job that lists bucket objects
explain: DLP job triggers automatically launch inspection jobs against new or updated data on a schedule, which is the hands-off recurring pattern. One-time jobs require manual reruns, a Scheduler listing job does not inspect content, and a bare Pub/Sub notification carries no DLP inspection logic.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: Before publishing an anonymized dataset, a privacy officer wants to measure how easily individuals could be re-identified from quasi-identifiers like age and ZIP code. Which DLP analysis quantifies this?
options: A Cloud Audit Log review of dataset access
Risk analysis measuring k-anonymity and related re-identification metrics
An inspection job listing infoTypes found
A de-identification job replacing the identifiers
explain: DLP risk analysis computes metrics like k-anonymity, l-diversity, and k-map against the dataset to quantify re-identification risk from quasi-identifiers. Inspection only locates sensitive data, de-identification transforms it without measuring residual risk, and audit logs record access events rather than statistical disclosure risk.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A mobile app needs to let users download private training videos stored in Cloud Storage without making the bucket public and without proxying every byte through the app backend. Which mechanism grants time-limited direct access?
options: Enabling Requester Pays on the bucket
Signed URLs, which grant temporary authenticated access to specific objects
Making the bucket publicly readable
Granting each user the Storage Object Viewer role
explain: Signed URLs embed a cryptographic signature and expiry, letting clients fetch specific private objects directly for a limited time. Public buckets expose everything permanently, per-user IAM grants are unmanageable for app audiences, and Requester Pays shifts cost attribution rather than granting access.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A web application lets users upload profile photos directly to Cloud Storage from the browser via an HTML form POST, with constraints on file size and type enforced at upload time. Which mechanism supports this?
options: A public bucket with an HTML form
IAM roles granted to anonymous users
A signed policy document that authorizes the constrained browser upload
A signed URL, which cannot enforce form-field conditions like content type and size
explain: Signed policy documents authorize HTML form uploads directly to Cloud Storage with enforceable conditions on size, type, and key naming. Signed URLs cannot express declarative form-field conditions, public buckets abandon access control, and IAM cannot grant rights to anonymous users.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: An organization wants a guarantee that no bucket can ever be made publicly accessible, even by mistake. Which organization policy constraint enforces this?
options: Quarterly manual audits of bucket IAM policies
Removing the Storage Admin role from users
constraints/storage.publicAccessPrevention enforced at the organization
constraints/storage.uniformBucketLevelAccess
explain: The storage.publicAccessPrevention org policy blocks any grant of public access to buckets, which is the preventive organization-wide guarantee. Uniform bucket-level access standardizes ACL usage rather than blocking public grants, manual audits detect mistakes after the fact rather than preventing them, and removing Storage Admin breaks legitimate administration.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A single sales table contains rows for all regions, but each regional manager must only see their own region's rows when querying the table directly. Which BigQuery feature enforces this?
options: Column-level security masking the region column
Dataset-level IAM granting Data Viewer to all managers
Row-level security with a filter based on the session user's region
An authorized view that selects all rows
explain: Row-level security applies a row filter evaluating the current user, so each manager querying the table sees only their region's rows. An authorized view selecting everything enforces nothing, column-level security masks columns rather than filtering rows, and dataset-level Data Viewer grants full-table access to everyone.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: Analysts need to query a customer table but must never see the national ID column, while the fraud team needs the full table. Which feature hides just that column from the analysts?
options: An authorized view excluding the fraud team's queries
Splitting the table into two datasets
Column-level security using policy tags on the national ID column
Row-level security filtering analyst rows
explain: Column-level security with policy tags restricts the national ID column to principals granted the Fine-Grained Reader role on the taxonomy, while other columns remain queryable. Row-level security filters rows rather than columns, an authorized view excluding the fraud team inverts the requirement, and splitting tables duplicates data and complicates governance.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A team wants database logins on Cloud SQL for MySQL to use short-lived tokens tied to Google identities instead of shared passwords in application config. Which authentication approach provides this?
options: The Cloud SQL Auth Proxy without IAM configuration
Connecting over public IP with SSL
IAM database authentication, which authenticates with short-lived access tokens
Built-in authentication with a strong shared password
explain: IAM database authentication lets users and service accounts log in with temporary IAM access tokens instead of passwords, enabled via the cloudsql_iam_authentication flag. Built-in authentication relies on stored passwords, the Auth Proxy alone does not change the credential type, and SSL over public IP encrypts transport without replacing passwords.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A security team wants continuous detection of misconfigurations like public buckets and open firewall rules across the organization. Which Security Command Center capability provides this?
options: Cloud Asset Inventory, which only lists resources
VPC Flow Logs, which record network traffic
Security Health Analytics, which scans for misconfigurations and reports findings
Event Threat Detection, which analyzes logs for active threats
explain: Security Health Analytics continuously evaluates resource configurations against security best practices and surfaces misconfiguration findings. Event Threat Detection looks for active malicious behavior in logs rather than config drift, Asset Inventory provides the resource list without security evaluation, and flow logs capture network telemetry rather than posture findings.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A finding about a legacy bucket fires repeatedly and the team has accepted the risk with a documented exception until migration completes. How can they suppress the noise without deleting the finding?
options: Delete the finding from Security Command Center
Disable Security Health Analytics entirely
Remove the bucket from the organization
Create a mute rule matching the finding so it is hidden from the active findings view
explain: Mute rules suppress matching findings from active views while preserving the underlying finding record for audit. Findings cannot be deleted outright, disabling the detector blinds the whole organization, and removing the bucket destroys the data the exception was meant to protect.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A SOC triages hundreds of Security Command Center findings daily and needs to tag which analyst owns each finding and its review status. Which feature supports this workflow?
options: Log views, which filter log entries
IAM conditions, which scope role bindings
Notification channels, which route alert emails
Security marks, which attach custom key-value metadata to findings and assets
explain: Security marks let teams annotate findings and assets with custom labels like owner and status for triage workflows. Log views scope log access rather than annotating findings, IAM conditions control access rather than tracking triage, and notification channels deliver alerts without recording ownership.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A healthcare company wants explicit approval before Google support personnel can access their data during a support case. Which control provides this?
options: Access Transparency logs, which only record access after the fact
VPC Service Controls, which block API access from outside
Customer-managed encryption keys, which approve each access
Access Approval, which requires customer approval before Google admin access
explain: Access Approval enrolls the organization so that Google personnel access requests require explicit customer approval, with optional automatic approval rules. Access Transparency provides audit logs of access that already occurred, VPC Service Controls govern API data movement rather than Google admin access, and CMEK controls encryption keys rather than approving support access.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A company wants a mandatory rule blocking all outbound traffic to a known-malicious IP range that no folder or project admin can override. At which level should this firewall policy be attached?
options: A VPC firewall rule in each project's network
A hierarchical firewall policy at the folder level
A Cloud Armor policy on the load balancer
A hierarchical firewall policy at the organization level with a deny egress rule
explain: Hierarchical firewall policies at the organization level apply to all VMs beneath and cannot be overridden by lower-level admins, making them the right vehicle for mandatory guardrails. Per-project VPC rules can be modified by project admins, folder-level policies do not cover sibling folders, and Cloud Armor protects load balancer frontends rather than VM egress.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A company wants all SSH access to VMs managed through IAM with no locally managed SSH keys in instance metadata. Which organization policy constraint enforces OS Login everywhere?
options: constraints/compute.disableSerialPortAccess
constraints/iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation
Enabling IAP for TCP forwarding
constraints/compute.requireOsLogin enforced at the organization
explain: The compute.requireOsLogin constraint forces OS Login on all instances, centralizing SSH key management in IAM and disabling metadata-based keys. The serial port constraint governs console access rather than SSH, the key creation constraint governs service account keys rather than SSH keys, and IAP tunneling is an access path rather than an enforcement mechanism.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A hardened baseline requires the interactive serial console to be unavailable on all production VMs to reduce the attack surface. Which organization policy constraint enforces this?
options: constraints/compute.requireOsLogin
constraints/compute.vmExternalIpAccess
Deleting all SSH keys from project metadata
constraints/compute.disableSerialPortAccess enforced on the production folder
explain: The compute.disableSerialPortAccess constraint disables serial port access, including the interactive serial console, on covered instances. OS Login governs SSH key management rather than the serial console, the external IP constraint governs public IPs, and deleting metadata SSH keys does not disable the serial console itself.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security

q: A company is finishing its Google Cloud security baseline and wants to require phishing-resistant two-step verification for all administrator accounts. Which enforcement approach provides this?
options: Grant admins the Owner role so 2SV is automatic
Enable 2SV only on the billing account
Rely on strong passwords with annual rotation
Enforce 2-Step Verification for admins in the Google Admin console and require security keys
explain: Two-step verification is enforced through the Google Workspace or Cloud Identity Admin console, where administrators can require it for admin accounts and mandate security keys for phishing resistance. IAM roles do not enable 2SV, billing-account settings do not govern user authentication, and passwords alone do not satisfy a phishing-resistant MFA requirement.
domain: Section 4: Configuring access and security
